verses.translation:
Dhritarashtra spoke:
When they were in the field of virtue, in the field of the Kurus,
Assembled together, desiring to fight,
What did my army and that of the
Sons of Pandu do, Sanjaya?
verses.accessible: King Dhritarashtra asked: 'Sanjaya, gathered on the holy field of Kurukshetra and eager for battle, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?'
notes: • Kuruk~etra is an actual place, a small plain in the Panjab north of Delhi near Panipat.

verses.translation:
Sanjaya spoke:
Seeing indeed the army
Of the sons of Pandu arrayed,
King Duryodhana, approaching his Master (Drona),
Spoke these words:
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'After seeing the Pandava army drawn up in battle formation, King Duryodhana approached his teacher, Drona, and spoke these words:'

verses.translation:
Behold O Master, this great army
Of the sons of Pandu
Arrayed by the son of Drupada,
Wise by your instruction.
verses.accessible: Duryodhana said: 'Master, look at this massive army of the sons of Pandu, arranged in battle lines by your talented student, the son of Drupada.'
notes: • Both Drol)a and Drupada, as befits great heroes in mythology, had odd births. Drupada's father, Pr~ata, lost his seed at the sight of Menaka, an apsara (nymph), wife of a Gandharvll (flereal being). He tried to trample out the seed. Hence his name "rapid step." Nevertheless, Drupada was born from this seed. Drol)a's father, Bharadvaja, lost his seed under similar circumstances. It fell into a bucket he was carrying. Drol)a means " bucket" see chapter on the setting of the Bhagavad Gita.

verses.translation:
Here are heroes, mighty archers,
Equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna,
Yuyudhana and Virata,
And Drupada, the great warrior;
verses.accessible: 'Here are mighty archers and heroic warriors equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna: great heroes such as Yuyudhana, Virata, and the formidable Drupada.'

verses.translation:
Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana,
And the valorous King of Kashi,
Purojit and Kuntibhoja
And Shaibya, bull among men.
verses.accessible: 'There is Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the valiant King of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, a leader among men.'
notes: • Kuntibhoja, a Yadava prince, has an interesting relationship with the PliI.1Qava princes. He is, by adoption, their father-in-law, having adopted Prtha, daughter of his cousin Sura, who was also a Yadava prince. Upon adoption, Prthli took her foster father's name and became known as Kunt!. Kunti, formerly Prthli, thus belonged to the Yadava clan, and was an aunt of Krishna, whose father, Vasudeva, was her brother (and a son of Sura). Ultimately she became the mother of the first three PaI.1Qava princes (Yudhi~thira, Bhlma and Arjuna), as well as KarI.1a. Throughout the Bhagavad Gita Arjuna is referred to as Partha (Son of Prtha), or Kaunteya (Son of Kunti). - See chapter on "The Setting of the Bhagavad Glta."

verses.translation:
And mighty Yudhamanyu
And valorous Uttamaujas;
The son of Subhadra and the sons of Draupadi,
All indeed great warriors.
verses.accessible: 'There is the powerful Yudhamanyu, the heroic Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra, and the five sons of Draupadi—every one of them a master chariot warrior.'

verses.translation:
Those of ours who are indeed distinguished,
Know them! O highest of the Twiceborn,
The leaders of my army
I name for you by proper names:
verses.accessible: 'Now, best of teachers, let me also name the most distinguished leaders on our own side, so you know the generals who command my army:'

verses.translation:
Your Lordship and Bhishma and Karna
and Kripa, always victorious in battle,
Ashvatthama and Vikarna
and the son of Somadatta also;
verses.accessible: 'There is yourself, revered master, along with Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa, who is always victorious in battle. There is also Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Somadatta's son.'

verses.translation:
And many other heroes
whose lives are risked for my sake,
attacking with various weapons,
all skilled in battle.
verses.accessible: 'There are countless other heroes as well, all ready to risk their lives for my sake. They are armed with every kind of weapon, and all of them are masters of warfare.'
notes: • The compound /ollrapraharm,,.b mea ns literally "weapons strike and weapons to hurl."

verses.translation:
Sufficient is that force of ours
Guarded by Bhishma;
Insufficient though is
The force guarded by Bhima.
verses.accessible: 'Our army, protected by Grandfather Bhishma, is vast and invincible, while their army, guarded by Bhima, is limited and vulnerable.'
notes: ... This stanza has puzzled many translators because (I) Duryodhana's (the speaker's) forces are actually greater than those of the Pal).9aVaS (therefore hardly" insufficient"); (2) tad" that" seems to refer to something nearby while idam "this" seems to refer to something far off; (3) Bhi~ma is generally regarded as a much greater leader of troops than Bhima; (4) the words sound unnatural corning from Duryodhana who is supposed to be encouraging his forces with a pep talk. The eminent Sanskrit scholar J. A. B. van Buitenen has investigated the matter and published his conclusions in the Journal of the American Oriental Society (Vol. 85, No. I, Jan.-March 1965). The Vulgate version, from which practically all translations have been made, was, according to van Buitenen, preceded by another version used by Bhaskara the Vedantin, in the ninth century or thereabouts. In that version, which still survives, the names Bhi~ma and Bhima are transposed and the stanza reads: aparyaptam tad asmakam balam bhimabhirak~itam paryaptam tv idam ete~am balam bhismabhirak~itam

verses.translation:
And in all movements,
Stationed each in his respective place,
All of you, indeed,
Protect Bhishma!
verses.accessible: 'Therefore, all of you must hold your assigned positions throughout the battle lines and give your full protection to Bhishma!'
notes: which in van Buitenen's translation reads: " That army guarded by Bhima is not equal to us; On the other hand, this army, guarded by Bhi~ma is equal to them." Actually, though Bhi~ma is the leader of the Kauravas, Bhima is not the leader of the Pal)<;Iavas. Edgerton thinks the name Bhima is chosen in order to make a word play on the two names.

verses.translation:
Making him (Duryodhana) happy,
The aged Kuru, his grandsire,
Roaring like a lion,
Blew his conch horn powerfully.
verses.accessible: To cheer Duryodhana up, the aged patriarch Bhishma—the grand elder of the Kuru clan—let out a roar like a lion and blew a powerful blast on his conch shell.

verses.translation:
And thereupon the conch horns and the kettledrums,
The cymbals, drums and trumpets
All at once were sounded.
The uproar was tremendous.
verses.accessible: At once, conch shells, kettledrums, cymbals, drums, and trumpets all blared together in an explosive clash of sound. The roar was deafening.

verses.translation:
Then, standing in the great chariot
Yoked with white horses,
Krishna and Arjuna
Sounded forth their divine conch horns.
verses.accessible: Then, standing in their magnificent chariot hitched to white horses, Krishna and Arjuna blew their own sacred conch shells in response.
notes: • Arjuna's chariot is drawn by four horses.

verses.translation:
Krishna blew his Panchajanya;
Arjuna blew Devadatta,
While Bhima, terrible in action,
Blew the great conch horn Paundra.
verses.accessible: Krishna blew his conch horn, Panchajanya; Arjuna blew his, Devadatta; and Bhima, the terrifying warrior of mighty deeds, sounded his massive conch, Paundra.

verses.translation:
King Yudhishthira,
Son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya;
Nakula and Sahadeva
Blew Sughosa and Manipushpaka.
verses.accessible: King Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya, while the twin brothers Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

verses.translation:
And the King of Kashi, supreme archer,
And Shikhandi, that great warrior,
Dhrishtadyumna and Virata
And Satyaki, the invincible;
verses.accessible: The King of Kashi, a supreme archer, the great warrior Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the undefeated Satyaki;

verses.translation:
Drupada and the sons of Draupadi
All together, O Lord of the Earth,
And the strong armed son of Subhadra
Blew their conch horns, each his own.
verses.accessible: King Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and the strong-armed son of Subhadra—each and every one of them, O King, blew their own battle horns.

verses.translation:
The noise burst asunder
The hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra,
And the tumult caused
The sky and the earth to resound.
verses.accessible: That thunderous roar echoed between heaven and earth, shattering the confidence and striking terror into the hearts of Dhritarashtra’s sons.

verses.translation:
Then, Arjuna, having seen the sons of Dhritarashtra
Drawn up in battle array,
Raised his bow as the clash of weapons began.
verses.accessible: Then Arjuna, whose chariot banner bore the crest of Hanuman the monkey, looked across at Dhritarashtra’s sons lined up in battle formation. As weapons were about to clash, he lifted his bow.
notes: • Arjuna's standard was a flag with the symbol of a monkey. Incidentally, the monkey was Hanuman, the monkey god, who assisted Rama in bringing back the kidnapped SUa, his wife, in the Ramayana.

verses.translation:
Arjuna then spoke these words to Krishna:
O Lord of the earth,
Cause my chariot to stand in the middle
Between the two armies, Imperishable One,
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'O Krishna, please drive my chariot between the two armies and halt there, O Infallible One,'

verses.translation:
Until I behold these warriors,
Battle-hungry and arrayed.
With whom must I fight
In undertaking this battle?
verses.accessible: 'so that I may clearly see these warriors assembled here eager for war, and know with whom I must fight in this great battle.'

verses.translation:
I behold those who are about to give battle,
Having come together here,
Wishing to do service in warfare
For the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana).
verses.accessible: 'I want to see all those who have gathered here ready for combat, eager to serve the wicked son of Dhritarashtra in this war.'

verses.translation:
Thus Krishna was addressed by Arjuna, O Dhritarashtra,
Having caused the chief chariot
To stand in the middle between the two armies.
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'O King Dhritarashtra, addressed in this way by Arjuna, Krishna drove that magnificent chariot into the open space between the two vast armies.'
notes: • Dhrtara~tra the blind king to whom the scene is being described.

verses.translation:
Before the eyes of Bhishma and Drona
And all these rulers of the earth,
Arjuna said: Behold these
Kurus assembled.
verses.accessible: Halting right before Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers of the earth, Krishna said: 'Look, Arjuna! Behold all the Kurus gathered here!'

verses.translation:
Arjuna saw standing there
Fathers, then grandfathers,
Teachers, maternal uncles, brothers,
Sons, grandsons, friends as well;
verses.accessible: Standing there between the lines, Arjuna saw his own elders and family: fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and lifelong companions.

verses.translation:
Arjuna saw fathers-in-law, companions,
In the two armies,
And contemplated
All his kinsmen, arrayed.
verses.accessible: He saw fathers-in-law and dear friends spread across both armies. Gazing upon all his kinsmen standing ready to battle each other,

verses.translation:
Filled with infinite pity,
Despondent, he said this:
Having seen my own people, Krishna,
Desiring to fight, approaching.
verses.accessible: Arjuna was overcome with profound sorrow and pity, and spoke in despair: 'O Krishna, seeing my own kin standing before me, eager for battle,'

verses.translation:
My limbs sink down,
My mouth dries up,
My body trembles,
And my hair stands on end;
verses.accessible: 'my limbs go weak, my mouth goes completely dry, my whole body trembles, and my hair stands on end.'

verses.translation:
Gandiva (Arjuna’s bow) falls from (my) hand,
My skin burns,
I am unable to remain as I am,
And my mind seems to ramble.
verses.accessible: 'My bow, Gandiva, slips from my hands, and my skin feels like it is on fire. I can barely stay on my feet, and my mind is reeling in confusion.'

verses.translation:
I perceive inauspicious omens,
O Krishna,
And I foresee misfortune
In destroying my own people in battle.
verses.accessible: 'I see bad omens all around us, Krishna, and I cannot see any good coming from killing our own family in this war.'

verses.translation:
I do not desire victory, Krishna,
Nor kingship nor pleasures.
What is kingship to us, Krishna?
What are enjoyments, even life?
verses.accessible: 'I do not desire victory, Krishna, nor a kingdom or its pleasures. What good is a kingdom to us? What good are luxuries, or even life itself,'
notes: .. Govinda (lit. "cow finder "). "Chief of Cowherds" presumes an adoption into Sanskrit of the Prakrit "gopendra" (gopa Indra), but this is the translation usually accepted.

verses.translation:
Those for whose sake we desire
Kingship, enjoyments, and pleasures,
They are arrayed here in battle,
Abandoning their lives and riches.
verses.accessible: 'when the very people for whom we desire wealth, kingship, and joy are standing here on the battlefield, ready to forfeit their lives and fortunes?'

verses.translation:
Teachers, fathers, sons,
And also grandfathers,
Maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons,
Brothers-in-law, and other kinsmen.
verses.accessible: 'They are our teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and dear relatives.'

verses.translation:
I do not desire to kill
Them who are bent on killing, Krishna,
Even for the sovereignty of the three worlds.
How much less then for the earth?
verses.accessible: 'Even if they want to kill me, Krishna, I have no desire to kill them—not even for control over all three worlds, let alone for this earthly kingdom!'

verses.translation:
What joy would it be for us
To strike down the sons of Dhritarashtra, O Krishna?
Evil thus would cling to us,
Having killed these aggressors.
verses.accessible: 'What possible joy could we find in slaughtering the sons of Dhritarashtra, Krishna? Only sin and guilt would cling to us if we murder these men, even if they are the aggressors.'
notes: .. Janardana, " Agitator of Men" is an epithet of the god Vishnu, of whom Krishna is the earthly avatar.

verses.translation:
Therefore we are not justified in killing
The sons of Dhritarashtra, our own kinsmen.
How, having killed our own people,
Could we be happy, Krishna?
verses.accessible: 'Therefore, it is not right for us to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we ever find happiness after slaughtering our own family, Krishna?'

verses.translation:
Even if those
Whose thoughts are overpowered by greed do not perceive
The wrong caused by the destruction of the family,
And the crime of treachery to friends.
verses.accessible: 'Even if their minds are so blinded by greed that they see no crime in destroying a family and no sin in betraying friends,'

verses.translation:
Why should we not know enough
To turn back from this evil,
Through discernment of the wrong caused
By the destruction of the family, O Krishna?
verses.accessible: 'why shouldn't we have the wisdom to turn away from this terrible evil, Krishna, when we can clearly see the destruction that wiping out a family brings?'

verses.translation:
In the destruction of the family,
The ancient family laws vanish;
When the law has perished,
Lawlessness overpowers the entire family also.
verses.accessible: 'When a family is destroyed, its ancient traditions and moral principles perish with it. And when sacred principles collapse, lawlessness overpowers the remaining family.'

verses.translation:
Because of the ascendancy of lawlessness, Krishna,
The family women are corrupted;
When women are corrupted, O Krishna,
The intermixture of caste is born.
verses.accessible: 'With the rise of lawlessness, Krishna, the women of the family are corrupted; and when moral integrity is lost, it creates confusion and the breakdown of society.'

verses.translation:
Intermixture brings to hell
The family destroyers and the family, too;
The ancestors of these indeed fall,
Deprived of offerings of rice and water.
verses.accessible: 'This social collapse drags both the family and its destroyers into hell. Even the ancestors fall from peace, neglected and deprived of the sacred offerings of food and water.'

verses.translation:
By these wrongs of the family destroyers,
Producing intermixture of caste,
Caste duties are abolished,
And eternal family laws also.
verses.accessible: 'Through the sins of those who destroy the family and shatter social harmony, ancient community duties and timeless family traditions are completely wiped out.'

verses.translation:
Men whose family laws have been obliterated,
O Krishna,
Dwell indefinitely in hell,
Thus we have heard repeatedly,
verses.accessible: 'We have been taught, Krishna, that those whose family traditions are destroyed are doomed to suffer in misery without end.'

verses.translation:
Ah! Alas! We are resolved
To do a great evil,
Which is to be intent on killing
Our own people, through greed for royal pleasures.
verses.accessible: 'What a terrible tragedy! We are preparing to commit a monstrous sin, driven by our greed for royal power and royal pleasures, ready to kill our own people.'

verses.translation:
If the armed sons of Dhritarashtra
Should kill me in battle
While I was unresisting and unarmed,
This would be a greater happiness for me.
verses.accessible: 'It would be far better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in their hands, were to strike me down on this battlefield while I stood unarmed and unresisting!'

verses.translation:
Thus having spoken on the battlefield,
Arjuna sat down upon the seat of the chariot,
Throwing down both arrow and bow,
With a heart overcome by sorrow.
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'Having spoken these words on the battlefield, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows and sank down into the seat of his chariot, his heart overwhelmed with grief.'

verses.translation:
Sanjaya spoke:
To him thus overcome by pity, despairing,
Whose eyes were filled with tears and downcast,
Krishna spoke these words:
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'Seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with pity and sorrow, his eyes filled with tears and downcast in despair, Krishna spoke these words to him:'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Whence has this timidity of yours
Come to you in time of danger?
It is not acceptable in you, does not lead to heaven,
And causes disgrace, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Arjuna, where did this weakness come from at such a critical moment? It is unworthy of a noble warrior, it does not lead to heaven, and it brings only disgrace.'

verses.translation:
Do not become a coward, Arjuna.
This is not suitable to you.
Abandoning base faintheartedness,
Stand up, Arjuna!
verses.accessible: Do not surrender to cowardice, Arjuna, for it does not become you. Shake off this shameful weakness of heart and stand up to fight!

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
How can I kill in battle
Bhishma and Drona, O Krishna?
How can I fight with arrows against
These two venerable men, O Krishna?
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'Krishna, how can I attack Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle? Both of them deserve my deepest respect and worship.'

verses.translation:
Indeed, instead of slaying these noble gurus
It would be preferable to live on alms here on earth;
Having slain the gurus, with desire for worldly gain,
I would enjoy here on earth delights smeared with blood.
verses.accessible: It would be far better to live by begging for food in this world than to slaughter these noble teachers. Even if they are driven by wealth and power, if I kill them, every pleasure I enjoy on this earth will be smeared with their blood.
notes: • This and the next three stanzas are in tTi~!ubh metre, otherwise known as the k~atriya metre, eleven syllables to the line. This differs from the sloka metre (eight syllables per line) used in most of the poem.

verses.translation:
And this we do not know: which for us is preferable,
Whether we should conquer them or they should conquer us.
The sons of Dhritarashtra, having killed whom we would not wish to live,
Are standing before us.
verses.accessible: We do not even know which outcome is better—whether we conquer them or they conquer us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand right before us, and if we kill them, we will have no desire to go on living.
notes: • The first two lines of this stanza contain an extra syllable apiece not uncommon in tri1!ubh metre.

verses.translation:
My own being is overcome by pity and weakness.
My mind is confused as to my duty. I ask you
Which is preferable, for certain?
Tell that to me, your pupil. Correct me, I beg you.
verses.accessible: My spirit is paralyzed by grief, and my mind is completely confused about my duty. Tell me with certainty what is best for me. I am your student—please guide me, for I surrender myself entirely to you.

verses.translation:
Indeed, I do not see what will dispel
This sorrow of mine which dries up my senses,
Even if I should obtain on earth unrivaled and
Prosperous royal power, or even the sovereignty of the gods.
verses.accessible: I cannot see anything that could drive away this sorrow that is numbing my senses—not even winning an unrivaled, wealthy kingdom on earth, or gaining total sovereignty over the gods.

verses.translation:
Sanjaya spoke:
Thus having addressed Krishna, Arjuna said,
“I shall not fight,”
And having spoken, he became silent.
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'Having spoken these words to Krishna, Arjuna declared, "I will not fight," and fell completely silent.'
notes: • 8/oka metre resumes. t gwjakesa has been translated by some native translators as gu4aka lsa, "Conqueror of Sleep." It is generally believed that gu4aka, "sleep," is an artificial word, invented to explain gu4akesa, and not the other way around.

verses.translation:
To him, the dejected Arjuna, Krishna,
Beginning to laugh, O Dhritarashtra,
In the middle between the two armies,
Spoke these words:
verses.accessible: O King, standing there between the two armies, Krishna smiled gently and addressed the grief-stricken Arjuna:

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
You have mourned those that should not be mourned,
And you speak words as if with wisdom;
The wise do not mourn for the dead or for the living.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'You are grieving for those who do not need your grief, yet you speak words that sound like wisdom. The truly wise mourn neither for the living nor for the dead.'

verses.translation:
Truly there was never a time when I was not,
Nor you, nor these lords of men;
And neither will there be a time when we shall cease to be
From this time onward.
verses.accessible: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor any of these kings; nor will any of us ever cease to exist in the future.

verses.translation:
Just as in the body childhood, adulthood, and old age
Happen to an embodied being,
So also he (the embodied being) acquires another body.
The wise one is not deluded about this.
verses.accessible: Just as the soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age within this physical body, it simply moves on to another body after death. The wise are not confused by this transition.
notes: • The embodied, i.e. that which is in, but not of, the body, viz. the lltman, or self.

verses.translation:
Physical sensations, truly, Arjuna,
Causing cold, heat, pleasure, or pain,
Come and go and are impermanent.
So manage to endure them, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Physical sensations like cold and heat, pleasure and pain, come from the senses contacting the world. They are temporary, constantly coming and going. Learn to endure them patiently, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Indeed, the man whom these (i.e. the sensations) do not afflict,
O Arjuna,
The wise one, to whom happiness and unhappiness are the same,
Is ready for immortality.
verses.accessible: The person who is not shaken by these sensations, who stays calm and balanced in both pleasure and pain—that wise person is ready for immortality.

verses.translation:
It is found that the unreal has no being;
It is found that there is no non-being of the real.
The certainty of both these propositions is indeed surely seen
By the perceivers of truth.
verses.accessible: What is unreal has no true existence, and what is real never ceases to exist. Those who have seen the ultimate truth clearly understand the distinction between the two.

verses.translation:
Know that that by which all this universe
Is pervaded is indeed indestructible;
No one is able to accomplish
The destruction of the imperishable.
verses.accessible: Know that the reality which pervades the entire universe can never be destroyed. No one has the power to destroy the imperishable soul.
notes: • I.e. the iitman (self) or Brahman.

verses.translation:
These bodies inhabited by the eternal,
The indestructible, the immeasurable embodied Self,
Are said to come to an end.
Therefore fight, Arjuna!
verses.accessible: These physical bodies are temporary and come to an end, but the soul within is eternal, indestructible, and boundless. Therefore, Arjuna, stand and fight!
notes: • I.e. the litman or Brahman.

verses.translation:
He who imagines this (the embodied Self) the slayer
And he who imagines this (the embodied Self) the slain,
Neither of them understands
This (the embodied Self) does not slay, nor is it slain.
verses.accessible: Anyone who believes the soul can kill, or who thinks the soul can be killed, lacks true understanding. The soul neither kills nor is it killed.

verses.translation:
Neither is this (the embodied Self) born nor does it die at any time,
Nor, having been, will it again come not to be.
Birthless, eternal, perpetual, primaeval,
It is not slain when the body is slain.
verses.accessible: The soul is never born, nor does it ever die. It did not come into existence at a point in time, nor will it ever cease to be. It is unborn, eternal, everlasting, and ancient; it does not perish when the body dies.
notes: • Trii/ubh metre.

verses.translation:
He who knows this, the indestructible, the eternal,
The birthless, the imperishable,
In what way does this man cause to be slain, Arjuna?
Whom does he slay?
verses.accessible: Arjuna, when a person knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and unchanging, how could that person ever kill anyone or cause anyone to be killed?
notes: • Sloka metre resumes.

verses.translation:
As, after casting away worn out garments,
A man later takes new ones,
So, after casting away worn out bodies,
The embodied Self encounters other, new ones.
verses.accessible: Just as a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the soul casts off an old, worn-out body and enters into a new one.
notes: • TriNubh metre.

verses.translation:
Weapons do not pierce this (the embodied Self),
Fire does not burn this,
Water does not wet this,
Nor does the wind cause it to wither.
verses.accessible: Weapons cannot cut the soul, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and the wind cannot wither it.
notes: • 8loka metre resumes.

verses.accessible: It cannot be pierced, burned, drowned, or dried out. It is eternal, all-pervading, unshakeable, immovable, and timeless.

verses.translation:
It is said that this is unmanifest,
Unthinkable, and unchanging.
Therefore, having understood in this way,
You should not mourn.
verses.accessible: The soul is invisible, beyond the reach of human thought, and completely unchangeable. Understanding it this way, you have no reason to grieve.
notes: • I.e. the foregoing propositions.

verses.translation:
And moreover even if you think this
To be eternally born or eternally dead,
Even then
You should not mourn for this, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Even if you believe the soul is constantly born and constantly dies with the body, even then, mighty Arjuna, you still have no reason to mourn.

verses.translation:
For the born, death is certain;
For the dead there is certainly birth.
Therefore, for this, inevitable in consequence,
You should not mourn.
verses.accessible: For anyone who is born, death is certain; and for anyone who dies, rebirth is equally certain. Since this cycle is completely unavoidable, you should not grieve over it.

verses.translation:
Beings are such that their beginnings are unmanifest,
Their middles are manifest,
And their ends are unmanifest again.
What complaint can there be over this?
verses.accessible: All living beings are unmanifest before birth, manifest during life, and unmanifest again after death, Arjuna. Why should you grieve over this natural order?

verses.translation:
Someone perceives this as a wonder,
Another declares this as a wonder,
Still another hears of this as a wonder;
But even having heard of this, no one knows it.
verses.accessible: Some gaze upon the soul as a wonder, others speak of it as a wonder, and still others hear of it as a wonder; yet even after hearing about it, hardly anyone truly understands it.
notes: • Triltubh metre with second line one syllable too long. t This stanza explains the mystical nature of Brahman and the atman.

verses.translation:
This, the embodied Self, is eternally indestructible
In the body of all, Arjuna.
Therefore you should not mourn
For any being.
verses.accessible: The soul living within the body of every creature can never be destroyed, Arjuna. Therefore, you have no reason to mourn for anyone.

verses.translation:
And, perceiving your own caste duty,
You should not tremble.
Indeed, anything superior to righteous battle
Does not exist for the kshatriya (man of warrior caste).
verses.accessible: Considering your own duty as a warrior, you should not waver. For a warrior, there is no higher purpose than fighting in a righteous cause.

verses.translation:
And if by good fortune they gain
The open gate of heaven,
Happy are the kshatriyas, Arjuna,
When they encounter such a fight.
verses.accessible: Fortunate are the warriors, Arjuna, who are presented with such an opportunity to fight—a righteous battle that opens wide the gates of heaven without their seeking it.

verses.translation:
Now, if you will not undertake
This righteous war,
Thereupon, having avoided your own duty and glory,
You shall incur evil.
verses.accessible: Now, if you refuse to fight this righteous battle, you will abandon your duty, ruin your honor, and bring moral failure upon yourself.

verses.translation:
And also people will relate
Your undying infamy;
And, for one who has been honored,
Disgrace is worse than dying.
verses.accessible: People will speak of your disgrace for generations to come. And for someone who has been deeply respected, dishonor is far worse than death.

verses.translation:
The great warriors will think
That you have abstained from the battle through fear,
And among those by whom you have been held in high esteem
You shall come to be held lightly.
verses.accessible: The great chariot generals will believe you retreated from battle out of fear. Those who once held you in highest esteem will lose all respect for you.

verses.translation:
And your enemies will speak
many words of you that should not be spoken,
deriding your capacity.
What greater hardship is there than that?
verses.accessible: Your enemies will mock you with cruel and insulting words, scorning your courage and strength. What could possibly be more painful than that?

verses.translation:
Either, having been slain, you shall attain heaven,
Or, having conquered, you shall enjoy the earth.
Therefore stand up, Arjuna,
Resolved to fight.
verses.accessible: If you are killed, you will attain heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, stand up, Arjuna, resolved to fight!

verses.translation:
Holding pleasure and pain to be alike,
Likewise gain and loss, victory and defeat,
Then engage in battle!
Thus you shall not incur evil.
verses.accessible: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat with an equal mind. Then throw yourself into the battle! By fighting in this spirit, you will never incur any wrongdoing.

So far, I have shared with you the wisdom of analytical knowledge. Now listen to the wisdom of selfless action. When your mind is guided by this understanding, Arjuna, you will break free from the bondage of karma.
notes: • Sdmkhya, one of the six traditional systems of Hindu philosophy, and one of the oldest. The others are Mfmiimsii, Yoga, Vediinta, Viiise#ka, and Nyiiya. The Siimkhya system is attributed to the sage Kapila (circa SOO B.C.) and is known as the" reason method" of salvation, while Yoga, or at least karma- Yoga (the Yoga of action) is the "action method." The two often overlap in the Bhagavad Gita, and are not always distinct. Siimkhya is the older of the two. From it comes the concept of the gU!las. I t postulates a cosmology in which results are implied in causes, and in which the universe remains constant, nothing new ever being added to or subtracted from it. Nothing is ever created. Everything is a manifestation or mutation of what has always existed. Thus death is merely a transitory state leading to other states. In this, Siimkhya has a parallel in the modern scientific theory of the conservation of matter and energy. Siimkhya does not recognize gods or sacrifices. It is said to have influenced Buddhism.

verses.translation:
Here (in the yoga doctrine of practice) no effort is lost,
Nor is any loss of progress found.
Even a little of this discipline
Protects one from great danger.
verses.accessible: On this spiritual path, no effort is ever wasted, and no progress is ever lost. Even a little practice of this discipline protects you from great fear.
notes: It is known as "the way of knowledge," and it proposes knowledge as the principal means of salvation. Still other means of salvation mentioned in the Glta are meditation and love of God.

verses.translation:
Here there is a single resolute understanding, Arjuna.
The thoughts of the irresolute
Have many branches and are, indeed, endless.
verses.accessible: Those who are resolute in their purpose have a single, focused mind, Arjuna. But the thoughts of the indecisive branch off endlessly in every direction.

verses.translation:
The ignorant ones proclaim
This flowery discourse, Arjuna,
Delighting in the letter of the Veda
And saying, “There is nothing else.”
verses.accessible: Unwise people preach flowery words, Arjuna, obsessing over the ritual promises of the scriptures and claiming, 'There is nothing beyond this!'

verses.translation:
Full of desires, intent on heaven,
They offer rebirth as the fruit of action,
And are addicted to many specific rites
Aimed at the goal of enjoyment and power.
verses.accessible: Driven by selfish cravings and longing only for heavenly pleasures, they perform elaborate rituals to gain worldly power and enjoyment, but their actions only bind them to future rebirths.
notes: • I.e. the "ignorant ones" of the preceding stanza.

verses.translation:
To those (the ignorant ones) attached to enjoyment and power,
Whose thought is stolen away by this kind of talk,
Resolute insight
In meditation is not granted.
verses.accessible: Those who cling to pleasure and power, whose minds are swept away by such empty promises, cannot develop the resolute focus needed for deep meditation.

verses.translation:
The Vedas are such that their scope is confined to the three qualities;
Be free from those three qualities, Arjuna,
Indifferent toward the pairs of opposites, eternally fixed in truth,
Free from thoughts of acquisition
and comfort, and possessed of the Self.
verses.accessible: The scriptures deal with the three fundamental qualities of material nature. Rise above these three qualities, Arjuna! Be free from the pull of opposites, stay rooted in pure goodness, let go of the anxiety to acquire and protect possessions, and remain centered in your true Self.

verses.translation:
As much value as there is in a well
When water is flooding on every side,
So much is the value in all the Vedas
For a brahman who knows.
verses.accessible: Just as a small well is of little use when a freshwater flood surrounds you on every side, all the scriptures are of limited use to a wise person who has directly realized the ultimate truth.
You have a right to your actions, but never to the fruits of your actions. Never let the results of action be your motive, and never give in to attachment to inaction.
notes: • Acting without regard or desire for the fruits of action is one of the most constant teachings of the Bhagavad Gitii. It refers to "disinterested action," which is not to be confused with irresponsible or careless action. According to the law of karma an individual is responsible for his actions throughout eternity, or until he achieves nirvii1;la. The" fruits" (usually translated in the plural, though the singular phalam is used in the Sanskrit) mean the results of action, and they are of three kinds: those of obligatory action, those of action prompted by desire, and those that arise from delusion (see XVIII 23, 24, 25). The first of these is really action without desire for the fruits, i.e. action which is a duty. The second and third are related to desire, and the elimination of desire for the fruits of action is basic to the GUll's teaching. The last line, about "inaction" is an injunction against sloth one of the evils associated with the gU1;Ia of tamas, or darkness. Action prompted by delusion (see above) is also associated with tamas. Thus, action prompted by greed, desire for wealth, desire for power, or desire for fame is not advised.

verses.translation:
Fixed in yoga, perform actions,
Having abandoned attachment, Arjuna,
And having become indifferent to success or failure.
It is said that evenness of mind is yoga.
verses.accessible: Perform your duty with a steady mind, Arjuna, letting go of selfish attachment and remaining balanced in both success and failure. That inner balance is what yoga truly means.

verses.translation:
Action is inferior by far
To the yoga of wisdom, Arjuna.
Seek refuge in wisdom!
Despicable are those whose motives are based on the fruit of action.
verses.accessible: Selfish action is far inferior to action guided by the yoga of wisdom, Arjuna. Take refuge in clear understanding, for pitiful are those whose motive is only the reward.

verses.translation:
He whose wisdom is established
Casts off, here in the world, both good and evil actions;
Therefore devote yourself to yoga!
Yoga is skill in action.
verses.accessible: A person guided by wisdom rises above both good and bad deeds in this life. Therefore, dedicate yourself to yoga, for yoga is skill in action.

verses.translation:
Those who are established in wisdom,
The wise ones, who have abandoned the fruit born of action,
And are freed from the bondage of rebirth,
Go to the place that is free from pain.
verses.accessible: By uniting their intellect with wisdom, the wise let go of the fruits born of action. Freed from the bondage of rebirth, they attain a state completely beyond all suffering.

verses.translation:
When your intellect crosses beyond
The thicket of delusion, then you shall become disgusted
With that which is yet to be heard
And with that which has been heard (in the Veda).
verses.accessible: When your intellect crosses beyond the dense thicket of delusion, you will no longer be swayed by ritual teachings you have heard or have yet to hear.

verses.translation:
When your intellect stands
fixed in deep meditation, unmoving,
disregarding Vedic doctrine,
then you shall attain Self-realization.
verses.accessible: When your mind is no longer distracted by conflicting teachings and stands firm, unshakeable in deep meditation, you will attain true union with the Divine.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
How does one describe him who is of steady wisdom,
Who is steadfast in deep meditation, Krishna?
How does he who is steady in wisdom speak?
How does he sit? How does he move?
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'Krishna, what are the marks of a person whose wisdom is steady and firmly anchored in meditation? How do they speak, how do they sit, and how do they move in the world?'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
When he leaves behind all desires
Emerging from the mind, Arjuna,
And is contented in the Self by the Self,
Then he is said to be one whose wisdom is steady.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'When a person completely lets go of all selfish cravings in the mind, Arjuna, and finds total contentment within the Self alone, that person is said to be established in steady wisdom.'

verses.translation:
He whose mind is not agitated in misfortune,
Whose desire for pleasures has disappeared,
Whose passion, fear, and anger have departed,
And whose meditation is steady, is said to be a sage.
verses.accessible: One whose mind remains untroubled in sorrow, who is free from craving amidst pleasures, and who has cast out attachment, fear, and anger—that person is called a sage of steady wisdom.

verses.translation:
He who is without attachment on all sides,
Encountering this or that, pleasant or unpleasant,
Neither rejoicing nor disliking;
His wisdom stands firm.
verses.accessible: Whoever is free from attachment in all circumstances, neither rejoicing when good fortune arrives nor feeling bitterness when misfortune strikes—their wisdom is firmly established.

verses.translation:
And when he withdraws completely
The senses from the objects of the senses,
As a tortoise withdraws its limbs into its shell,
His wisdom stands firm.
verses.accessible: And when someone can withdraw their senses from tempting objects, just as a tortoise pulls its limbs safely inside its shell, their wisdom stands firm.

verses.translation:
Sense objects turn away from the abstinent man,
But the taste for them remains;
But the taste also turns away
From him who has seen the Supreme.
verses.accessible: When people restrain their senses from outer pleasures, the objects fall away, but the inner taste for them lingers. Yet even that subtle craving disappears once they experience the Supreme.
notes: • Flavor being the object of hunger, most basic of desires. t The atman.

verses.translation:
The turbulent senses
Carry away forcibly
The mind, Arjuna,
Even of the striving man of wisdom.
verses.accessible: The senses are so turbulent and powerful, Arjuna, that they can forcibly sweep away the mind of even a wise person who is actively striving for self-control.

verses.translation:
Restraining all these senses,
Disciplined, he should sit, intent on Me;
He whose senses are controlled,
His wisdom stands firm.
verses.accessible: Mastering all the senses, one should sit disciplined and centered on Me. For whoever keeps their senses completely under control has wisdom that stands firm.
When a person constantly dwells on sensory objects, attachment to them develops. From attachment arises selfish desire, and from thwarted desire comes anger.
notes: • The use of three different prefixes to jiiyate (it is born), viz., upa, sam, aMi, testifies to the fact that in Sanskrit, such prefixes are sometimes used merely for elegance (in this case avoidance of repetition), and do not necessarily convey any difference in meaning.

verses.accessible: From anger comes delusion, and from delusion comes confusion of memory. When memory is clouded, clear reasoning is destroyed; and when reasoning is destroyed, a person is completely ruined.

verses.translation:
With the elimination of desire and hatred,
Even though moving among the objects of the senses,
He who is controlled by the Self,
By self-restraint, attains tranquility.
verses.accessible: But a person who moves through the world with senses under control—free from both craving and aversion—attains deep inner peace and serenity.

verses.translation:
In tranquility the cessation of all sorrows
Is born for him.
Indeed, for the tranquil-minded
The intellect at once becomes steady.
verses.accessible: In that inner peace, all sorrows come to an end. For when the mind is serene and clear, the intellect quickly becomes steady and unshakable.

verses.translation:
There is no wisdom in him who is uncontrolled,
And there is likewise no concentration in him who is uncontrolled,
And in him who does not concentrate, there is no peace.
How can there be happiness for him who is not peaceful?
verses.accessible: An undisciplined person lacks wisdom and cannot focus their mind. Without focus, there can be no inner peace; and without peace, how can anyone find happiness?

verses.translation:
When the mind runs
After the wandering senses,
Then it carries away one’s understanding,
As the wind carries away a ship on the waters.
verses.accessible: When the mind constantly chases after the wandering senses, it sweeps away a person's wisdom, just as a sudden gale blows a ship off course on stormy waters.

verses.translation:
Therefore, O Arjuna,
The wisdom of him whose senses
Are withdrawn from the objects of the senses;
That wisdom stands firm.
verses.accessible: Therefore, Arjuna, whoever has completely reined in their senses from tempting objects has wisdom that is firmly rooted.

verses.translation:
The man of restraint is awake
In that which is night for all beings;
The time in which all beings are awake
Is night for the sage who sees.
verses.accessible: What seems like dark night to ordinary people is the time when the self-disciplined sage is wide awake. And what ordinary people are awake to is like dark night to the sage who sees the truth.
notes: .. Meaning that the" sage who sees" perceives the light of the atman, which is dark as night to others, while the others see the light of the senses which is dark as night to the sage.

verses.translation:
Like the ocean, which becomes filled yet remains unmoved and stands still
As the waters enter it,
He whom all desires enter and who remains unmoved
Attains peace; not so the man who is full of desire.
verses.accessible: Just as rivers pour into the ocean, yet the deep ocean remains still and unmoved, all desires flow into the wise person without causing a ripple. Such a person attains peace—never the one who frantically chases desires.
notes: • Trinubh metre.

verses.translation:
The man who abandons all desires
Acts free from longing.
Indifferent to possessions, free from egoticism,
He attains peace.
verses.accessible: Whoever lets go of all selfish cravings and lives free from longing, without possessiveness and without ego, attains true peace.
notes: • Sloka metre resumes.

verses.translation:
This is the divine state, Arjuna.
Having attained this, he is not deluded;
Fixed in it, even at the hour of death,
He reaches the bliss of God.
verses.accessible: This is the divine state of ultimate reality, Arjuna. Once a person attains it, they are never bewildered again. Anchored in this state even at the hour of death, they enter the supreme peace of the Divine.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
If it is Your conviction that knowledge
Is better than action, O Krishna,
Then why do You urge me to engage in this terrible action?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'Krishna, if You believe that spiritual wisdom is superior to action, why do You urge me to engage in this terrible battle?'

verses.translation:
With speech that seems equivocal,
You confuse my intelligence.
Tell me surely this one thing:
How should I attain the highest good?
verses.accessible: Arjuna continued: 'Your words seem contradictory, and they confuse my mind. Tell me decisively: which single path will lead me to the highest good?'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke;
In this world there is a two-fold basis (of devotion)
Taught since ancient times by Me, O Arjuna:
That of knowledge — the yoga of the followers of Sankhya
And that of action — the yoga of the yogins.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'O pure-hearted Arjuna, long ago I taught that there are two spiritual paths in this world: the path of wisdom (Jnana Yoga) for those inclined toward contemplation, and the path of selfless action (Karma Yoga) for those inclined toward active life.'
notes: • See footnote on p. 13 6 .

verses.translation:
Not by abstention from actions
Does a man attain the state beyond karma,
And not by renunciation alone
Does he approach perfection.
verses.accessible: No one attains freedom from karma merely by refusing to act, nor can anyone achieve spiritual perfection simply by giving up all work.

verses.translation:
Indeed, no one, even in the twinkling of an eye,
Ever exists without performing action;
Everyone is forced to perform action, even action which is against his will,
By the qualities which originate in material nature.
verses.accessible: Indeed, no one can remain completely inactive even for a single moment. Every living being is helplessly driven to act by the forces of nature.

verses.translation:
He who sits, restraining his organs of action,
While in his mind brooding over
The objects of the senses, with a deluded mind,
Is said to be a hypocrite.
verses.accessible: Anyone who restrains their physical body while constantly daydreaming about sense pleasures is only deceiving themselves; such a person is a hypocrite.

verses.translation:
But he who undertakes the control
of the senses by the mind, Arjuna,
and, without attachment, engages the organs of action
in the yoga of action, is superior.
verses.accessible: On the other hand, someone who controls their senses with a focused mind and uses their body to perform selfless work without attachment is truly worthy of respect.

verses.translation:
Perform your duty,
For action is indeed better than nonaction,
And even the mere maintenance of your body
Could not be accomplished without action.
verses.accessible: Therefore, carry out your required duties, because taking action is far better than doing nothing. Without action, you could not even maintain your own physical body.

verses.translation:
Aside from action for the purpose of sacrifice,
This world is bound by action.
Perform action for the purpose of sacrifice, Arjuna,
Free from attachment.
verses.accessible: This world is bound by the consequences of action, except when work is done as a selfless offering. Therefore, Arjuna, perform your duties as an offering to the Divine, completely free from selfish attachment.

verses.translation:
Having created mankind along with sacrifice,
Prajapati, (the Lord of Creatures) anciently said,
“By this (i.e. sacrifice), may you bring forth;
May this be your wishfulfilling cow.”
verses.accessible: In the beginning, having created humanity alongside the spirit of sacrifice, the Creator declared: 'May you flourish through this sacrifice; let it be the source that fulfills your righteous desires.'

verses.translation:
“By this (i.e. sacrifice) may you nourish the gods
and may the gods nourish you;
by nourishing each other,
you shall attain the highest welfare.”
verses.accessible: 'Nourish the divine powers of nature through sacrifice, and may they nourish you in return. By supporting one another selflessly, you will achieve the highest prosperity.'
notes: • bhiivayate, "may you cherish," sometimes translated "may you foster," "prosper ye" or "may you nourish," is actually a causative form of the root, ,jbhu, "be," "exist." Thus its literal meaning is "may you cause (the gods) to be." The metaphysical inference is interesting. Man causes the gods to be, and in return the gods cause man to be. This is by no means the only place in religiQus literature where a mutual creation is hinted at man creating god and god creating man. The idea also reminds one of William James' statement in "Essays on Faith and Morals": " I confess that I do not see why the very existence of an invisible world may not depend in part on the personal response which anyone of us may make to the religious appeal. God himself, in short, may draw vital strength and increase of very being from our fidelity."

verses.translation:
“The gods, nourished by the sacrifice,
Will indeed give you desired enjoyments;
He who enjoys these gifts while not offering to them in return,
Is a thief.”
verses.accessible: 'Nourished by your offerings, the divine powers will provide the necessities of life. But anyone who enjoys these gifts without giving back in return is nothing more than a thief.'

verses.translation:
The good, who eat the remainder of the sacrifice,
Are released from all evils;
But the wicked, who cook only for their own sake,
Eat their own impurity.
verses.accessible: Good people who eat what remains after offering food in sacrifice are freed from all guilt. But selfish people who cook only for themselves are truly consuming their own downfall.

verses.translation:
Beings exist from food,
Food is brought into being by rain,
Rain from sacrifice,
And sacrifice is brought into being by action.
verses.accessible: All living beings are sustained by food, and food comes from rain. Rain is generated through the cycle of sacrifice, and sacrifice arises from dedicated action.
notes: • Throughout the Bhagavad Gitii, the word karma (action) is used in several senses. Sometimes, as here, it refers to religious action, the ritual action of the priest performing the sacrifice. Elsewhere it refers to the warlike action proper to the warrior caste to which Arjuna belongs. At still other places it has the meaning of the sum of past actions that is carried into a future life.

verses.translation:
Know that ritual action originates in Brahman (the Vedas)
And Brahman arises from the Imperishable;
Therefore the all-pervading Brahman
Is eternally established in sacrifice.
verses.accessible: Understand that action originates from the divine word of creation, and that word flows from the eternal Supreme Spirit. Therefore, the all-pervading Divine is forever present in every selfless act.
notes: • Edgerton has pointed out that this stanza does not constitute the logical syllogism that it seems on first reading to be. "Sacrifice" is not the starting point of the series, but an intermediate term.

verses.translation:
He who does, here on earth,
Turn the wheel thus set in motion,
Lives, Arjuna,
Maliciously, full of sense delights, and in vain.
verses.accessible: Whoever fails to do their part in keeping this cosmic wheel of life turning lives a selfish life. Indulging only their personal cravings, Arjuna, they live in vain.
notes: • I.e. The circular sequence: sacrifice, the rain god, food, beings, sacrifice, the rain god, etc. etc.

verses.translation:
He whose delight is only in the Self,
Whose satisfaction is in the Self,
And who is content only in the Self;
For him the need to act does not exist.
verses.accessible: Yet for the person who finds joy within the true Self, who is completely satisfied in the Self and content with who they truly are, there are no obligations left to fulfill.

verses.translation:
He has no purpose at all in action,
Or in non-action,
And he has no need of any being
For any purpose whatsoever.
verses.accessible: Such an enlightened soul has nothing to gain from what they do, nor anything to lose from what they leave undone. They do not depend on anyone in this world for anything.

verses.translation:
Therefore, constantly unattached,
Perform that action which is your duty.
Indeed, by performing action while unattached,
Man attains the Supreme.
verses.accessible: Therefore, always carry out your duties without personal attachment. By working selflessly, a person attains the highest spiritual realization.
notes: • The" therefore" is not a consequence of the preceding stanzas, which describe the person who has attained complete concentration on the atman. This stanza is the advice to Arjuna to perform action while unattached, in order to attain the state described in III 17 and 18.

verses.translation:
Perfection was attained by kings like Janaka
With action alone.
For the mere maintenance of the world,
You should act.
verses.accessible: King Janaka and other great leaders reached perfection through action alone. Even if only to guide society and maintain order in the world, you should do your duty.
notes: • Janaka, a famous philosopher king who, with his priest and adviser, Yajfiavalkya, opposed the brahman priesthood, claiming that he himself, though a member of the warrior caste, could perform sacrifices without brahman help. Eventually he became a brahman and a riijar$i, or royal seer. He was the father of Sita, the heroine of the Ramayat)a. He is thought to have influenced the Buddha, who was also a member of the k~atriya caste. The reference is to J anaka, as a k~atriya (warrior or doer) attaining perfection through deeds rather than austerities.

verses.translation:
Whatever the greatest man does,
Thus do the rest;
Whatever standard he sets,
The world follows that.
verses.accessible: Whatever an exemplary leader does, others will imitate. Whatever standard they set, the rest of the world follows.

verses.translation:
For Me, O Arjuna, there is nothing whatever
To be done in the three worlds,
Nor is there anything not attained to be attained.
Nevertheless I engage in action.
verses.accessible: Arjuna, there is nothing in all the three worlds that I am required to do, nor is there anything I lack that I need to attain. Yet I still remain constantly engaged in action.

verses.translation:
Indeed, if I, unwearied, should not engage
In action at all,
Mankind would follow
My path everywhere, O Arjuna.
verses.accessible: If I were ever to stop working tirelessly, Arjuna, people everywhere would follow My example and abandon their responsibilities.

verses.translation:
If I did not perform action,
These worlds would perish
And I would be the cause of confusion;
I would destroy these creatures.
verses.accessible: If I ceased to act, these worlds would fall into ruin. I would cause moral confusion and bring about the destruction of all these living beings.

verses.translation:
While those who are unwise act
From attachment to action, O Arjuna,
So the wise should act without attachment,
Intending to maintain the welfare of the world.
verses.accessible: Just as the unwise act out of selfish attachment to their work, Arjuna, the wise should act without attachment, working solely for the welfare and guidance of the world.

verses.translation:
One should not unsettle the minds of
The ignorant who are attached to action;
The wise one should cause them to enjoy all actions,
While himself performing actions in a disciplined manner.
verses.accessible: Wise people should not confuse the minds of the ignorant who are attached to the fruits of their labor. Instead, by performing their own duties with discipline and joy, they should inspire everyone to do their work.

verses.translation:
Actions in all cases are performed
By the qualities of material nature;
He whose mind is confused by egoism
Imagines, “I am the doer.”
verses.accessible: All actions in this world are carried out by the forces of material nature. But when a person is deluded by ego, they mistakenly think, 'I am the doer.'

verses.translation:
But he who knows the truth, O Arjuna,
About the two roles of the qualities and action, thinking,
“The qualities work among the qualities,”
Is not attached.
verses.accessible: However, someone who understands the truth about nature's forces and human action knows that nature's qualities are merely interacting with other qualities of nature. Understanding this, Arjuna, they never become attached.

verses.translation:
Those deluded by the qualities of material nature
Are attached to the actions of the qualities.
The perfect knower should not disturb
The foolish men of incomplete knowledge.
verses.accessible: Those who are misled by the forces of nature become deeply attached to the actions of their senses. Those who see the full truth should not shake the faith of those who only understand part of it.

verses.translation:
Deferring all actions in Me,
Meditating on the supreme Spirit,
Having become free from desire and selfishness,
With your fever departed, fight!
verses.accessible: Surrender all your actions to Me, keep your mind centered on the divine Self, let go of selfish desire and ego, and with your inner turmoil healed, stand up and fight!
notes: • I.e. allowing God to initiate all actions.

verses.translation:
Men who constantly practice
This teaching of Mine,
Believing, not sneering,
Are also released from the bondage of actions.
verses.accessible: Those who consistently live by this teaching of Mine, full of sincere faith and free from cynical fault-finding, are also freed from the binding chains of their actions.

verses.translation:
But those who, sneering at this,
Do not practice My teaching,
Confusing all wisdom,
Know them to be lost and mindless.
verses.accessible: But those who scoff at My teaching and refuse to practice it are blind to all true wisdom. Know that such mindless critics are completely lost.

verses.translation:
One acts according to one’s own material nature.
Even the wise man does so.
Beings follow their own material nature;
What will restraint accomplish?
verses.accessible: Even wise people act according to their own innate nature, and all living creatures follow their natural tendencies. What good can mere physical repression do?

verses.translation:
Passion and hatred are seated
In the senses in relation to their objects.
One should not come under the power of these two;
They are indeed one’s enemies.
verses.accessible: Attraction and aversion naturally arise between each of the senses and their objects. Do not let yourself be ruled by them, for they are spiritual ambushes along your path.

verses.translation:
Better one’s own duty though deficient
Than the duty of another well performed.
Better is death in one’s own duty;
The duty of another invites danger.
verses.accessible: It is far better to perform your own duty imperfectly than to master someone else's duty. Even death while fulfilling your own path brings honor, whereas trying to live another person's destiny is full of danger.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
Then impelled, by what
Does a man commit this evil,
Unwillingly even, O Krishna,
As if urged by force?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'Krishna, what drives a person to commit evil, even against their own will, as if compelled by an overpowering force?'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
This force is desire, this force is anger;
Its source is the rajas guna.
Voracious and greatly injurious,
Know this to be the enemy.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'It is selfish desire, which turns into anger when blocked. Born from the driving energy of passion (rajas), it has an insatiable appetite and causes immense harm. Recognize this as your greatest enemy in the world.'

verses.translation:
As fire is obscured by smoke,
And a mirror by dust,
As the embryo is enveloped by the membrane,
So the intellect is obscured by passion.
verses.accessible: Just as smoke conceals a burning fire, dust clouds a clear mirror, or the womb encloses an unborn child, so human wisdom is shrouded by selfish desire.

verses.translation:
O Arjuna, the knowledge even of the wise ones is obscured
By this eternal enemy,
Having the form of desire,
Which is as insatiable fire.
verses.accessible: Arjuna, the understanding of even the wisest people is obscured by this constant adversary—desire—which burns like an unquenchable fire that can never be satisfied.

verses.translation:
The senses, the mind and the intellect
Are said to be its (i.e. the eternal enemy’s) abode;
With these, it confuses the embodied one,
Obscuring his knowledge.
verses.accessible: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are the base camps where this enemy hides. By working through them, desire clouds our judgment and confuses the inner soul.

verses.translation:
Therefore, restraining the senses
First, O Arjuna,
Kill this evil demon
Which destroys knowledge and discrimination.
verses.accessible: Therefore, Arjuna, begin by bringing your senses under control. Then strike down this destructive enemy, which annihilates both spiritual knowledge and practical wisdom.
They say that the senses are powerful, but the mind is higher than the senses. The intellect is higher than the mind, and higher still than the intellect is the divine Self.
notes: • I.e. the Yoga of action, without desire for the fruits of action, see following stanza, also stanzas 40 and 41.

verses.translation:
Thus having known that which is higher than the intellect,
Sustaining the self by the Self,
Kill the enemy, O Arjuna,
Which has the form of desire and is difficult to conquer.
verses.accessible: Knowing that the Self is supreme above all, strengthen your lower self through the power of your higher Self. Conquering all inner weakness, Arjuna, defeat this formidable enemy known as selfish desire.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
I proclaimed this imperishable yoga to Vivasvat;
Vivasvat communicated it to Manu,
And Manu imparted it to Ikshvaku.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'I taught this imperishable wisdom of yoga to Vivasvat, the sun deity. Vivasvat passed it down to Manu, the father of humanity, and Manu instructed King Ikshvaku.'
notes: • Vivasvat, the Sun god. t Manu, Manu Vaivasvata, son of the Sun god. t Ik~vaku, son of Manu Vaivasvata. All are early legendary figures. See chapter on "The Setting of the Bhagavad Gita."

verses.translation:
Thus received by succession,
The royal seers knew this;
After a long time here on earth,
This yoga has been lost, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Passed down through this unbroken lineage of royal sages, this sacred wisdom was preserved. But over the ages, Arjuna, the knowledge was gradually lost to the world.

verses.translation:
This ancient yoga is today
Declared by Me to you,
Since you are My devotee and friend.
This secret is supreme indeed.
verses.accessible: Today, I am revealing this very same ancient yoga to you, because you are My devotee and My dear friend. This is the ultimate spiritual secret.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
Your birth was later,
The birth of Vivasvat earlier;
How should I understand this,
That You declared it in the beginning?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'You were born in our own era, while Vivasvat lived at the dawn of creation. How can I understand that You taught this wisdom to him in the very beginning?'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Many of My births have passed away,
And also yours, Arjuna.
I know them all;
You do not know them, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Arjuna, both you and I have passed through many lifetimes. I remember every one of them, but you have forgotten them.'

verses.translation:
Although I am birthless and My nature is imperishable,
Although I am the Lord of all beings,
Yet, by controlling My own material nature,
I come into being by My own power.
verses.accessible: Although I am unborn, imperishable in nature, and the Lord of all living beings, I master My own material creation and manifest in the world through My divine creative power.
notes: • There appears to be a contradiction here between "birthless" and "many of my births" of the preceding stanza, but Krishna's "births" refer to his "giving forth" of himself see following stanza.

verses.translation:
Whenever a decrease of righteousness
Exists, Arjuna,
And there is a rising up of unrighteousness,
Then I manifest Myself.
verses.accessible: Whenever righteousness declines in the world, Arjuna, and injustice and moral chaos surge, I embody Myself on earth.

verses.translation:
For the protection of the good
And the destruction of evil doers,
For the sake of establishing righteousness,
I am born in every age.
verses.accessible: To protect the good, to defeat wickedness, and to firmly re-establish righteousness, I appear age after age.
notes: • This conception of the" coming into being" from age to age to protect the good and punish the evil is not confined to Hunduism. Buddhism has a Buddha who arrives at different times for that purpose. Messianic Judaism, and thus Christianity, have parallels, though they require only one visitation of the Messiah, or avatar of God.

verses.translation:
He who knows in truth
My divine birth and action,
Having left his body, he is
Not reborn; he comes to Me, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Whoever truly understands the divine mystery of My birth and My work does not enter another cycle of rebirth when they leave this body; they come directly to Me, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Thinking solely of Me, resorting to Me,
Many whose greed, fear, and anger have departed,
Purified by the austerity of knowledge,
Have attained My state of being.
verses.accessible: Freed from selfish craving, fear, and anger, completely absorbed in Me and taking refuge in Me, countless seekers have been purified by the transforming fire of wisdom and have reached My divine state of being.

verses.translation:
In whatever way,
Men take refuge in Me, I reward them.
Men everywhere, Arjuna,
Follow My path.
verses.accessible: In whatever way people seek to connect with Me, I receive and welcome them accordingly. Whichever spiritual path they take, Arjuna, all seekers are ultimately walking toward Me.

verses.translation:
Desiring the success of ritual acts,
Men sacrifice here on earth to the Vedic gods.
Quickly indeed in the world of men
Ritual acts bring success.
verses.accessible: People longing for immediate success in their endeavors make offerings to the gods of this world, because in human society, worldly actions quickly yield outward results.

verses.translation:
The system of four castes was created by Me,
According to the distribution of the qualities and their acts.
Although I am the creator of this (the system),
Know Me to be the eternal non-doer.
verses.accessible: I created the four divisions of society based on each person's natural qualities and tendencies for work. Yet even though I am their creator, know that I remain the changeless, detached non-doer.
Actions do not bind Me, nor do I crave the results of any work. Anyone who truly understands this about My nature is also never bound by their own actions.

verses.translation:
Having known this, the ancients,
Seeking release, also performed action.
Therefore perform action
As it was earlier performed by the ancients.
verses.accessible: Knowing this truth, the ancient seekers of liberation carried out their responsibilities without attachment. Therefore, you too should perform your work, following the footsteps of those who came before you.

verses.translation:
“What is action? What is inaction?”
Thus, even the wise are confused in this matter.
This action I shall explain to you,
Having known which, you shall be released from evil.
verses.accessible: 'What is true action, and what is inaction?' Even the wisest thinkers are often puzzled by this question. I will explain the reality of action to you, and knowing this will free you from harm.
notes: • kavayas, poets. One must remember that much of Sanskrit religious literature was conceived in poetic form. Thus "poets" here (often translated "sages") were religious teachers who wrote, or rather sang, in verse.

verses.translation:
One must know the nature of action,
The nature of wrong action,
And also the nature of inaction.
The way of action is profound.
verses.accessible: You must understand right action, understand harmful action, and also understand inaction. The true nature of action is subtle and profound.

verses.translation:
He who perceives inaction in action,
And action in inaction,
Is wise among men;
He is a yogi and performs all actions.
verses.accessible: Whoever sees stillness within action, and action within stillness, is truly wise among human beings. That person is a yogi who lives in complete harmony, accomplishing all work without being bound by it.

verses.translation:
He who has excluded desire and motive
From all his enterprises,
And has consumed his karma in the fire of knowledge,
Him the wise men call a sage.
verses.accessible: The wise call a person a true sage when all their endeavors are free from selfish ambition, and their past karma has been completely consumed in the purifying fire of wisdom.

verses.translation:
He who has abandoned all attachment to the fruits of action,
Always content, not dependent,
Even when performing action,
Does, in effect, nothing at all.
verses.accessible: Letting go of attachment to the fruits of their work, always inwardly fulfilled and free from outside dependence, they do nothing at all in an ego-driven sense, even while actively engaged in tasks.

verses.translation:
Performing action with the body alone,
Without wish, restrained in thought and self,
With all motives of acquisition abandoned
He incurs no evil.
verses.accessible: Free from cravings, with thoughts and impulses disciplined, having released the desire to possess things, they perform action with their body alone and incur no negative consequences.

verses.translation:
Content with whatever comes to him,
Transcending the dualities (i.e. pleasure, pain, etc.), free from envy,
Constant in mind whether in success or in failure,
Even though he acts, he is not bound.
verses.accessible: Content with whatever comes without clinging, rising above the pairs of opposites like pleasure and pain, free from jealousy, and calm in both success and failure, they are not bound even while they act.

verses.translation:
The work of one who is free from attachment, who is liberated,
Whose thought is established in knowledge,
Who does work only as a sacrifice,
Is wholly dissolved.
verses.accessible: When someone works without selfish attachment, living in spiritual freedom with their mind firmly rooted in wisdom, their actions are performed purely as a sacrifice, and all their karmic ties dissolve completely.

verses.translation:
Brahman is the offering, Brahman is the oblation
Poured out by Brahman into the fire of Brahman,
Brahman is to be attained by him
Who always sees Brahman in action.
verses.accessible: The act of offering is Divine, the offering itself is Divine, poured by the Divine into the fire of the Divine. Those who see the Divine in every action will surely attain the Divine.
notes: • "The entire act consists of Brahman because it is of Brahman's nature: the sacrifice is Brahman, the utensils are Brahman, the fire in which the sacrifice is offered is Brahman, the sacrificer himself is Brahman. He who contemplates this insight, contemplates the act-as-Brahman. Such a one is capable of knowing the proper form of the titman which is Brahman through his acts, because his acts are of Brahman's nature. In other words, the acts performed by an aspirant have the form of knowledge because they imply the realization that they consist of Brahman and are therefore a means of contemplating the titman ..... Ramanuja, tr. van Buitenen.

verses.translation:
Some yogins perform
Sacrifice to the gods;
Others offer sacrifice,
By sacrifice itself, in the fire of Brahman.
verses.accessible: Some yogis perform external rituals to the gods, while other spiritual seekers offer their very sense of self into the fire of the Supreme Spirit.

verses.translation:
Others offer senses like hearing
In the fire of restraint;
Still others offer sound and other objects of the senses
In the fire of the senses.
verses.accessible: Some offer their senses, like hearing and sight, into the fire of disciplined self-control, while others offer external sounds and sensations into the fire of their senses without getting attached.

verses.translation:
Others offer all actions of the senses
And actions of the vital breath
In the fire of the yoga of self-restraint,
Which is kindled by knowledge.
verses.accessible: Others surrender all the activities of their senses and the life-breath into the fire of self-mastery, which has been ignited by spiritual wisdom.

verses.translation:
Some offer as sacrifice their material possessions
Or their austerities and practice of yoga,
While ascetics of severe vows
Offer study of the scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.
verses.accessible: Some make a sacrifice of their material wealth, others sacrifice through self-discipline or the practice of meditation, while dedicated seekers of firm resolve offer the study of sacred teachings and wisdom as their sacrifice.

verses.translation:
Some offer inhalation into exhalation,
And others exhalation into inhalation,
Restraining the path of inhalation and exhalation,
Intent on control of the vital breath.
verses.accessible: Some practice breath control by offering the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, or the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, calming the flow of their life-force.
notes: • These are Yoga breathing excercises, as yet understood by few in the West, but familiar to all Yogins.

verses.translation:
Others who have restricted their foods
Offer the life breath into the life breath;
All these are knowers of sacrifice,
And their evils have been destroyed through sacrifice.
verses.accessible: Others practice mindful fasting, offering the life-energy into itself. All these practitioners understand the sacred meaning of sacrifice, and through their dedication, their impurities are burned away.

verses.translation:
The enjoyers of the nectar of the sacrificial remnants
Go to primeval Brahman.
Not even this world is for the non-sacrificing;
How then the other, Arjuna?
verses.accessible: Those who taste the nectar of selfless sacrifice unite with the eternal Supreme Spirit. But for someone who gives nothing in sacrifice, this present world holds no joy—so how could the next world be any better, Arjuna?

verses.translation:
Thus sacrifices are of many kinds,
Spread out before Brahman.
Know them all to be born of action.
Thus knowing, you shall be released.
verses.accessible: In these many ways, different forms of sacrifice are open before the Divine, and all of them are born through action. When you understand this truth, you will find spiritual freedom.

verses.translation:
Better than the sacrifice of material possessions
Is the wisdom sacrifice, Arjuna;
All action without exception, Arjuna,
Is fully comprehended in wisdom.
verses.accessible: Offering the sacrifice of spiritual wisdom is far greater than sacrificing material possessions, Arjuna, because all purposeful action ultimately reaches its fulfillment in wisdom.

verses.translation:
Know this! Through humble submission,
Through enquiry, through service (on your own part),
The knowing ones, the perceivers of truth,
Will be led to teach you knowledge.
verses.accessible: Learn this truth by approaching a wise teacher with reverence, asking thoughtful questions, and offering sincere service. The enlightened ones who see reality will guide you into wisdom.

verses.translation:
Knowing that, you shall not again
Fall into delusion, Arjuna;
And by that knowledge you shall see all beings
In yourself, and also in Me.
verses.accessible: Once you receive this wisdom, Arjuna, you will never fall into confusion again. By its light, you will see all living beings within your own true Self, and all beings within Me.

verses.translation:
Even if you were the most evil
Of all evildoers,
You would cross over all wickedness
By the boat of knowledge.
verses.accessible: Even if you were considered the most flawed of all wrongdoers, you would cross over the ocean of all your mistakes aboard the boat of spiritual wisdom.

verses.translation:
As the kindled fire
Reduces firewood to ashes, Arjuna,
So the fire of knowledge
Reduces all actions to ashes.
