verses.accessible: Just as a roaring fire reduces firewood to ashes, Arjuna, so the blazing fire of spiritual wisdom burns the binding effects of all actions to ashes.

verses.translation:
No purifier equal to knowledge
Is found here in the world;
He who is himself perfected in yoga
In time finds that knowledge in the Self.
verses.accessible: There is no purifier in this world as powerful as wisdom. Anyone who matures in the practice of yoga discovers that wisdom blossoming naturally within their own heart in due time.

verses.translation:
He who possesses faith attains knowledge;
Devoted to that (knowledge), restraining his senses,
Having attained knowledge, he quickly attains
Supreme peace.
verses.accessible: A person with sincere faith, deep dedication, and mastery over their senses attains this wisdom. Having attained wisdom, they quickly enter into supreme peace.

verses.translation:
The man who is ignorant, and does not have faith,
Who is of a doubting nature, is destroyed.
Neither this world nor that beyond,
Nor happiness, is for him who doubts.
verses.accessible: Those who lack understanding and faith, and whose hearts are poisoned by constant doubt, ruin themselves. For someone consumed by doubt, there is no peace in this world, no hope for the next, and no happiness anywhere.

verses.translation:
Action does not bind him
Who has renounced action through yoga,
Whose doubt is cut away by knowledge,
And who is possessed of the Self, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Actions have no power to bind someone who has surrendered their work through yoga, whose doubts have been cut to pieces by wisdom, and who is firmly centered in the Self, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Therefore, having cut away, with your own sword of knowledge,
This doubt that proceeds from ignorance and abides in your heart,
Resort to yoga!
Stand up, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Therefore, draw the sword of spiritual wisdom and cut away this paralyzing doubt born of ignorance in your heart. Embrace the path of selfless action, Arjuna, and stand up!

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
You praise renunciation of actions,
And again You praise yoga, Krishna.
Which one is the better of these two?
Tell this to me definitely.
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'Krishna, first You praise the renunciation of actions, but then You praise the path of selfless action. Which of these two is truly better? Please tell me clearly.'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Both renunciation and the yoga of action
Lead to incomparable bliss;
Of the two, however, the yoga of action
Is superior to the renunciation of action.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Both renouncing action and practicing selfless action lead to the highest spiritual freedom. But of the two, selfless action is better than merely giving up action.'
notes: • Ramanuja:" Both the Yoga of action and the Yoga of knowledge are ... equally autonomous means of attaining beatitude. But the Yoga of action is better than the Yoga of knowledge." The reason is that the atman can be secured through the Yoga of action. The aim of both is the same, but the Yoga of knowledge cannot be attained without the prior acquisition of the Yoga of action.

verses.translation:
He is to be known as the eternal sannyasi
Who neither hates nor desires,
Who is indifferent to the pairs of opposites, O Arjuna.
He is easily liberated from bondage.
verses.accessible: You should recognize someone as a true, lifelong renunciant if they neither hate nor crave anything. Being free from conflicting desires, Arjuna, they easily break free from the bonds of karma.

verses.translation:
“Sankhya and yoga are different,”
The childish declare; not the wise.
Even with one of them, practiced correctly,
One finds the fruit of both.
verses.accessible: Only beginners claim that the path of knowledge and the path of action are separate. The wise know that if you truly master even one of these paths, you gain the complete rewards of both.

verses.translation:
The place that is attained by the followers of Sankhya
Is also attained by the followers of yoga.
Sankhya and yoga are one.
He who perceives this, truly perceives.
verses.accessible: The spiritual state reached through knowledge is also reached through selfless action. The path of knowledge and the path of action are truly one, and whoever sees this sees the truth.

verses.translation:
Renunciation indeed, O Arjuna,
Is difficult to attain without yoga;
The sage who is disciplined in yoga
Quickly attains Brahman.
verses.accessible: Giving up action is very difficult to achieve without selfless action, Arjuna. But a thoughtful person who practices selfless action quickly attains union with the Divine.

verses.translation:
He who is devoted to yoga, whose self is purified,
Whose self is subdued, whose senses are conquered,
Whose self has become the self of all beings,
Is not tainted even when acting.
verses.accessible: Those devoted to selfless action purify their hearts, master their impulses, and control their senses. They see their own self in every living creature, so they remain untainted even while working in the world.

verses.translation:
“I do not do anything,” thus,
Steadfast in yoga, the knower of truth should think,
Whether seeing, hearing, touching, smelling,
Eating, walking, sleeping, breathing.
verses.accessible: Those who know the truth and are grounded in yoga understand, 'I am not really doing anything at all.' They remember this while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, or breathing.

verses.translation:
Talking, excreting, grasping,
Opening the eyes and shutting the eyes,
Believing
“The senses abide in the objects of the senses.”
verses.accessible: Even when speaking, letting go, grasping, or opening and closing their eyes, they realize it is only the senses interacting with the world.

verses.translation:
Offering his actions to Brahman,
Having abandoned attachment,
He who acts is not tainted by evil
Any more than a lotus leaf by water.
verses.accessible: Those who dedicate all their actions to the Divine and let go of selfish attachment are never stained by sin. Like a lotus leaf floating on water, they remain untouched by moisture.

verses.translation:
With the body, with the mind, with the intellect,
Even merely with the senses,
The yogins perform action toward self-purification,
Having abandoned attachment.
verses.accessible: Letting go of selfish attachment, yogis act using only their body, mind, intellect, and senses. Their work is done solely for inner purification.

verses.translation:
He who is disciplined in yoga, having abandoned the fruit of action,
Attains steady peace;
The undisciplined one, attached to fruit,
Is bound by actions prompted by desire.
verses.accessible: Whoever is disciplined in yoga lets go of results and finds lasting peace. But undisciplined people, driven by selfish craving and clinging to rewards, remain trapped by what they do.

verses.translation:
Renouncing all actions with the mind,
The embodied one sits happily, as the ruler
Within the city of nine gates,
Not acting at all, nor causing action.
verses.accessible: Mentally letting go of all attachment to action, the embodied soul rests peacefully as ruler of the body—a city with nine gates. It neither acts with ego nor forces anything to happen.
notes: • "the city whose gates are nine." The "city" is the body. The" nine gates" are the two eyes, the two ears, the two nostrils, the mouth and the organs of excretion and generation.

verses.translation:
The Lord does not create
Either the agency (the means of action) or the actions of people,
Or the union of action with its fruit.
Nature, on the other hand, proceeds (in all this).
verses.accessible: The Lord does not create human ego, nor does He force people to act or connect actions to their rewards. All of these unfold naturally through the workings of material nature.

verses.translation:
The Lord does not receive
Either the evil or the good deeds of anyone.
Knowledge is enveloped by ignorance.
By it (ignorance) people are deluded.
verses.accessible: The Lord does not take on anyone's good or bad deeds. Spiritual wisdom is clouded by ignorance, and that is why people become confused.

verses.translation:
But for those in whom this ignorance of the Self
Is destroyed by knowledge,
That knowledge of theirs
Causes the Supreme to shine like the sun.
verses.accessible: Yet when ignorance of the Self is destroyed by spiritual knowledge, that wisdom shines like the rising sun, revealing the supreme reality.

verses.translation:
They whose minds are absorbed in that (i.e. the Supreme),
Whose selves are fixed on that,
Whose basis is that, who hold that as the highest object,
Whose evils have been shaken off by knowledge, go to the end of rebirth.
verses.accessible: With their minds absorbed in the Supreme, their souls anchored in it, and their flaws washed clean by wisdom, they reach the state of freedom where suffering never returns.

verses.translation:
The wise see the same (Atman)
In a brahman endowed with wisdom and cultivation,
In a cow, in an elephant,
And even in a dog or in an outcaste.
verses.accessible: The wise look with equal vision upon all living beings. They see the same divine presence in an educated and humble scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog, or a social outcast.
notes: • Dog-cooker, a type of outcaste, offspring of a sadra father and a brahman mother, or offspring of a cal:u!ala (son of a sadra father and a brahman mother), or of a prostitute, or of parents of various foreign mountain tribes, or of parents of a mixed ktatriya and sadra lineage, or of mixed ktatriya and vaisya lineage. Such people served as public executioners and in other menial or unpleasant occupations.

verses.translation:
Even here on earth, rebirth is conquered
By those whose mind is established in impartiality.
Brahman is spotless and impartial;
Therefore they are established in Brahman.
verses.accessible: Those whose minds are established in equality conquer the cycle of rebirth right here on earth. Because the Divine is flawless and treats everyone equally, they live rooted in the Divine.
notes: to The word" impartial" refers to those who "see the same," i.e. see that all atmans are identical with their own (see introductory chapter on Cosmology).

verses.translation:
One should not rejoice upon attaining what is pleasant,
Nor should one shudder upon encountering what is unpleasant;
With firm intellect, undeluded,
Knowing Brahman, one is established in Brahman.
verses.accessible: Do not get carried away with excitement when something pleasant happens, and do not fall into despair when facing what is unpleasant. With clear understanding, free from confusion, the knower of the Divine rests securely in the Divine.

verses.translation:
He whose self is unattached to external sensations,
Who finds happiness in the Self,
Whose Self is united with Brahman through yoga,
Reaches imperishable happiness.
verses.accessible: Those who are unattached to external sensory pleasures find deep joy within themselves. United with the Divine through yoga, they enjoy happiness that never fades.

verses.translation:
Pleasures born of contact, indeed,
Are wombs (i.e. sources) of pain,
Since they have a beginning and an end (i.e. are not eternal), Arjuna.
The wise man is not content with them.
verses.accessible: Pleasures that come from the physical senses are actually sources of pain, Arjuna, because they have a beginning and an end. A wise person does not look for lasting happiness in them.

verses.translation:
He who is able to endure here on earth,
Before liberation from the body,
The agitation that arises from desire and anger,
Is disciplined; he is a happy man.
verses.accessible: Whoever learns to master the turbulent urges of desire and anger right here in this body, before death comes, is truly disciplined and happy.

verses.translation:
He who finds his happiness within, his delight within,
And his light within,
This yogin attains the bliss of
Brahman, becoming Brahman.
verses.accessible: The yogi who finds happiness within, peace within, and inner light attains union with the Divine. Such a person experiences the supreme bliss of spiritual freedom.
notes: • nirviiIJa, from nir ";vii, "blowout" as a candle is blown out, refers to the final extinction of the "self," following the round of rebirths, which the Hindus (Buddhists of the Theravada School too) regard as the ultimately desirable state of nonbeing. It is related to the Hindu belief that to be born at all is a tragedy.

verses.translation:
The seers, whose evils have been destroyed,
Whose doubts have been cut away, whose selves are restrained,
Who delight in the welfare of all beings,
Attain the bliss of Brahman.
verses.accessible: Sages whose flaws are erased, whose doubts are resolved, and whose minds are disciplined attain divine peace. They find deep joy in working for the welfare of all living beings.

verses.translation:
To those ascetics who have cast aside desire and anger,
Whose thought is controlled,
Who are knowers of the Self,
The bliss of Brahman exists everywhere.
verses.accessible: For seekers who have cast away craving and anger, mastered their thoughts, and realized their true Self, the peace of the Divine is ever-present all around them.

verses.translation:
Expelling outside contacts
And fixing the gaze between the two eyebrows,
Equalizing the inhalation and exhalation,
Moving within the nostrils,
verses.accessible: A meditating sage shuts out external sensory distractions. They steady their gaze between the eyebrows and balance the breath moving in and out through the nostrils.
notes: • These are elementary Yoga exercises, wellknown to all yogins. It might be remarked that, according to modern physiology and psychology, eye movement is apt to accompany thought, even such unconscious thought as occurs in dreams. " Putting the gaze between the two eyebrows," in other words rolling the eyeballs to their highest attainable point and drawing them toward the nose, keeping them there steadily, is a method of inhibiting thought. The other directions are for Yoga breathing exercises.

verses.accessible: With senses, mind, and intellect fully mastered, and liberation as their highest goal, the seeker who has cast off desire, fear, and anger is free forever.

verses.translation:
Having known Me, the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities,
The mighty Lord of all the world,
The friend of all creatures,
He (the sage) attains peace.
verses.accessible: Recognizing Me as the ultimate receiver of all devotions, the supreme Lord of all worlds, and the devoted friend of every living creature, the seeker attains everlasting peace.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
He who performs that action which is his duty,
While renouncing the fruit of action,
Is a renunciant and a yogin;
Not he who is without a consecrated fire, and who fails to perform sacred rites.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'The true renunciant and the real yogi is the one who performs their duties without depending on the rewards of their work. It is not someone who merely abandons their responsibilities or stops tending the sacred fire.'

verses.translation:
That which they call renunciation,
Know that to be yoga, Arjuna.
Without renouncing selfish purpose,
No one becomes a yogin.
verses.accessible: Understand that what is called renunciation is truly the same as yoga, Arjuna. No one can ever become a yogi without first letting go of selfish motives.

verses.translation:
For the sage desirous of attaining yoga,
Action is said to be the means;
For him who has already attained yoga,
Tranquility is said to be the means.
verses.accessible: For a seeker striving to ascend the path of yoga, selfless action is the essential means. But for one who has already reached the summit of yoga, inner stillness becomes the means.
notes: • By karmayoga (the Yoga of Action) one is able to succeed in Yoga because in karmayoga one does not risk being negligent about it. When a man aspires to the contemplation, i.e. to release, karmayoga will cause him to succeed; only when the contemplation of the iitman has already been secured, willjiiiinayoga (the Yoga of Knowledge), i.e. inactivity, cause him to succeed; or, in other words, a man must perform acts until he has attained release. Now, when has a man attained Yoga? When the yogin is no longer able to interest himself in the objects of prakrti (material nature) differing from the litman, or in corresponding acts, because naturally he does not experience anything but the iitman; for then all desires have gone. When a man wishes to attain Yoga, then he can only do so by practicing karmayoga, for at that stage one is still unable not to experience the objects and therefore karmayoga is one's only resource, because karmayoga means practicing one's interest in objects. However, one should save oneself by disengaging one's mind from its interest in objects and not perish by neglecting to do so. - Rllmllnuja.

verses.translation:
When he is attached neither to the objects of the senses
Nor to actions,
And has renounced all purpose,
He is then said to have attained yoga.
verses.accessible: A person is said to have truly mastered yoga when they are no longer attached to sensory pleasures or to their own actions, having completely surrendered all selfish ambitions.
notes: • See footnote previous stanza.

verses.accessible: Uplift yourself through the power of your own mind, and never drag yourself down. For your own mind can be your greatest friend, and your own mind can be your worst enemy.
notes: • In the case of one who is saving himself by disengaging his mind from its interest in the objects of sense, the mind (manas) will be his friend; in the case of one who wishes not to perish by neglecting to so disengage his mind, mind (manas) will be his enemy and bring about the opposite of beatitude freely adapted from Ramanuja, who thus equates manas (mind) with iitman (self) in interpreting this stanza.

verses.translation:
For him who has conquered himself by the Self,
The Self is a friend;
But for him who has not conquered himself,
The Self remains hostile, like an enemy.
verses.accessible: For someone who has conquered their mind through self-discipline, the mind is a loyal friend. But for one whose mind is undisciplined, that same mind remains hostile and behaves like an enemy.
notes: • See previous footnote.

verses.translation:
The highest Self of him who has conquered himself
And is peaceful, is steadfast
In cold, heat, pleasure, and pain;
Thus also in honor and dishonor.
verses.accessible: The higher Self of one who has mastered their mind and found inner peace remains steady through heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honor and disgrace.
notes: • Highest self, the self which has been exalted by Yoga practice.

verses.translation:
The yogin who is satisfied with knowledge and discrimination,
Who is unchanging, with conquered senses,
To whom a clod, a stone, and gold are the same,
Is said to have attained samadhi.
verses.accessible: A yogi who is deeply satisfied with spiritual wisdom and direct experience, who is unwavering and in full control of the senses, is firmly established in yoga. To such a person, a lump of dirt, a common stone, and pure gold are all the same.
notes: • Discrimination, i.e. knowledge of the iitman as well as of the iitman as a different entity from prakrti (material nature).

verses.translation:
He who is equal-minded toward friend, companion, and enemy,
Who is neutral among enemies and kinsmen,
And who is impartial among the righteous and also among the evil,
Is to be distinguished among men.
verses.accessible: That person stands out as truly exceptional who looks with equal goodwill upon friends, companions, enemies, neutral observers, mediators, critics, relatives, and both the saint and the sinner.
notes: • A consequence of contemplation of the dtman exclusively.

verses.translation:
The yogin should concentrate constantly
On the Self, remaining in solitude,
Alone, with controlled mind and body,
Having no desires and destitute of possessions.
verses.accessible: A yogi should regularly practice meditation in a quiet, solitary place. They should master their body and mind, living free from constant desires and the urge to possess things.

verses.translation:
Establishing a firm seat for himself
In a clean place,
Not too high, not too low,
Covered with a cloth, an antelope skin, and kusha grass,
verses.accessible: In a clean and quiet setting, they should prepare a stable seat that is neither too high nor too low. It should be comfortably layered with kusha grass, a deer skin, and a soft cloth.
notes: • N.B. The kusa grass is on the bottom, the antelope skin on top of it, and the cloth topmost. This was the proper seat for the meditating yogin.

verses.translation:
There, having directed his mind to a single object,
With his thought and the activity of the senses controlled,
Seating himself on the seat, he should practice
Yoga for the purpose of self-purification.
verses.accessible: Sitting there, focusing the mind on a single point and calming thoughts and senses, one should practice meditation for inner purification.
notes: • Directing the mind (concentrating it) on a single point or object is one of the preliminary techniques of Yoga. Its purpose is control of the mind, which tends to wander. It is very difficult for the average person to keep the mind concentrated on a single object for any length of time.

verses.translation:
Holding the body, head and neck erect,
Motionless and steady,
Gazing at the tip of his own nose
And not looking in any direction,
verses.accessible: Holding the body, neck, and head upright, steady and motionless, the meditator should fix their gaze toward the tip of the nose without looking around in any direction.
notes: • This and the following stanza concern yoga techniques aimed at controlling the mind. The sitting position is, of course, the lotus position with legs intertwined and feet emerging behind the opposite knee.

verses.translation:
With quieted mind, banishing fear,
Established in the brahmacharin vow of celibacy,
Controlling the mind, with thoughts fixed on Me,
He should sit, concentrated, devoted to Me.
verses.accessible: With a calm mind, free from fear, committed to a life of purity, and with thoughts disciplined and focused on Me, the yogi should sit fully absorbed, cherishing Me as the ultimate goal.

verses.translation:
Thus, continually disciplining himself,
The yogin whose mind is subdued
Goes to nirvana, to supreme peace,
To union with Me.
verses.accessible: Continually training the mind in this way, the yogi whose thoughts are quieted attains supreme peace. They reach the freedom of spiritual liberation and enduring union with Me.

verses.translation:
Yoga is not eating too much,
Nor is it not eating at all,
And not the habit of sleeping too much,
And not keeping awake either, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Yoga is not for someone who eats too much, Arjuna, nor for someone who starves themselves. It is not for someone who sleeps too much, nor for someone who stays awake all night.
notes: • This statement, not dissimilar to the" middle way" of the Buddha, is among several references in the Bhagavad GItll to extreme practices on the part of some ascetics. The following stanza continues the idea.

verses.translation:
For him who is moderate in food and diversion,
Whose actions are disciplined,
Who is moderate in sleep and waking,
Yoga destroys all sorrow.
verses.accessible: For those who practice moderation in food and recreation, balance in their work and habits, and regularity in sleep and waking, yoga brings an end to all sorrow.

verses.translation:
When he is absorbed in the Self alone,
With controlled mind,
Free from longing, from all desires,
Then he is said to be a saint.
verses.accessible: When the well-disciplined mind rests completely in the true Self, free from all selfish cravings and attachments, a person is said to be truly united in yoga.

verses.translation:
As a lamp in a windless place
Does not flicker, to such is compared
The yogin of controlled mind,
Performing the yoga of the Self.
verses.accessible: Just as a lamp does not flicker when placed in a windless room, so remains the steady, focused mind of a yogi meditating on the true Self.

verses.translation:
When the mind comes to rest,
Restrained by the practice of yoga,
And when beholding the Self, by the self,
He is content in the Self,
verses.accessible: When the mind becomes completely still through the regular practice of yoga, a person directly experiences the true Self within and finds complete contentment in that Self.

verses.translation:
He knows that infinite happiness
Which is grasped by the intellect and transcends the senses,
And, established there,
Does not deviate from the truth.
verses.accessible: In that stillness, they discover the boundless joy that lies beyond sensory pleasures and can only be realized by a clear intellect. Once grounded there, they never drift from the truth.

verses.translation:
Having attained this,
No greater gain can he imagine;
Established in this,
He is not moved even by profound sorrow.
verses.accessible: Having attained this inner treasure, they realize there is no greater fulfillment to be found. Firmly anchored here, they cannot be shaken even by the deepest sorrow.

verses.translation:
Let this, the dissolution of union with pain,
Be known as yoga; this yoga
Is to be practiced with determination
And with an undismayed mind.
verses.accessible: Understand this complete freedom from the grip of suffering to be the true meaning of yoga. This yoga should be practiced with unwavering determination and a courageous heart.

verses.translation:
Abandoning those desires whose origins lie in one’s intention,
All of them, without exception,
And completely restraining
The multitude of senses with the mind,
verses.accessible: One should completely let go of all cravings born of selfish imagination without exception. Using the disciplined mind, one must gently rein in the senses from every direction.

verses.translation:
Little by little, he should come to rest,
With the intellect firmly held.
His mind having been established in the Self,
He should not think of anything.
verses.accessible: Step by step, one should guide the mind to peace through a patient intellect and steady resolve. Keeping the attention focused entirely on the true Self, one should not think of anything else.

verses.translation:
Whenever the unsteady mind,
Moving to and fro, wanders away,
He should restrain it
And control it in the Self.
verses.accessible: Whenever the restless, unsteady mind wanders off to chase its distractions, gently pull it back and return its focus to the true Self.

verses.translation:
The yogin whose mind is peaceful,
Whose passions are calmed,
Who is free of evil and has become one with Brahman,
Attains the highest bliss.
verses.accessible: Supreme joy naturally comes to the yogi whose mind is quiet and whose turbulent passions are calmed. Free from negativity, they become one with the Divine.

verses.translation:
Thus constantly disciplining himself,
The yogin, freed from evil,
Easily encountering Brahman,
Attains happiness beyond end.
verses.accessible: By consistently training the self in this way, the yogi, cleansed of all inner impurities, effortlessly experiences the presence of the Divine and attains boundless happiness.

verses.translation:
He who is disciplined by yoga sees
The Self present in all beings,
And all beings present in the Self.
He sees the same (Self) at all times.
verses.accessible: Those disciplined in yoga see the same divine presence everywhere. They see the true Self dwelling within all living creatures, and all living creatures resting within that Self.
notes: • Samadarsana has a special meaning which the words "seeing the same" scarcely convey. The iitmalls, or selves, of all creatures are conceived to be the same once they have been separated from the material nature with which they are temporarily conjoined in life. "A person who has brought his iitman into Yoga, will see similarity in all iitmans when separated from prakrti (material nature); he will see that all beings are in his own iitman; in other words he will see that his own iitman has the same ferm as the iitmalls of all other beings and contrariwise, so that he has seen all that is iitman when he has seen one iitman." - Ramanuja.

verses.translation:
He who sees Me everywhere,
And sees all things in Me;
I am not lost to him,
And he is not lost to Me.
verses.accessible: Whoever sees Me everywhere and sees all things in Me is never separated from Me, and I am never separated from them.
notes: • Krishna (the Supreme Spirit) is here equating himself with the atman.

verses.translation:
The yogin who, established in oneness,
Honors Me as abiding in all beings,
In whatever way he otherwise acts,
Dwells in Me.
verses.accessible: The yogi who is rooted in oneness and honors Me residing in every being lives and moves in Me, no matter what outward circumstances they may face.
notes: • I.e. who recognizes that all iitmans are one, and all pervaded by the Supreme Spirit.

verses.translation:
He who sees equality in everything
In the image of his own Self, Arjuna,
Whether in pleasure or in pain,
Is thought to be a supreme yogin.
verses.accessible: The highest yogi, Arjuna, is the one who looks upon all beings as equal to themselves, feeling another person's joy or sorrow as if it were their own.
notes: • It is perhaps amusing to note the etymology of the words" sukha" (pleasure, comfort, bliss) and "dul;kha" (misery, unhappiness, pain). The ancient Aryans who brought the Sanskrit language to India were a nomadic, horseand cattle-breeding people who travelled in horseor ox-drawn vehicles. "Su" and "dus" are prefixes indicating good or bad. The word" kha," in later Sanskrit meaning " sky," "ether," or "space," was originally the word for "hole," particularly an axle hole of one of the Aryan's vehicles. Thus .. sukha" (a BV cpd.) meant, originally, .. having a good axle hole," while" dul;kha" meant" having a poor axle hole," leading to discomfort. t I.e. that pleasure and pain in others is the same as pleasure and pain in himself, since the selves of all beings are equal to his own self, or identical with it.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
This yoga which is declared by You
As evenness of mind, Krishna,
I do not perceive
The steady continuance of this because of (the mind’s) instability.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'Krishna, You describe yoga as a state of lasting balance and inner peace. But because the mind is so restless and unstable, I cannot see how anyone can maintain it steadily.'

verses.translation:
The mind, indeed, is unstable, Krishna,
Turbulent, powerful and obstinate;
I think it is as difficult
To control as the wind.
verses.accessible: The mind is restless, turbulent, powerful, and stubborn, Krishna! Trying to master it feels as difficult as trying to hold back the blowing wind.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Without doubt, O Arjuna,
The mind is unsteady and difficult to restrain;
But by practice, Arjuna,
And by indifference to worldly objects, it is restrained.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'There is no doubt, Arjuna, that the mind is restless and difficult to tame. But through dedicated practice and learning to let go of cravings, it can certainly be mastered.'

verses.translation:
I agree that yoga is difficult to attain
By him whose self is uncontrolled; but
By him whose self is controlled,
By striving, it is possible to attain through proper means.
verses.accessible: Yoga is certainly hard to achieve for someone with an undisciplined mind. But for one who learns self-control and makes sincere effort using the right methods, success is entirely possible.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke;
One who is uncontrolled though he has faith,
Whose mind has fallen away from yoga,
Who does not attain perfection in yoga,
Which way, Krishna, does he go?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'Krishna, what happens to someone who has sincere faith but lacks strong self-discipline, so their mind wanders away from yoga before they can reach spiritual perfection?'

verses.translation:
Is he not lost like a disappearing cloud
Having fallen from both worlds,
Having no solid ground, O Krishna,
Confused on the path of Brahman?
verses.accessible: Do they not perish like a broken cloud dissolving in the sky—falling away from both worldly rewards and spiritual realization, left without a foundation and confused on the path to the Divine?
notes: " "Both worlds," viz. the here and the hereafter, earth and heaven. t This is one of two instances in the Bhagavad Citii where Krishna is addressed as "Mighty Armed," usually Arjuna's nickname. The other instance is in XI 23. The nickname is used throughout the Mahiibhiirata as a designation for eminent warriors.

verses.translation:
You are able, Krishna,
To dispel the totality of this doubt of mine;
Other than You, no one
Comes forth to help me erase this doubt.
verses.accessible: Please clear away this doubt of mine completely, Krishna, because there is no one else in all the worlds who can truly remove it.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Arjuna, neither here on earth nor in heaven above
Is there found to be destruction of him;
No one who does good
Goes to misfortune, My Son.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Arjuna, neither in this world nor in the hereafter is such a seeker ever lost. No one who strives to do good, My dear friend, ever meets a bad end.'
notes: '" I.e. the uncontrolled man who has arrived at faith but has fallen from Yoga.

verses.translation:
Attaining the worlds of the meritorious,
Having dwelt there for endless years,
He who has fallen from yoga is born again
In the dwelling of the radiant and the illustrious.
verses.accessible: After reaching the heavenly realms of the virtuous and living there happily for countless years, a person who fell short in yoga is reborn into a family of pure values and noble character.

verses.translation:
Or he may be born in the family
Of wise yogins;
Such a birth as this is very difficult
To attain in the world.
verses.accessible: Or they may even be born directly into a family of wise spiritual teachers, although such a birth in this world is exceedingly rare.

verses.translation:
There he regains the knowledge
Derived from a former body,
And he strives onward once more
Toward perfection, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: In that new life, they naturally regain the spiritual wisdom developed in their previous body. From that foundation, they strive onward once more toward perfection, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
He is carried on, even against his will,
By prior practice;
He who even wishes to know of yoga
Transcends Brahman in the form of sound (i.e. Vedic recitation).
verses.accessible: Drawn forward naturally by the habits of their past practice, they continue to grow. Indeed, anyone who genuinely yearns to understand yoga rises above mere rituals and empty recitation.

verses.translation:
Through persevering effort and controlled mind,
The yogin, completely cleansed of evil,
And perfected through many births,
Then goes to the supreme goal.
verses.accessible: Striving with determined effort, purified of inner impurities, and perfected across many lifetimes, the devoted yogi eventually reaches the supreme goal.

verses.translation:
The yogin is superior to the ascetics,
He is also thought to be superior to the learned,
And the yogin is superior to those who perform ritual works.
Therefore, be a yogin, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: A yogi is considered greater than an ascetic practicing severe self-denial, greater than a scholar of theory, and greater than those who perform rituals for rewards. Therefore, Arjuna, be a yogi!

verses.translation:
Of all these yogins,
He who has merged his inner Self in Me,
Honors Me, full of faith,
Is thought to be the most devoted to Me.
verses.accessible: And among all yogis, the one who meditates on Me with deep faith, their heart and inner self fully devoted to Me—that is the one I consider the most deeply united with Me in yoga.
notes: • I.e. whose mind is perpetually fixed on God, or the Supreme Spirit, through bhokti, or love.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
With mind absorbed in Me, Arjuna,
Practicing yoga, dependent on Me,
You shall know Me completely,
Without doubt; hear that!
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Listen, Arjuna, to how you can know Me completely and without any doubt, by focusing your mind on Me, taking refuge in Me, and practicing yoga.'

verses.translation:
To you I shall explain in full this knowledge,
Along with realization,
Which, having been understood, nothing further
Remains to be known here in the world.
verses.accessible: I will reveal this knowledge to you completely, along with its practical realization. Once you understand this, nothing else in this world remains to be known.

verses.translation:
Of thousands of men,
Scarcely anyone strives for perfection;
Even of the striving and the perfected,
Scarcely anyone knows Me in truth.
verses.accessible: Among thousands of people, hardly anyone strives for spiritual perfection. And even among those who strive and achieve success, rare is the person who truly knows Me as I am.

verses.translation:
Earth, water, fire, air,
Ether, mind, intellect
And egoism this,
My material nature, is divided into eight parts.
verses.accessible: My material nature is divided into eight elements: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego.
notes: • These are Siimkhya categories.

verses.translation:
Such is My inferior nature,
But know it as different from
My highest nature, the Self, O Arjuna,
By which this universe is sustained.
verses.accessible: This is My lower, material nature. But know, Arjuna, that I have a higher, spiritual nature—the life-force of conscious beings—that sustains this entire universe.
notes: • God has two prahrtis, a lower and a higher one. The lower one is the prahrti of this world consisting of endless various objects, means and occasions of material experience and divided into eight categories" (see stanza 4) ... "God's higher prahrti, however, is not of the same order of this non-spiritual prahrti which solely consists of the objects experienced by the spiritual beings, but is constituted by the spiritual beings themselves, the jivas." - Ramanuja.

verses.translation:
All creatures have their birth in this, My highest nature.
Understand this!
I am the origin and also the dissolution
Of the entire universe.
verses.accessible: Understand that all living beings arise from these two natures of Mine. I am both the source from which the entire universe originates and the resting place into which it dissolves.

verses.translation:
Nothing higher than Me exists,
O Arjuna.
On Me all this universe is strung
Like pearls on a thread.
verses.accessible: There is nothing higher than Me, Arjuna. The entire universe is strung on Me like pearls on a thread.

verses.translation:
I am the liquidity in the waters, Arjuna,
I am the radiance in the moon and sun,
The sacred syllable (Om) in all the Vedas,
The sound in the air, and the manhood in men.
verses.accessible: I am the taste in water, Arjuna, the radiance in the sun and moon, the sacred syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and the strength and courage in human beings.
notes: • "That which contains the rabbit" (SaSin), along with sasiiilka (rabbit marked) one of the most common of all Sanskrit terms for the moon, said to arise because the Hindus saw a "rabbit in the moon."

verses.translation:
I am the pure fragrance in the earth,
And the brilliance in the fire,
The life in all beings,
And the austerity in ascetics.
verses.accessible: I am the pure fragrance of the earth, the brilliant heat of fire, the life-force in all living creatures, and the inner discipline of spiritual seekers.
Know Me, Arjuna, as the eternal seed of all living beings. I am the intelligence of the wise and the brilliance of the glorious.

verses.translation:
And the might of the mighty I am,
Which is freed from lust and passion,
And I am that desire in beings
Which is according to law, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: I am the strength of the strong, free from selfish craving and passion. And in all living beings, Arjuna, I am the desire that aligns with moral duty.

verses.translation:
And those states of being which are sattvic,
And those which are rajasic and tamasic,
Know that they proceed from Me.
But I am not in them; they are in Me.
verses.accessible: Know that all states of being—whether characterized by harmony and goodness, passion and restlessness, or ignorance and dullness—proceed from Me. Yet I am not controlled by them; they exist within Me.
notes: .. All these entities with their peculiar individuality and characteristics have originated from God, are se$as (remainders) of God and depend on God inasmuch as they constitute his body, and God himself is modified by all these entities of which He is the iilman. These entities which are of the nature of sattva, rajas and lamas and which exist in this world in the form of body, senses, material objects and their causes, depend on God whose body they constitute. God himself, however, does not depend on them. - Riimiinuja.

verses.translation:
All this universe is deluded by these three states of being,
Composed of the qualities.
It does not recognize Me,
Who am higher than these, and eternal.
verses.accessible: Deluded by these three qualities of material nature, the entire world fails to recognize Me, who stand far beyond them, changeless and eternal.

verses.translation:
Divine indeed is this illusion of Mine made up of the three qualities,
And difficult to penetrate;
Only those who resort to Me
Transcend this illusion.
verses.accessible: This divine illusion of Mine, woven from the three modes of nature, is difficult to pierce. But those who take refuge in Me cross beyond this illusion.

verses.translation:
Evil doers, lowest of men,
Deprived of knowledge by illusion,
Do not seek Me,
Attached as they are to a demoniacal existence.
verses.accessible: Wrongdoers and the foolish do not turn to Me. Their understanding has been stripped away by illusion, and they embrace a selfish, destructive way of life.

verses.translation:
Among benevolent men, four kinds worship Me, Arjuna:
The distressed, those who desire wealth,
Those who desire knowledge,
And the man of wisdom, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Four kinds of virtuous people turn to Me in devotion, Arjuna: the distressed who suffer, the seekers of worldly success, the curious who seek knowledge, and the wise who know the truth.
notes: • The common translation " desirous of wealth," which is favored by many native translators, is obviously so much at odds with the other teachings of the Bhagavad Gita, that it cannot be entertained by the thoughtful reader. Sri Krishna Prem has suggested that" artha " here refers to the paramiirtha, or highest spiritual knowledge. Ramanuja says that the expression arthiirthl (which is the nom. sg. of arthiirthin) refers to "those who aspire to acquire knowledge of the iitman as distinct fromprakrti," or material nature. The meaning of the last three catagories of "benevolent men" is further explained in the next book (VIII) from stanza 8 onward.

verses.translation:
Of them the man of wisdom, eternally steadfast,
Devoted to the One alone, is preeminent.
I am indeed exceedingly fond of the man of wisdom,
And he is fond of Me.
verses.accessible: Of these, the wise person is the foremost—constantly united with Me and dedicated with single-minded devotion. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise, and they are deeply dear to Me.

verses.translation:
All these are indeed noble,
But the man of wisdom is thought to be My very Self.
He, indeed, whose mind is steadfast,
Abides in Me, the supreme goal.
verses.accessible: All of these seekers are noble, but I consider the wise person to be My very Self. With a steady and devoted mind, they remain firmly centered in Me as the supreme goal.

verses.translation:
At the end of many births,
The man of wisdom resorts to Me,
Thinking “Vasudeva (Krishna) is all.”
Such a great soul is hard to find.
verses.accessible: After many lifetimes of spiritual seeking, the person of wisdom takes refuge in Me, realizing that the Divine is everything that exists. Such a great soul is extraordinarily rare.
notes: • Vasudeva, literally" the son of Vasudeva," or Krishna, whose father was a son of Sura, descendant of Yadu. At the birth of Vasudeva, the father, the gods sounded the heavenly drums, knowing that an avatiir of Vishnu (i.e. Krishna) was to be born into his family. Krishna was a brother of Kunti, mother of the three principal Pal).Qu princes (see chapter" The Setting of the Bhagavad Gita "). Here Krishna is identified with

verses.translation:
Men whose knowledge has been carried away
By these and those desires, resort to other gods,
Having recourse to this and that religious rite,
Constrained by their own material natures.
verses.accessible: Those whose wisdom is clouded by various selfish cravings turn to other deities, practicing specific rituals dictated by their own conditioned natures.

verses.translation:
Whoever desires to honor with belief
Whatever worshiped form,
On him I bestow
Immovable faith.
verses.accessible: Whatever form of divinity a devotee chooses to worship with faith, I steady their heart and make that faith firm.

verses.translation:
He, who, endowed with this faith,
Desires to propitiate that form,
Receives from it his desires
Because those desires are decreed by Me.
verses.accessible: Filled with that firm faith, they pray to that chosen form and receive what they desire. Yet in truth, it is I alone who grant those blessings.
notes: • All religions are subsumed here, and the speaking God explains that all worship, of whatever kind, goes to Him, and that all boons, begged from whatever gods, are granted by Him alone. The stanza is an instance of the strong monotheistic element in the Gltli, also of its religious tolerance.

verses.translation:
But temporary is the fruit
For those of small understanding.
To the gods the godworshipers go;
My worshippers come surely to Me.
verses.accessible: Yet the rewards gained by people of limited understanding are temporary. Those who worship the lesser gods go to those gods, but My devotees come directly to Me.

verses.translation:
Though I am unmanifest, the unintelligent
Think of Me as having manifestation,
Not knowing My higher being
Which is imperishable and unsurpassed.
verses.accessible: Those who lack deeper understanding believe that I, the unmanifest Divine, am merely a limited mortal being, unaware of My supreme, changeless, and boundless nature.
notes: * This stanza discusses idolatry, the worship of the God "fallen into manifestation," i.e. as a statue, or image, or as a human being, or even an animal or inanimate object.

verses.translation:
I am not manifest to all,
Being enveloped in yoga maya;
This deluded world does not recognize Me,
The birthless and imperishable.
verses.accessible: Veiled by My divine power of illusion, I am not visible to everyone. This bewildered world fails to recognize Me as unborn and imperishable.

verses.translation:
I know the departed beings
And the living, Arjuna,
And those who are yet to be;
But no one knows Me.
verses.accessible: I know all beings of the past, the present, and the future, Arjuna, but no one fully knows Me.

verses.translation:
Because of the arising of desire and hatred,
Because of the deluding (power) of the opposites, Arjuna,
All beings fall into delusion
At birth.
verses.accessible: From the very moment of birth, Arjuna, all creatures are swept into confusion by the conflict of opposites, driven by desire and aversion.

verses.translation:
But those in whom evil has come to an end,
Those men whose actions are pure;
They, liberated from the deluding power of the opposites,
Worship Me with firm vows.
verses.accessible: But those whose wrongful actions have come to an end, and whose lives are pure and virtuous, are freed from the delusion of opposites. They worship Me with unwavering resolve.

verses.translation:
Those who strive toward release from
Old age and death, depending on Me,
Know Brahman thoroughly,
As well as the Self and all action.
verses.accessible: Those who take refuge in Me and strive for freedom from old age and death come to know Brahman completely, along with the true nature of the inner self and the entirety of action.

verses.translation:
They who know Me as the Adhibhuta and the Adhidaiva,
As well as the chief of sacrifice,
They truly know Me with steadfast thought
Even at the hour of death.
verses.accessible: Those who know Me as the underlying reality of the physical world, the divine realm, and all sacrifice remain fully aware of Me with steady minds, even at the moment of death.
notes: • adhibhata (supreme being) and adhidiiiva (supreme god) are sometimes translated as "the penetrating influence of the Supreme Spirit" and "the divine agent operating on material objects" respectively. The two terms are further explained in the following chapter.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
What is this Brahman? What is the Adhyatma?
What is action, O highest among Spirits?
And the Adhibhuta, what is it declared to be?
And the Adhidaiva, what is it said to be?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'What is Brahman, and what is the inner self? What is action, O Supreme Person? What is said to be the physical world, and what is the divine realm?'

verses.translation:
In what manner, and what, is the Adhiyajna
Here in this body, O Krishna?
And how at the hour of death
Are You to be known by those who are self-controlled?
verses.accessible: Arjuna continued: 'And who is the Lord of sacrifice here within this body, and how does He dwell here, Krishna? How can those who have mastered themselves know You at the hour of death?'

Krishna said: 'Brahman is the supreme, imperishable reality, and its presence within the individual is called the inner self. The creative power that brings living beings into existence is called action.'
notes: • But Ramanuja says: "Karman (action) is the procreative act connected with a woman which causes a human being, etc., to originate. An aspirant to kiiiviilya (complete detachment of the iitman from material nature) should know that all this, and all that is connected with it, is to be feared and avoided." The point is debatable. Karma has many meanings.

verses.translation:
The Adhibhuta is the perishable nature of being (or the sphere of the supreme Spirit in acting on the individual, i.e. nature).
The Adhidaivata is the supreme divine Agent itself (the purusha).
The Adhiyajna (Lord of Sacrifice) is Myself,
Here in this body, O Arjuna.
verses.accessible: The physical world consists of perishable material creation, while the divine realm is the cosmic person, the supreme conscious spirit. And here within this physical body, Arjuna, I Myself am the Lord of all sacrifice.
notes: • All the terms here are technical and sometimes puzzling. Edgerton regards the language of these stanzas as grandiloquent. But native commentators take it very seriously, and some of their definiions are included here. Ramanuja identifies the Adhyiitman with svabhiiva (inherent disposition) or prakrti (material nature) - "that which is not the self, but is conjoined with the self." The Adhibhuta, according to him, is "the transitoriness of the elements, ether, etc., of which elements sound, touch, etc., are developments." The Adhidiiivata "connotes the purufa; it means' being beyond the pantheon of Indra, Prajapati, etc.' The Adhiyajiia is God- He who is to be propitiated by sacrifice."

verses.translation:
And at the hour of death, he who dies remembering Me,
Having relinquished the body,
Goes to My state of being.
In this matter there is no doubt.
verses.accessible: Whoever leaves their body at the time of death remembering Me alone enters directly into My divine nature. Of this there is no doubt.

verses.translation:
Moreover, whatever state of being he remembers
When he gives up the body at the end,
He goes respectively to that state of being, Arjuna,
Transformed into that state of being.
verses.accessible: Whatever state of being a person remembers when leaving the body at the end of life, to that state they will go, Arjuna, because their mind has been constantly shaped by that thought.

verses.translation:
Therefore, at all times
Meditate on Me,
With your mind and intellect fixed on Me.
In this way, you shall surely come to Me.
verses.accessible: Therefore, remember Me at all times and do your duty in battle. With your mind and intellect focused on Me, you will surely come to Me.

verses.translation:
With a mind disciplined by the practice of yoga,
Which does not turn to anything else,
To the divine supreme Spirit
He goes, Arjuna, meditating on Him.
verses.accessible: By disciplining the mind through regular yoga practice so that it does not wander toward anything else, one who meditates steadily on the supreme divine Spirit reaches Him, Arjuna.
notes: • According to Ramanuja's commentary, stanzas 8, 9 and 10 refer to the tiisvarytirthin (He who aims at superhuman power), who sees God in terms of God's power, and who" remains fixed on God as the result of daily practice of Yoga." He is the "desirous of knowledge" of VII I 6, where he is referred to as the jijfitisu.

verses.translation:
He who meditates on the ancient seer,
The ruler, smaller than the atom,
Who is the supporter of all, whose form is unthinkable,
And who is effulgent like the sun, beyond darkness;
verses.accessible: One should meditate on the Supreme as the all-knowing Seer, the timeless Ruler, subtler than the smallest particle, the sustainer of everything, whose form is beyond human imagination, shining like the sun far beyond all darkness.
notes: • Tri~!ubh metre. t "He will attain the aiivarya (power) which God himself possesses, when he has concentrated his pra!la (vital breath) between the brows and then, in virtue of his daily practiced worship, with his mind unwavering because all samskaras (preparatory reformations of the mind) have been passed, represents God to himself as the omniscient, primaeval Lord of the universe, the creator of all, subtler than the jfva (monad of the life principle), whose proper form is of another order than everything else and who is possessed of a divine form peculiar to none but Him."l{ilmanuja.

verses.translation:
At the hour of death, with unmoving mind,
Endowed with devotion and with the power of yoga,
Having made the vital breath enter between the two eyebrows,
He reaches this divine supreme Spirit.
verses.accessible: At the moment of death, with an unwavering mind, filled with devotion and the strength of yoga, centering the life-breath between the eyebrows, that seeker reaches the supreme divine Spirit.
notes: • Tri~!ubh metre continues. The last line is one syllable too long. t As in several such Yoga techniques, the anatomical elements arc vague to the non-yogin.

verses.translation:
That which those who know the Vedas call the imperishable,
Which the ascetics, free from passion, enter,
Desiring which they follow a life of chastity,
That path I shall explain to you briefly.
verses.accessible: I will briefly describe to you that supreme goal which scholars of sacred scripture call imperishable, into which detached seekers enter, and for the sake of which they live lives of dedicated self-restraint.
notes: • Tri~tubh metre continues.

verses.translation:
Closing all the gates of the body,
And confining the mind in the heart,
Having placed the vital breath in the head,
Established in yoga concentration,
verses.accessible: One should close all the senses of the body, hold the mind steadily within the heart, and raise the life-breath to the crown of the head through focused yoga concentration.
notes: • Sloka metre resumes. t Gates of the body, nine in number, viz. the two eyes, two nostrils, two ears, mouth, organ of generation, organ of excretion.

verses.translation:
Uttering the single-syllable “Om” Brahman
Meditating on Me,
He who goes forth, renouncing the body,
Goes to the supreme goal.
verses.accessible: Then, departing the body while chanting the sacred syllable Om—the sound of Brahman—and remembering Me, one reaches the supreme goal.
notes: .. According to Ramanuja's commentary, stanzas 12 and 13 refer to the kaivalyarthin (seeker of complete detachment) who seeks the complete severance of the atman from the body, and worships God as the ak~ara, or indestructible, eternal essence (Brahman). He is mentioned in VII 16, as the artharthin, or seeker of knowledge of the atman as different from prakrti, or material nature. This is the" Highest Truth" of VII 16.

verses.translation:
He who thinks of Me constantly,
Whose mind does not ever go elsewhere,
For him, the yogin who is constantly devoted,
I am easy to reach, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: For the yogi who remembers Me constantly with an undivided heart, never letting their mind wander elsewhere, I am easily reached, Arjuna.
notes: • According to Ramanuja's commentary, this and stanzas 15 and 16 are devoted to thejiilillin of VII 16, the" man of wisdom," who is never without direct concentration on God, "his mind focussed on God alone because God is incomparably dear to him, and because he cannot sustain his iitman without representing God (to himself). . .. And God himself, unable to endure separation from his worshipper, will choose him." According to the same source, the iiisvaryiirthin (stanza 8 et seq.) is reborn. But the kiiivalyiirthin (stanzas 12 and 13) and the jfiiinin, described in this and the following stanzas, are not reborn, but go to union with Brahman, or God.

verses.translation:
Approaching Me, those whose souls are great,
Who have gone to the supreme perfection,
Do not incur rebirth,
That impermanent home of misfortune.
verses.accessible: Having reached Me, those great souls who have attained supreme perfection are never reborn into this temporary world of sorrow.

verses.translation:
Up to Brahma’s realm of being,
The worlds are subject to successive rebirths, Arjuna;
But he who reaches Me
Is not reborn.
verses.accessible: Every realm in this universe, even the highest world of the creator Brahma, is subject to the cycle of rebirth, Arjuna. But whoever reaches Me will never be born again.

verses.translation:
They who know that the day of Brahma
Extends as far as a thousand yugas,
And that the night of Brahma ends only in a thousand yugas;
They are men who know day and night.
verses.accessible: Those who understand cosmic time know that a single day of the creator Brahma lasts for a thousand cosmic ages, and his night lasts just as long. They truly comprehend the nature of day and night.
notes: .. yuga, an "age" of the world, which is a division of a mahayuga, or period of 4,320,000 years. There are four yugas: the krtayuga, or golden age, which lasts for 1,728,000 years and is named for the side of the die marked with four dots. The treta yuga, which lasts for 1,296,000 years, which is less virtuous and is named for the side of the die with three dots; the dvapara yuga, which lasts for 864,000 years, represents a growing predominance of evil over good and is named for the side of the die marked with two dots; and the kali yuga, or dark age, which lasts for 432,000 years, is a period of predominant evil and is named for the side of the die marked with a single dot. It takes a thousand mahayugas, or 4,320,000,000 years, to make a kalpa, or one day of Brahmli, an equal number to make one night of Brahmii. We are, as this volume goes to press, in the 5,079th year of a kali yuga that began on February 18, 3102

verses.translation:
From the unmanifest, all manifestations
Come forth at the arrival of (Brahma’s) day;
At the arrival of (Brahma’s) night, they are dissolved,
At that point to be known as the unmanifest again.
verses.accessible: At the dawn of Brahma’s cosmic day, all living beings emerge from the unmanifest realm. When his night falls, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest state.

verses.translation:
This multitude of beings,
Having come to be again and again, is dissolved
Helplessly at the arrival of night, Arjuna,
And it comes into existence again at the arrival of day.
verses.accessible: This vast multitude of beings is born again and again, dissolving helplessly when cosmic night arrives, only to arise once more at the break of day.
notes: • This and the previous stanza describe the periodic creation of all beings and their subsequent dissolution. The" night of Brahma" which lasts for a kalpa (4,320,000,000 years, see footnote to VIII 17), and during this time all life is in latent, "unmanifest" form. At the arrival of the "day of Brahma," all beings, animal, vegetable and mineral, are created again, to go through their much smaller lives and reincarnations, all of which end at the recurrence of the" night of Brahma," when they pass into the unmanifest again. The day of Brahma is equal in length to the night of Brahma.

verses.translation:
But higher than this state of being
Is another unmanifest state of being
Higher than the primeval unmanifest,
Which, when all beings perish, does not perish.
verses.accessible: Yet beyond this changing unmanifest state lies another unmanifest reality—eternal and timeless. Even when all living beings and universes perish, that reality never perishes.

verses.translation:
This unmanifest is the imperishable, thus it is said.
They call it the supreme goal,
Attaining which, they do not return.
This is My supreme dwelling place.
verses.accessible: This eternal unmanifest realm is called the imperishable, and it is known as the supreme destination. Those who reach it never return; that is My highest abode.

verses.translation:
This is the supreme Spirit, Arjuna,
Attainable by one-pointed devotion,
Within which all beings stand,
And by which all this universe is pervaded.
verses.accessible: That supreme Spirit, Arjuna, is attained through wholehearted devotion. All living beings dwell within Him, and by Him the entire universe is pervaded.

verses.translation:
But at which times the yogins
Return or do not return,
As they depart at death,
Of these times I shall speak, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Now listen, Arjuna, as I describe the times and paths of departure at death, following which yogis either return to this world or achieve liberation without return.

verses.translation:
Fire, brightness, day, the bright lunar fortnight,
‘The six months of the northern course of the sun:
Departing then, the men who know Brahman
Go forth to Brahman.
verses.accessible: Marked by fire, daylight, the waxing moon, and the six months when the sun travels northward—departing along this path of light, those who know Brahman attain the ultimate reality.
notes: " This and the following stanzas present a formula to be found in the Chandogya Upanishad, V 9, I to 5, and in the BrhadaraQyaka Upanishad, VI 2, 15 and 16. There is also a shorter reference in Chandyoga IV 15, 5, which does not mention the" dark" path. In the BrhadaraQyaka Upanishad, the distinction between those who follow the path of light and those who follow the path of darkness lies not only in the time of death but also between those who meditate on the "five fires" (viz. Heaven, the Rain god, the World, Man and Woman) and those who merelY perform rituals, the latter going the path of darkness and rebirth. t "upper going" means northern because the north of India is higher than the south.

verses.translation:
Smoke, night, the dark lunar fortnight,
The six months of the southern course of the sun;
Attaining by these the lunar light,
The yogin is born again.
verses.accessible: Marked by smoke, nighttime, the waning moon, and the six months when the sun travels southward—departing along this path of darkness, the yogi reaches the lunar realm and must return to rebirth.
notes: • When identifying directions, the Hindu faces east where the sun rises. Thus" right hand" means south.

verses.translation:
These are the two paths, light and dark,
Thought to be eternal for the universe.
By one he does not return;
By the other he returns again.
verses.accessible: These two paths—one of light and one of darkness—are considered eternal in this world. Following the path of light, one never returns; following the path of darkness, one is reborn again.
notes: ... The choice of whether to return or not is apparently up to the yogin. The literature abounds with yogins who have delayed their deaths so as to reach the half-year that will eventuate in either return or non-return. (Cf. the case of Bhi~ma, who delayed his death at the Battle of Kuruk~etra see chapter" The Setting of the Bhagavad GitiL)" The existence of the "two paths" (light and dark) must seem rather arbitrary to the Western reader. Ramanuja refers them to the jiiiinin and kiiivalyiirthin of VII 16 on the one hand, and the iiiivarYiirthin of the same stanza on the other. But this does not explain the element of free will which allows the yogin to fix the time of his death and choose between the two paths.

verses.translation:
Knowing these two paths
The yogin is not confused at all.
Therefore, at all times,
Be steadfast in yoga, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Knowing these two paths, Arjuna, a dedicated yogi is never confused or led astray. Therefore, remain steadfast in your practice of yoga at all times.

verses.translation:
The yogin, having known all this, goes beyond
The pure fruit of action which comes from study of the Vedas,
Sacrifices, austerities, and gifts,
And goes to the supreme primal state.
verses.accessible: The yogi who grasps this truth rises beyond all the spiritual merits gained from studying sacred scriptures, performing rituals, practicing austerities, or giving charity, and reaches the supreme, eternal home.
notes: • Tri${ubh metre.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
But this most secret thing
I shall declare to you, who do not disbelieve:
Knowledge and realization combined,
Having learned which you shall be released from evil.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Because you have an open heart and do not doubt Me, I will now reveal to you this most profound, secret wisdom—knowledge paired with direct realization. Once you understand this, you will be freed from all worldly suffering.'
notes: • Sioha metre resumes.

verses.translation:
This is royal knowledge, a royal secret,
A supreme purifier,
Plainly intelligible, righteous,
Easy to practice, imperishable.
verses.accessible: This is royal knowledge, the king of secrets, and the greatest purifier. It can be directly experienced, it aligns with universal truth, it is joyful and easy to practice, and its value never fades.

verses.translation:
Men who have no faith
In this knowledge, Arjuna,
Not attaining to Me, are born again
In the path of death and transmigration.
verses.accessible: Those who have no faith in this spiritual truth, Arjuna, fail to reach Me. They remain trapped in the endless cycle of death and rebirth.

verses.translation:
This whole universe is pervaded
By Me in My unmanifest aspect.
All beings abide in Me;
I do not abide in them.
verses.accessible: In My unmanifest form, I pervade this entire universe. All living beings exist within Me, yet I am not contained within them.

verses.translation:
And yet beings do not abide in Me.
Behold my divine yoga!
Sustaining beings and not dwelling in beings
Is my Self, causing beings to be.
verses.accessible: And at the same time, created beings do not restrict Me—behold My divine mystery! My Spirit creates and sustains all living beings, yet remains completely independent of them.
notes: • The explanation of the apparent paradox follows: "God is the source of all phenomena, but is not touched by them" - Radhakrishnan. t "God pervades beings by virtue of his will ... God supports all beings, but no being is of use to him." freely excerpted from Ramanuja.

verses.translation:
As the mighty wind, going everywhere,
Dwells eternally in space,
So all beings
Dwell in Me. Consider this!
verses.accessible: Just as the mighty wind blows everywhere but always rests within vast space, understand that in the same way, all beings dwell within Me.

verses.translation:
All beings, Arjuna,
Go to My own material nature
At the end of a kalpa;
At the beginning of a kalpa, I send them forth.
verses.accessible: At the end of a cosmic cycle, Arjuna, all creatures merge back into My material nature. Then, at the dawn of a new cycle, I send them forth once again.
notes: • Day of Brahman, see Book VIII 17, note (i.e. 4,320,000,000 years).

verses.translation:
Resting on My own material nature,
I send forth again and again
This entire multitude of beings,
Which is powerless, by the power of My material nature.
verses.accessible: Mastering My own material nature, I project this multitude of beings over and over, all moving helplessly under the forces of nature.
notes: • God creates these beings anew (at the beginning of a new kalpa), reposing upon his own prakrti (material nature), which is capable of development into various shapes. God creates the fourfold creation of gods, men, animals and immovables every now and then because of his bewildering prakrti which consists of gu'.las. He develops this prakrti into eight forms (cf. VII 4 and following stanza). - Rlimlinuja.

verses.translation:
And these actions do not bind Me,
Arjuna;
I sit indifferently,
Unattached to these actions.
verses.accessible: Yet none of these actions bind Me, Arjuna. I remain unattached, watching over creation with calm impartiality.

verses.translation:
With Me as overseer, material nature
Produces all things animate and inanimate.
From this cause, Arjuna,
The universe revolves.
verses.accessible: Under My watchful eye, nature gives birth to everything that moves and everything that is still. Because of this, Arjuna, the wheel of the universe keeps turning.

verses.translation:
The deluded despise Me,
Clad in human form,
Not knowing My higher being
As the great Lord of beings.
verses.accessible: Foolish people look down on Me when I appear in human form, completely unaware of My higher nature as the Supreme Lord of all life.

verses.translation:
Those of vain hopes, vain actions,
Vain knowledge, devoid of discrimination,
Abide in a fiendish and demoniacal nature,
Which is deluding.
verses.accessible: Trapped by confusion, their hopes are futile, their actions meaningless, and their knowledge shallow. Lacking wisdom, they adopt a selfish, cruel, and deceptive nature that only leads them further astray.
notes: • prakrtim (nature) is not used here in the usual sense of" material nature," but is part of a simple attribute.

verses.translation:
But those whose souls are great, Arjuna,
Partaking of a celestial nature,
Worship Me single-mindedly,
Knowing Me as the origin of beings and as the imperishable.
verses.accessible: Great souls, however, rest in their divine nature, Arjuna. They worship Me with single-minded devotion, knowing Me as the imperishable source of everything that exists.

verses.translation:
Perpetually glorifying Me
And striving with firm vows,
And honoring Me with devotion,
Ever steadfast, they worship Me.
verses.accessible: Always praising Me, striving with firm resolve, and bowing before Me with deep love and devotion, they stay constantly connected to Me in worship.

verses.translation:
And by the wisdom sacrifice,
Others, sacrificing, worship Me
As the one and as the manifold,
Variously manifested, facing in all directions (i.e. omniscient).
verses.accessible: Others worship Me through the offering of wisdom. They see Me as the One, as the many diverse forms in creation, and as the infinite Presence facing everywhere.

verses.translation:
I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice,
I am the offering, I am the medicinal herb,
I am the sacred text, I am also the clarified butter,
I am the fire, and I am the pouring out (of the oblation).
verses.accessible: I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice, and I am the offering made to the ancestors. I am the healing herb, the sacred chant, the clarified butter, the holy fire, and the offering poured into the flames.

verses.translation:
I am the father of the universe,
The mother, the establisher, the grandfather,
The object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable “Om,”
The Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
verses.accessible: I am the father of this world, the mother, the sustainer, and the ancestor of all. I am the truth to be known, the sacred purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
notes: • The ~g, Sarna and Yajur Vedas are the three principal Vedas, or compilations of ancient Vedic lore, the first being devoted to verses of praise, the second to the traditions of chant applied largely to the same verses, and the third to ritual formulas.

verses.translation:
I am the goal, the supporter, the great Lord, the witness,
The abode, the refuge, the friend,
The origin, the dissolution and the foundation,
The treasure house and the imperishable seed.
verses.accessible: I am the ultimate goal, the sustainer, the master, the silent witness, the true home, the refuge, and the dearest friend. I am the beginning, the end, the foundation, the resting place, and the eternal seed.

verses.translation:
I radiate heat, I withhold and
Send forth the rain;
And I am both immortality and death,
Being and non-being, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: I give off heat as the sun, and I hold back and release the rain. I am immortality and I am death; I am that which exists and that which does not, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Those who know the three Vedas, the soma drinkers, those whose evils are cleansed,
Worship Me with sacrifices and seek to go to heaven.
They, attaining the pure world of the Lord of the gods,
Enjoy in heaven the gods’ celestial pleasures.
verses.accessible: Those who follow the rituals of the three Vedas, purifying themselves and offering sacrifices, pray for a place in heaven. Reaching the realm of Indra, king of the gods, they enjoy celestial pleasures and divine delights.
notes: .. Tri~!ubh metre. t This is the only mention in the Gita of the chief of the Vedic gods, Indra, though the surviving mutation of his name in the word" indriya" meaning" sense" or "power" is common, and he is mentioned in X 22, by another name. The use of the name here is in its common meaning, "chief" thus the Indra or "chief" of the gods.

verses.translation:
Having enjoyed the vast world of heaven,
They enter the world of mortals when their merit is exhausted.
Thus conforming to the law of the three Vedas,
Desiring enjoyments, they obtain the state of going and returning.
verses.accessible: After enjoying the vast heavenly realm, they return to the mortal world once their earned spiritual merit runs out. By following ritual rules driven by selfish desires, they only earn endless coming and going.
notes: Tri~!ubh

verses.translation:
Those men who worship, directing their thoughts to Me,
Whose minds do not go elsewhere;
For them, who are constantly steadfast,
I secure what they lack and preserve what they already possess.
verses.accessible: But for those who worship Me with undivided devotion, keeping Me always in their hearts, I personally provide what they need and protect what they have.
notes: • 8loka metre resumes.

verses.translation:
Even those who worship other gods
With faith,
Also worship Me, Arjuna,
Though they do so in ignorance.
verses.accessible: Even those who worship other deities with sincere faith are really worshiping Me, Arjuna, even if they do not follow the direct path.

verses.translation:
For I am the enjoyer and the Lord
Of all sacrifices.
But they do not recognize Me in truth;
Hence they fall.
verses.accessible: I am the recipient and the master of all sacrifices and worship. But because they do not recognize My true divine nature, they fall back into the cycle of rebirth.
Those who dedicate themselves to the gods go to the gods; those who honor the ancestors go to the ancestors; those who worship spirits go to the spirits; but those who worship Me come directly to Me.

verses.translation:
He who offers to Me with devotion and a pure heart
A leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water,
That offering of devotion
I accept from him.
verses.accessible: Whoever offers Me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or even a cup of water with genuine love and a pure heart, I gratefully accept that humble gift of devotion.
notes: • "I eat." The ancient belief was that the gods actually" ate" part of the sacrificial offering.

verses.translation:
Whatever you do, whatever you eat,
Whatever you offer, whatever you give,
Whatever austerities you perform, Arjuna,
Do that as an offering to Me.
verses.accessible: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give away, and whatever self-discipline you practice, Arjuna, dedicate it all as an offering to Me.

verses.translation:
You shall certainly be liberated
From the bonds of action which produce good and evil fruits;
Liberated, with your mind disciplined by the yoga of renunciation,
You shall come to Me.
verses.accessible: In this way, you will be freed from the chains of action and its pleasant or painful results. With your mind anchored in this spirit of selfless offering, you will be liberated and come to Me.

verses.translation:
I am the same (Self) in all beings;
There is none disliked or dear to Me.
But they who worship Me with devotion
Are in Me, and I am also in them.
verses.accessible: I look upon all beings with equal love; no one is hated by Me, and no one is favored over another. Yet those who turn to Me with heartfelt devotion live in Me, and I live in them.
notes: • "Being a refuge for all, God is the same toward all iitmans (selves) of gods, men, animals and immovables, which, according to their class, configuration, nature and knowledge, exist in an infinite plurality of forms." - Ramanuja. The meaning is that God exists in all iitmans (selves) and is therefore a part, equal in quantity, of all beings, thus "the same" in all beings.

verses.translation:
If even the evil doer
Worships Me with undivided devotion,
He is to be thought of as righteous,
For he has indeed rightly resolved.
verses.accessible: Even if someone who has lived a terrible life turns to Me with wholehearted devotion, that person should be regarded as good, for they have made the right resolve.

verses.translation:
Quickly he becomes virtuous and
Goes to everlasting peace.
Arjuna, know for certain that
No devotee of Mine is ever lost
verses.accessible: Very quickly their mind becomes pure and they find lasting peace. Proclaim it boldly, Arjuna: no one who loves Me is ever lost!

verses.translation:
They who take refuge in Me, Arjuna,
Even if they are born of those whose wombs are evil (i.e. those of low origin),
Women, Vaishyas, even Shudras,
Also go to the highest goal.
verses.accessible: Whoever takes refuge in Me, Arjuna—even those born into humble circumstances or looked down upon by society, whether women, merchants, or laborers—they all reach the highest spiritual goal.
notes: • viiisyiis members of the merchant or peasant caste, third in order of rank. t sudriis members of the servant caste, fourth in order of rank and lowest of the four original castes.

verses.translation:
How much more easily then, the pure Brahmins
And the devoted royal seers!
Having attained this impermanent and unhappy world,
Devote yourself to Me.
