verses.accessible: How much more certain, then, is the goal for devoted spiritual seekers and noble leaders! Having found yourself in this fleeting, sorrowful world, dedicate your heart to Me.

verses.translation:
With mind fixed on Me, be devoted to Me;
Sacrificing to Me, make reverence to Me.
Thus steadfast, with Me as your supreme aim,
You yourself shall come to Me.
verses.accessible: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, and bow before Me. Uniting yourself with Me and making Me your highest aim, you will surely come to Me.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Again, O Arjuna,
Hear My supreme word
Which I shall speak to you, who are beloved,
With a desire for your welfare.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Listen once again, mighty Arjuna, to My supreme message. Because you are so dear to Me, I share this with you for your highest good.'

verses.translation:
Neither the multitude of gods
Nor the great seers know My origin.
In truth I am the source of the gods
And the great seers.
verses.accessible: Neither the host of gods nor the great sages know My origin, because I am the ultimate source from which all gods and sages come.

verses.translation:
He who knows Me, the birthless and the beginningless,
The mighty Lord of the world,
He among mortals is undeluded;
He is released from all evils.
verses.accessible: Whoever knows Me as unborn, without beginning, and the supreme ruler of all worlds, is freed from confusion and released from all wrongdoing.

verses.translation:
Intellect, knowledge, freedom from delusion,
Patience, truth, self-restraint, tranquility,
Pleasure, pain, birth, death,
And fear and fearlessness,
verses.accessible: Clear intellect, knowledge, freedom from doubt, forgiveness, truthfulness, self-control, peace of mind, joy and sorrow, birth and death, fear and courage—

verses.translation:
Non-violence, impartiality, contentment,
Austerity, charity, fame, disrepute,
The manifold conditions of beings,
Arise from Me alone.
verses.accessible: nonviolence, balance, contentment, self-discipline, generosity, fame, and dishonor—all these diverse qualities of living beings arise from Me alone.

verses.translation:
The seven great seers of old,
And also the four Manus,
From whom have sprung these creatures of the world,
Originated from Me, born of My mind.
verses.accessible: The seven great ancient sages and the four ancestral Manus were born from My mind and share My essence. From them, all the generations of people in this world have descended.
notes: II Seven legendary seers (r#s) - Kasyapa, Atri, Vasi~tha, Visvamitra, Gotama, Jamadagni and Bharadvaja sometimes identified with the seven stars of the Lesser Bear constellation, sometimes with other heavenly bodies. For Kasyapa see chapter" The Setting of the Bhagavad Gita." t Manus seem to come in various quantities. Fourteen are commonly listed. All are purely legendary figures. One, Manu Vaivasvata, is supposed to have been the great Hindu lawgiver, author of the post-Vedic Miinava dharmasiistra, and progenitor of the human race.

verses.translation:
He who knows in truth
This, My manifested glory and power,
Is united with Me by unwavering yoga;
Of this there is no doubt.
verses.accessible: Anyone who truly understands this divine glory and power of Mine is united with Me through unwavering yoga. Of this, there is no doubt.

verses.translation:
I am the origin of all;
All proceeds from Me.
Thinking thus, the intelligent ones,
Worship Me.
verses.accessible: I am the source of everything; from Me all creation flows. Understanding this truth, wise people worship Me with hearts full of devotion.

verses.translation:
Those who think of Me, who absorb their lives in Me,
Enlightening each other,
And speaking of Me con stantly,
They are content and rejoice.
verses.accessible: With their minds centered on Me and their lives devoted to Me, they enlighten one another and constantly speak of Me, finding deep contentment and joy.

verses.translation:
To those who are constantly steadfast,
Those who worship Me with love,
I give the yoga of discrimination
By which they come to Me.
verses.accessible: To those who are ever steadfast and worship Me with love, I give the intuitive wisdom by which they can come directly to Me.

verses.translation:
Out of compassion for them,
I, who dwell within their own beings,
Destroy the darkness born of ignorance
With the shining lamp of knowledge.
verses.accessible: Out of pure compassion for them, I dwell within their hearts and destroy the darkness of ignorance with the shining lamp of wisdom.
notes: • This phrase has been variously translated. Edgerton makes it "while remaining in my own true state," and some others follow him. I prefer the present translation.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode,
The supreme purifier,
The eternal divine Spirit,
The primal God, unborn and all-pervading.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'You are the supreme reality, the ultimate home, and the purest light. You are the eternal divine Spirit, the original God, unborn and all-pervading.'

verses.translation:
Thus they call You, all the seers,
The divine seer Narada,
Also Asita, Devala, and Vyasa,
And You Yourself (now) tell me so.
verses.accessible: All the ancient seers have declared this about You—including the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa—and now You have told me so Yourself.
notes: • Narada, a legendary seer to whom some of the verses of the Bg Veda are ascribed. t Asita Devala, legendary composer of some other hymns of the Bg Veda. t Vyasa, legendary compiler of the Vedas and the Mahabharata. The name means "arranger," "compiler," or "divider."

verses.translation:
All this which You speak to me, Krishna,
I believe to be true;
Indeed, neither the gods nor the demons, O Blessed one,
Know Your manifestation.
verses.accessible: I believe that everything You tell me is completely true, Krishna. Neither the gods nor the demons fully comprehend Your divine mystery.

verses.translation:
Supreme Being, O Lord of the universe, You know Yourself through Yourself alone,
Highest of spirits,
Source of welfare of beings, Lord of beings,
God of gods, O Lord of the universe.
verses.accessible: You alone know Yourself through Your own power, Supreme Being, creator and master of all life, God of all gods, Lord of the universe!

verses.translation:
Please describe without reserve
The divine self-manifestations
By which You pervade
These worlds, and abide in them.
verses.accessible: Please tell me, without holding anything back, about the divine manifestations through which You fill and sustain all these worlds.

verses.translation:
How may I know You, O Yogin,
Constantly meditating on You?
And in what various aspects of being
Are You to be thought of by me, O Blessed One?
verses.accessible: How can I know You, great Master, as I meditate on You constantly? In what specific aspects of creation should I think of You, Blessed Lord?

verses.translation:
Explain to me further in detail
Your power and manifestation, O Krishna.
I am never satiated with hearing
Your nectar-like words.
verses.accessible: Describe Your divine powers and manifestations in detail once more, Krishna. I can never hear enough of Your words—they are like sweet nectar to me.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Listen! I shall explain to you
My divine self-manifestations;
Those only that are prominent,
For there is no end to My extent.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Yes, I will describe My divine manifestations to you, Arjuna, focusing on the most prominent ones—for there is no end to My infinite extent.'

verses.translation:
I am the Self, Arjuna,
Abiding in the heart of all beings;
And I am the beginning and the middle
Of beings, and the end as well.
verses.accessible: I am the true Self, Arjuna, living within the heart of every single creature. I am their beginning, their middle, and their end.
Among the solar deities, I am Vishnu; among radiant lights, I am the glowing sun; among the wind spirits, I am Marichi; and among the night lights of the sky, I am the moon.
notes: • The Adityas, originally seven, later twelve in number, were a group of supreme gods. t Marlci was the chief of the Maruts or storm gods. t Maruts were the storm gods who helped Indra slay the cosmic dragon, in order to bring water to the world.

verses.accessible: Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda of sacred song; among the gods, I am Indra; among the senses, I am the mind; and in living beings, I am consciousness itself.
notes: • The Veda concerned with chants. t One of the names of Indra, the chief Vedic god, mentioned by his usual name only in IX 20.

verses.accessible: Among the Rudras, I am Shiva; among nature spirits and guardians, I am Kubera, lord of wealth; among the elemental Vasus, I am fire; and among mountain peaks, I am Mount Meru.
notes: • Rudras, or" roarers," storm gods and gods of destruction and renewal. t Sarilkara, Shiva, god of fertility and destruction. t Vittesa, otherwise known as Kubera, lord of wealth. § Yak~as and Rak~as, spirits of vague character, sometimes hostile and sometimes benevolent. II Pavaka, one of the names of Agni, the Vedic god of fire. The word means "purifier." , Vas us, a group of eight" bright" gods, •• Mt. Meru was the Olympos of Hindu mythology.

verses.accessible: Know Me as Brihaspati, the chief of spiritual teachers; among military leaders, I am Skanda, general of the divine army; and among bodies of water, I am the boundless ocean.
notes: .. Skanda, the god of war, otherwise known as Karttikeya.

verses.accessible: Among the great sages, I am Bhrigu; among sacred words, I am the single syllable Om; among forms of prayer and sacrifice, I am silent repetition; and among towering landmarks, I am the Himalayas.
notes: • Bhrgu, ancient seer, so illustrious that he mediated quarrels among the gods.

verses.accessible: Among all trees, I am the sacred fig tree; among divine sages, I am Narada; among celestial singers, I am Chitraratha; and among perfected spiritual masters, I am the sage Kapila.
notes: ,.. Narada, ancient seer to whom some verses of the ~g Veda are ascribed. t Gandharvas, the musicians of paradise. t Citraratha, heavenly chief of the Gandharvas. § Kapila, a sage, founder of the Saritkhya school of philosophy, one of the oldest of the Hindu systems.

verses.accessible: Among horses, know Me as Uchchaishravas, born from the nectar of immortality; among royal elephants, I am Airavata; and among humans, I am the king.
notes: .. Uccai!:tsravas, the name of Indra's horse, or of the horse of the Sun god, born of nectar that was churned from the ocean. The name means "high sounding." t Airavata, Indra's elephant. The name means

verses.accessible: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, I am the wish-granting cow of plenty; I am the creative power of love that brings forth life; and among serpents, I am Vasuki.
notes: • Kamadhuk, a mythical cow, able to provide its master with anything desired. t Kandarpa, god of love or desire, otherwise known as Kama. t Vasuki, a serpent king.

verses.accessible: Among celestial serpents, I am Ananta; among creatures of the waters, I am Varuna; among ancestral spirits, I am Aryaman; and among those who maintain law and order, I am Yama, lord of justice.
notes: • Ananta, a mythical snake whose coils encircle the earth and who symbolizes eternity. The word meal;1s "unending." t Varul)a, originally a Vedic god, the sustainer of the universe. Here, in the later religion, a water god, the" water king." t Aryaman, chief of the ancestors. § Yama, god of death.

verses.accessible: Among titans, I am the devoted Prahlada; among forces that measure all things, I am Time; among wild beasts, I am the lion, king of animals; and among birds, I am the eagle Garuda.
notes: .. Prahlada, a Daitya (enemy of the gods) prince who defected from the Daityas, became pious and worshipped Vishnu. t Daityas, demons at war with the gods. t The word" mrgendra" (mrga indra) means literally" king of beasts." § Vainateya (son of Vinata), otherwise known as Garu<;ia, a fabulous bird, and vehicle of Vishnu.

verses.accessible: Among purifiers, I am the sweeping wind; among warriors wielding weapons, I am Rama; among creatures of the deep, I am the crocodile; and among sacred rivers, I am the Ganges.
notes: " Rama, warrior and hero of the epic, the Ramayal)a, or possibly Parasurama, see chapter " Setting of the Bhagavad GWi." t Makara, a sea monster sometimes equated with a crocodile, shark or dolphin, the Capricorn of the Hindu zodiac, and vehicle of Varuna. ! So called because when Vishnu permitted the Ganges to flow, the sage Jahnu drank it up. Later he allowed it to flow from his ear.

verses.translation:
Of creations I am the beginning and the end,
And also the middle, O Arjuna;
Of all knowledge, the knowledge of the supreme Self.
I am the logic of those who debate.
verses.accessible: Of all creations, Arjuna, I am the beginning, the middle, and the end. Of all fields of knowledge, I am the spiritual science of the Self; and in honest debate, I am the logic that reveals the truth.
Among the letters of the alphabet, I am the first letter 'A'; among compound words, I am the balanced pair. I am infinite, endless Time; and I am the universal Creator, facing in every direction.
notes: • dvandva is the simple copulative compound, where two or more words are joined together.

verses.translation:
I am all-destroying death,
And the origin of those things that are yet to be.
Among the feminine qualities, I am fame, prosperity, speech,
Memory, wisdom, courage, and patience.
verses.accessible: I am all-consuming death, and I am the birth of everything yet to come. Among feminine virtues, I am fame, grace, speech, memory, insight, resilience, and patient forgiveness.
notes: .. All these listed nouns are of feminine gender.

verses.accessible: Among sacred chants, I am the great Brihat-saman; among poetic meters, I am the Gayatri; among months of the year, I am Margashirsha at harvest time; and among the seasons, I am blossoming spring.
notes: .. brhatsaman, a type of chant to Indra in the Sarna Veda. t gayatTt, a B-g Vedic metre consisting of three lines of eight syllables each, thought suitable for brahmans. It exists only in the Vedic literature. t maTgaStT~a, the month when the moon enters the constellation of mrga siras (" deer head," fifth lunar mansion), roughly November-December. It is interesting that Krishna's months and seasons are the Spring and Autumn. The hot Indian summer and the damp Indian winter are avoided.

verses.translation:
I am the gambling of the dishonest,
The splendor of the splendid;
I am victory, I am effort,
I am the goodness of the good.
verses.accessible: I am the cunning game of the gambler, and I am the brilliance of the brilliant. I am victory, I am tireless determination, and I am the moral goodness of the noble.
notes: • This line may also be translated: I am the truth of truth-tellers. (Sattva means either "good," "true" or "reaL")

verses.accessible: Among the Vrishni clan, I am Krishna; among the Pandava brothers, I am you, Arjuna; among silent sages, I am Vyasa; and among inspired poets, I am Ushana.
notes: • Vr~l).is, a clan from which Krishna himself is descended. t Vasudeva, patronymic of Krishna himself: .. Son of Vasudeva." t Vyasa, legendary sage supposed to have compiled the Vedas. His identity is chronologically confused. He is supposed to have compiled the Mahlibhlirata, of which the Bhagaved GTta is a part, and he appears in that Epic as the natural grandfather of the Pal).Qava princes. (See chapter, .. The Setting of the Bhagavad Glta.")

verses.translation:
Of punishers, I am the scepter,
And I am the guidance of those desirous of victory;
Of secrets, I am silence and
The knowledge of the wise.
verses.accessible: I am the scepter of justice that guides rulers, and I am the wise strategy of those seeking righteous victory. Among hidden secrets, I am the power of silence; and I am the deep wisdom of the wise.

verses.translation:
And also I am that which is the seed of all creatures,
Arjuna;
There is nothing that could exist without
Existing through Me, whether moving or not moving.
verses.accessible: Whatever is the vital seed of all living things, Arjuna, I am that. Nothing in existence—whether moving or still—can exist without Me.

verses.translation:
There is no end to My divine
Manifestations, Arjuna.
This has been declared by Me
As an example of the extent of My manifestations.
verses.accessible: There is no end to My divine powers and glories, Arjuna. What I have shared with you is merely a small glimpse of My boundless presence.

verses.translation:
Whatever manifested being that is
Glorious and vigorous, indeed,
Understand that in every case
He originates from a fraction of My splendor.
verses.accessible: Whenever you see anything that is glorious, beautiful, mighty, or full of life, understand that it springs from a mere spark of My radiant splendor.

verses.translation:
But what is this extensive
Knowledge to you, Arjuna?
I support this entire universe constantly
With a single fraction of Myself.
verses.accessible: But what need is there for you to learn all these endless details, Arjuna? I support and sustain this entire universe with only a single fraction of My being.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
As a favor to me, You have spoken
About the highest secret
Known as the supreme Self.
With this my delusion is gone.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'Out of compassion for me, You have revealed the supreme secret of the Self. Hearing Your words, all my confusion has vanished.'
notes: " The line is one syllable too long, a rarity in the Sloka stanzas of this poem.

verses.translation:
The origin and the dissolution of beings
Have been heard in detail by me
From You, O Krishna,
And also Your imperishable majesty.
verses.accessible: I have heard from You in great detail about how all living beings come to be and how they pass away, Krishna, and about Your inexhaustible, eternal majesty.

verses.translation:
Thus, as You have described
Yourself, O supreme Lord,
I desire to see Your divine form,
O Supreme Spirit.
verses.accessible: O Supreme Lord, You are just as You have described Yourself. Yet I deeply long to behold Your divine, sovereign form with my own eyes, O Supreme Spirit.

verses.translation:
If You think it possible
For me to see this, O Lord
Of Yogins, then show me
Your imperishable Self.
verses.accessible: If You think it is possible for me to behold it, O Lord of yoga, then please reveal Your imperishable Self to me.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Behold, Arjuna, My forms,
A hundred fold, a thousandfold,
Various, divine,
And of various colors and shapes.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Behold, Arjuna, My hundreds and thousands of divine forms, in countless varieties, shapes, and colors!'

verses.translation:
Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras,
The two Asvins, the Maruts too;
Many wonders unseen before,
Behold, Arjuna!
verses.accessible: Behold the solar gods, the deities of light, the storm gods, the twin celestial healers, and the wind gods. Look upon countless wonders never seen before, Arjuna!
notes: • Adityas, celestial deities led by the Vedic god VarUl;la. t Vasus, beneficent gods led by Indra, Agni or Varuna. . t Rudras, lit. "roarers," gods who drive away evil. § Asvins, celestial horsemen, always a pair, who herald the dawn and are skilled in healing. II Maruts, storm gods, friends of Indra, the thunderbolt hurler and chief god of the Vedas.

verses.translation:
Behold now the entire universe,
With everything moving and not moving,
Standing together here in My body, Arjuna,
And whatever else you desire to see.
verses.accessible: Look right here, Arjuna: behold the entire universe gathered as one inside My body—everything that moves and everything that is still—along with anything else you wish to see.

verses.translation:
But you are not able to see Me
With your own eyes.
I give to you a divine eye;
Behold My majestic power!
verses.accessible: However, you cannot see Me with your physical eyes. Therefore, I give you divine vision. Behold now My majestic, cosmic power!

verses.translation:
Sanjaya spoke:
Having spoken thus, O King,
The great Lord of yoga, Hari (Krishna),
Revealed to Arjuna
His majestic supreme form.
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'Having spoken these words, O King, the great Lord of yoga, Krishna, revealed His supreme, majestic form to Arjuna.'

verses.translation:
Of many mouths and eyes,
Of many wondrous aspects,
Of many divine ornaments,
Of many uplifted divine weapons.
verses.accessible: This form possessed countless mouths and eyes, countless breathtaking marvels, divine ornaments beyond measure, and countless raised celestial weapons.

verses.translation:
Wearing divine garlands and apparel,
With divine perfumes and ointments,
Made up of all marvels, the resplendent
Lord, endless, facing in all directions.
verses.accessible: Adorned with celestial garlands and robes, anointed with heavenly fragrances, radiant and full of endless wonders, the infinite Lord faced in every direction all at once.

verses.translation:
Ifa thousand suns should rise all at once
In the sky,
Such splendor would resemble
The splendor of that great Being.
verses.accessible: If the blinding light of a thousand suns were to blaze all at once across the sky, that brilliance might begin to resemble the glory of that supreme Being.
notes: to This was the stanza that occurred to the American nuclear physicist Robert Oppenheimer as he witnessed the explosion of the first atom bomb.

verses.translation:
There Arjuna then beheld
The entire universe established in one,
Divided in many groups,
In the body of the God of Gods.
verses.accessible: There, gathered together in one place within the body of the God of gods, Arjuna beheld the entire cosmos in all its vast and manifold divisions.

verses.translation:
Then Arjuna,
Who was filled with amazement,
Whose hair was standing on end,
Bowing his head to the Lord
With joined palms, said:
verses.accessible: Overwhelmed with awe and with his hair standing on end, Arjuna bowed his head before the Lord, folded his hands in reverence, and spoke.

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
I see the gods, O God, in Your body,
And all kinds of beings assembled;
Lord Brahma on his lotus seat,
And all the seers and divine serpents.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'O Lord, within Your body I see all the gods and every kind of living being assembled. I see the creator Brahma seated upon his lotus throne, surrounded by holy sages and celestial serpents.'
notes: • Tr#tubh metre begins as Arjuna commences to describe the Great Manifestation, and continues through most of this book (i.e. until stanza 51). t Brahmil (masculine), the creator god of the Hindu trinity. Not to be confused with Brahman

verses.translation:
I see You everywhere, infinite in form,
With many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes;
Not the end, nor the middle, nor yet the beginning of You do
I see, O Lord of all, whose form is the universe.
verses.accessible: I see You everywhere, limitless in form, with countless arms, bellies, faces, and eyes. O Lord of the universe, whose very form is the cosmos, I can see no beginning, no middle, and no end to You!

verses.translation:
Crowned, armed with a club and bearing a discus,
A mass of splendor, shining on all sides,
With the immeasurable radiance of the sun and blazing fire,
I see You, who are difficult to behold.
verses.accessible: I see You crowned with glory, armed with a mace and a discus—a mass of blazing light shining on all sides. You are almost impossible to look upon, radiating the immeasurable brilliance of roaring fire and the blazing sun.
You are the imperishable reality, the supreme truth to be known. You are the ultimate resting place of this universe, the inexhaustible guardian of eternal dharma, and the timeless, primal Spirit.

verses.translation:
With infinite power, without beginning, middle, or end,
With innumerable arms, the moon and sun being Your eyes,
I see You, the blazing fire Your mouth,
Burning all this universe with Your radiance.
verses.accessible: I see You without beginning, middle, or end, endowed with infinite power and countless arms. The sun and moon are Your eyes, blazing fire pours from Your mouths, and Your burning radiance scorches the whole universe.
notes: • saSin, that which contains the rabbit. The Hindus saw a rabbit in the moon, and this is a very common term for" moon." t Most translators avoid hutasa (huta asa), "oblation eating," which refers to the partaking of sacrifice, or render it as "fire," and translate vaktram as "face." The present translation, however, coincides with vaktra, "mouth," in stanza 23, and vaktra means" talker" or organ of speech, as well as "face."

verses.translation:
This space between heaven and earth,
Is pervaded by You alone in all directions.
Seeing Your marvelous and terrible form,
The three worlds tremble, O great Being.
verses.accessible: You alone fill the entire space between heaven and earth and every direction beyond. At the sight of this wondrous and terrifying form of Yours, O Great Soul, all three worlds tremble in dread!

verses.translation:
The throngs of gods enter into You,
Some, terrified, with reverent gestures praise You;
Saying “Hail,” the throngs of great seers and perfected ones
Extol You with abundant praises.
verses.accessible: Crowds of celestial gods are entering into You; some, terrified, fold their hands and chant Your praise. Throngs of great sages and perfected masters cry, 'Peace and blessing!' honoring You with magnificent hymns.

verses.translation:
‘The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, the Sadhyas,
The Vishve devas, the two Ashvins, the Maruts, and the Ushma pas,
The throngs of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and perfected ones,
All behold You, amazed.
verses.accessible: The storm gods, the solar deities, the gods of light, the ether spirits, the cosmic gods, the twin healers, the wind gods, the ancestors, heavenly musicians, nature spirits, titans, and perfected beings—all gaze upon You in utter astonishment.
notes: • l\1inor gods, see note stanza 6. t Slidhyas, a group of celestial beings with exquisitely refined natures thought to inhabit the ether. t Visve devas, group of twelve minor godlings. a § Steam Drinkers, a class of ancestors. II Gandharvas, celestial musicians. ,. y ak~as, a group of supernatural beings, sometimes benelovent, sometimes not . •• Asuras, a class of demons, enemies of the gods.

verses.translation:
Having seen Your great form, which has many mouths and eyes,
Which has many arms, thighs, and feet,
Which has many bellies, and mouths gaping with many tusks,
O Krishna, the worlds tremble, and so do I.
verses.accessible: Seeing Your colossal form with its countless mouths and eyes, its countless arms, thighs, and feet, its countless bellies, and its terrifying jaws bristling with fangs—all the worlds shudder in fear, and so do I!
notes: • Here referring to Krishna.

verses.translation:
Having seen You touching the sky, blazing, many colored,
Gaping-mouthed, with enormous fiery eyes;
I tremble indeed in my heart, and
I find neither courage nor tranquility, O Vishnu!
verses.accessible: When I see You touching the sky, blazing in vibrant colors, with Your jaws wide open and Your massive eyes burning with fire, my soul is shaken to its core. I find neither strength nor peace, O Vishnu!
notes: • Vishnu, the god of whom Krishna is the avatar.

verses.translation:
And having seen Your mouths, bearing many tusks,
Glowing like the fires of universal destruction,
I lose my sense of direction, and I do not find comfort.
Have mercy! Lord of Gods, abode of the universe!
verses.accessible: Looking upon Your mouths bristling with deadly fangs, raging like the fires of universal destruction at the end of time, I lose all sense of direction and can find no comfort. Have mercy, O Lord of gods, refuge of the universe!

verses.translation:
And entering into You, all the sons of Dhritarashtra,
Along with the throngs of kings,
Bhishma, Drona, and Karna, the son of the charioteer,
And also with our chief warriors,
verses.accessible: All the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with the hosts of allied kings, Bhishma, Drona, and Karna, together with the foremost warriors from our own army,

verses.translation:
They quickly enter Your fearful mouths,
Which gape with many tusks;
Some are seen with crushed heads,
Clinging between Your teeth.
verses.accessible: are rushing headlong into Your terrifying, fanged mouths! Some are caught between Your teeth, their heads crushed to powder.

verses.translation:
As the many torrents of the rivers
Flow toward the ocean,
So those heroes of the world of men
Enter your flaming mouths.
verses.accessible: Just as countless turbulent rivers rush onward into the ocean, so do these great warriors of the human world pour into Your flaming jaws.

verses.translation:
As moths enter a blazing flame
To their destruction with great speed
So also, these creatures swiftly enter
Your mouths to their destruction.
verses.accessible: Just as swarms of moths plunge headlong into a blazing fire to their own destruction, so too these armies rush into Your mouths to meet their doom.

verses.translation:
You lick up, swallowing on all sides
All the worlds, with your flaming mouths.
Filling all the universe with splendor,
Your terrible rays blaze forth, O Vishnu!
verses.accessible: You lick up and swallow all the worlds on every side with Your burning mouths. Your terrible rays scorch the entire cosmos, filling everything with blinding radiance, O Vishnu!

Tell me who You are, appearing in such a terrifying form! Salutations to You, O supreme God—please have mercy! I want to understand who You are in Your primal reality, for I cannot comprehend Your purpose.'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
I am Time, the mighty cause of world destruction,
Who has come forth to annihilate the worlds.
Even without any action of yours, all these warriors
Who are arrayed in the opposing ranks, shall cease to exist
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, fully grown and come forth here to consume all creation. Even without your participation, none of the warriors drawn up in these opposing ranks will survive.'

verses.translation:
Therefore stand up and attain glory!
Having conquered the enemy, enjoy prosperous kingship.
These have already been struck down by Me;
Be the mere instrument, O Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Therefore, rise up and claim your glory! Conquer your enemies and enjoy a rich, prosperous kingdom. All these warriors have already been struck down by Me; you need only be My instrument, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and
Karna too, others also, warrior heroes, have been killed by Me.
Do not hesitate! Kill!
Fight! You shall conquer the enemy in battle.
verses.accessible: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and the other brave fighters have already been marked for death by Me. Do not grieve or hesitate—fight, and you will surely defeat your enemies on the battlefield!'

verses.translation:
Sanjaya spoke:
Having heard this utterance of Krishna,
Arjuna, with joined palms, trembling,
Prostrating himself, terrified,
And bowing down, thus spoke in a choked voice to Krishna:
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'Hearing these words of Krishna, Arjuna trembled with folded hands. Deeply terrified, he bowed low to the ground and spoke to Krishna in a choked, faltering voice:'

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
Rightly, O Krishna, the universe
Rejoices and is gratified by Your praise.
The demons, terrified, flee in all directions;
And all the throngs of the perfected ones bow before You.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'It is only right, Krishna, that the universe rejoices and celebrates Your glory! Terrified demons flee in every direction, while all the hosts of perfected souls bow before You in deep reverence.

verses.translation:
And why should they not bow to You, O great One,
Who are the original Creator, greater even than Brahma!
Infinite Lord of Gods, you are the dwelling place of the universe,
The imperishable, the existent, the non-existent, and that which is beyond both.
verses.accessible: And why shouldn't they bow to You, O Great Soul? You are the primal Creator, greater even than Brahma. Infinite Lord of gods, sanctuary of the cosmos, You are the imperishable reality—existence, non-existence, and that which lies beyond them both.

You are the primal God, the ancient Spirit, the supreme resting place of all creation. You are the knower, that which is to be known, and the highest home. The whole universe is pervaded by You, O Being of infinite form!

verses.translation:
You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the Moon,
The Lord of creatures, and the great grandfather.
Salutations to You a thousand times,
And again salutations, salutations to You!
verses.accessible: You are the wind, death, fire, the waters, the moon, the Lord of creation, and the great-grandfather of all. A thousand salutations to You, again and again—salutations to You forever!
notes: • Vayu, the Vedic wind god. t Yama, literally "going," the Vedic god of the dead, and punisher of departed spirits. t Agni, god of fire. § Varul)a, Vedic" sustainer of the universe," later, and here, god of the waters. II sasiinka, the moon, literally the "rabbit marked," sometimes simply saSin, "that which contains the rabbit," favorite Hindu designation for the moon, because the Hindu's saw a rabbit instead of a " man" in the moon.

verses.translation:
Salutations to You from in front and behind,
Salutations to You on all sides also, O All.
You are infinite valor and boundless might.
You pervade all, therefore You are all.
verses.accessible: I bow to You in front, I bow to You from behind, and I bow to You from every side, O You who are Everything! Boundless in strength and limitless in might, You pervade and encompass all things—therefore, You are everything!

verses.translation:
Whatever I have said impetuously as if in ordinary friendship,
“Oh Krishna, Oh Son of Yadu, Oh Comrade,”
In ignorance of Your majesty,
Through negligence or even through affection,
verses.accessible: If I ever spoke rashly to You, thinking of You merely as a friend, saying, 'Hey Krishna, hey cousin, hey comrade!' unaware of Your vast greatness, whether out of carelessness or fond intimacy,

verses.translation:
And if, with humorous purpose, You were disrespectfully treated,
While at play, resting, while seated or while dining,
When alone, O Krishna, or even before the eyes of others,
For that I ask forgiveness of You, immeasurable One.
verses.accessible: and if I ever treated You disrespectfully in jest—while relaxing, resting, sitting, or sharing a meal, whether we were alone or in the presence of others—for all of that, O immeasurable Lord, I beg Your forgiveness!

verses.translation:
You are the father of the world, of all things moving and motionless.
You are to be adored by this world.
You are the most venerable Guru.
There is nothing like You in the three worlds.
How then could there be another greater, O Being of incomparable glory?
verses.accessible: You are the father of this entire world, of everything that moves and everything that is still. You are the most venerable teacher, worthy of all worship. In all three worlds, no one is Your equal—how could anyone ever surpass You, O Being of matchless power?

verses.translation:
Therefore, bowing down, prostrating my body,
I ask forgiveness of You, O Lord;
As is a father to a son, a friend to a friend,
A lover to a beloved, please, O God, be merciful!
verses.accessible: Therefore, bowing low and prostrating my whole body, I plead for Your grace, O adorable Lord! Please be patient with me, as a father is with his child, as a friend is with a friend, or as a lover is with the beloved.

verses.translation:
Having seen that which has never been seen before, I am delighted
And yet my mind trembles with fear.
Show me that form, O God, in which You originally appeared.
Have mercy, Lord of Gods, dwelling of the universe.
verses.accessible: I am overjoyed to have seen what no one has ever seen before, yet my heart trembles with dread. Please show me Your familiar divine form once again; have mercy, Lord of gods, refuge of the universe!

verses.translation:
I desire to see you wearing a crown,
Armed with a club, discus in hand, as before;
Become that four-armed form,
O thousand armed One, O You who have all forms.
verses.accessible: I long to see You as You were before, wearing Your crown, holding Your mace and discus. Assume that four-armed form once again, O thousand-armed Lord of universal forms!'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
By My grace toward you, Arjuna, this
Supreme form has been manifested through My own power,
This form of Mine, made up of splendor, universal, infinite, primal,
Which has never before been seen by other than you.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Out of grace toward you, Arjuna, I have used My divine power to reveal this supreme form of Mine—radiant, cosmic, limitless, and primal—which no one other than you has ever seen before.'

verses.translation:
Not by Vedic sacrifice nor (Vedic) recitation, not by gifts,
And not by ritual acts nor by severe austerities,
Can I be seen in such a form in the world of men
By any other than you, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Neither through the study of sacred scriptures, nor by sacrifices, charity, rituals, or harsh penances can I be seen in this cosmic form in the human world by anyone except you, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Have no fear or confusion
On seeing this terrible form of Mine,
Be again free from fear and cheered in heart.
Behold, My (previous) form!
verses.accessible: Do not let fear overwhelm you or bewilder your mind after seeing this terrifying form of Mine. Free yourself from dread, take heart, and look upon My familiar form once again.'

verses.translation:
Sanjaya spoke:
Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Krishna
Revealed his own (previous) form again.
Having resumed His gentle, wonderful appearance,
He calmed Arjuna, who was terrified.
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'Having said this to Arjuna, Krishna revealed His familiar form once more. Assuming His gentle, comforting appearance, the Great Soul calmed Arjuna’s fears.'

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
Seeing Your gentle
Human form, O Krishna,
Now I am composed
And my mind is restored to normal.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'Seeing Your gentle human form once again, Krishna, I have regained my composure, and my mind has returned to normal.'
notes: • Here metre resumes.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
This form of Mine which you have beheld
Is difficult to see;
Even the gods are constantly longing
To behold it.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'This cosmic form of Mine that you have just witnessed is extremely difficult to behold. Even the gods are constantly yearning for a single glimpse of it.'

verses.translation:
Not through study of the Vedas, not through austerity,
Not through gifts, and not through sacrifice
Can I be seen in this form
As you have beheld Me.
verses.accessible: Neither through mastering the sacred scriptures, nor through severe penances, nor through generous giving, nor through ritual sacrifice can I be seen in the way you have just seen Me.

verses.translation:
By undistracted devotion alone
Can I be known,
And be truly seen in this form,
And be entered into, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Only through single-minded, unwavering devotion can I truly be known, seen as I really am, and entered into, Arjuna.
notes: • Sanskrit has no passive infinitive. To form one, the auxiliary .jsak, is used, as here sakya draftum, "I can be seen," sakya jiiiitum, "I can be known."

verses.translation:
He who does all work for Me, considers Me as the Supreme,
Is devoted to Me, abandons all attachment,
And is free from enmity toward any being,
Comes to Me, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Whoever dedicates all their work to Me, cherishes Me as their supreme goal, loves Me with pure devotion, remains free from selfish attachment, and holds no hatred toward any living creature—that person comes directly to Me, Arjuna.'

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
The constantly steadfast devotees
Who worship You with devotion,
And those who worship the eternal unmanifest;
Which of these has the better knowledge of yoga?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'Between those devotees who are always dedicated and worship You personally with love, and those who meditate on the eternal, formless, and unmanifest reality—which of them has a deeper understanding of yoga?'

verses.translation:
The Blessed. Lord spoke:
Those who are eternally steadfast, who worship Me,
Fixing their minds on Me,
Endowed with supreme faith;
I consider them to be the most devoted to Me.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Those who fix their minds on Me, worshiping Me with constant dedication and supreme faith, are the ones I consider most deeply united with Me.'

verses.translation:
But those who honor the imperishable,
The indefinable, the unmanifest,
The all-pervading and unthinkable,
The unchanging, the immovable, the eternal,
verses.accessible: On the other hand, some worship the imperishable, undefinable, and formless Divine—the all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, and eternal reality.

verses.translation:
Controlling all the senses,
Even-minded on all sides,
Rejoicing in the welfare of all creatures,
They also attain Me.
verses.accessible: By mastering all their senses, treating everyone equally, and dedicating themselves to the well-being of all living beings, they also reach Me.
notes: • The substance of stanzas I, 2, 3 and 4 concerns two aspects of the Lord, and this point has been discussed by several native commentators. Those who worship Him as an imaginary form, fixing their minds on Him are considered the most devoted (stanza 2). But those who worship Him as the atman, or Brahman, devoid of all attributes and formless (stanzas 3 and 4), also attain to Him.

verses.translation:
The trouble of those whose minds
Are fixed on the unmanifest is greater,
For the goal of the unmanifest is attained
With difficulty by embodied beings.
verses.accessible: Yet the struggle is much greater for those whose minds are set on the formless Divine, because an abstract, invisible goal is very difficult for beings with physical bodies to reach.

verses.translation:
But those who, renouncing all actions
In Me, and regarding Me as the Supreme,
Worship Me, meditating on Me
With undistracted yoga,
verses.accessible: But those who dedicate all their actions to Me, cherish Me as their highest goal, and worship Me by meditating with single-minded devotion—
notes: • Again, the two aspects of the Lord, and the two corresponding methods of worship are discussed. Those who worship the Lord as the iitman, or self, or, in a larger sense, Brahman (in stanza 5), and those who worship the imaginary image on which the mind is "fixed" or " intent" (in stanzas 6 and 7). The former method is described as the more difficult.

verses.translation:
Of those whose thoughts have entered into Me,
I am soon the deliverer
From the ocean
Of death and transmigration, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: I quickly rescue them from the ocean of death and rebirth, Arjuna, because their hearts and minds are centered on Me.

verses.translation:
Keep your mind on Me alone,
Your intellect on Me.
Thus you shall dwell in Me hereafter.
There is no doubt of this.
verses.accessible: Focus your mind on Me alone, and let your understanding rest in Me. Beyond any doubt, you will live united with Me from now on.

verses.translation:
Or if you are not able
To keep your mind steadily on Me,
Then seek to attain Me
By the constant practice of yoga, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: If you cannot keep your mind steadily focused on Me, Arjuna, then seek to reach Me through the regular practice of yoga.

verses.translation:
If you are incapable even of practice,
Be intent on My work;
Even performing actions for My sake,
You shall attain perfection.
verses.accessible: If you are unable to manage regular spiritual practice, then dedicate your actions to My service. Even by simply doing your work for My sake, you will achieve perfection.

verses.translation:
But if you are unable even to do this,
Then, resorting to devotion to Me,
And abandoning all the fruits of action,
Act with self-restraint.
verses.accessible: And if you cannot even do that, then take refuge in devotion to Me, master yourself, and let go of all attachment to the results of your actions.

True knowledge is indeed better than mechanical practice, and meditation is higher than theoretical knowledge. Better still than meditation is letting go of the results of your actions, for deep peace immediately follows that letting go.

verses.translation:
He who hates no being,
Friendly and compassionate,
Free from attachment to possessions, free from egotism,
Indifferent to pain and pleasure, patient,
verses.accessible: The devotee who feels no hatred toward any creature, who is friendly and compassionate, free from selfishness and ego, patient, and balanced in both pleasure and pain,

verses.translation:
The yogin who is always contented and balanced in mind,
Who is self-controlled, and whose conviction is firm,
Whose mind and intellect are fixed on Me,
And who is devoted to Me, is dear to Me.
verses.accessible: who is always content, self-disciplined, firm in faith, and whose mind and intellect are dedicated to Me—that devoted person is deeply dear to Me.

verses.translation:
He from whom the world does not shrink,
And who does not shrink from the world,
Who is freed from joy, envy, fear, and distress,
Is dear to Me.
verses.accessible: Anyone who does not agitate others and is not agitated by the world, living free from turbulent excitement, anger, fear, and anxiety, is very dear to Me.
notes: I< "A devotee who, through ... karmayoga (the Yoga of action), practices bhaktiyoga (the Yoga of devotion or love) is beloved of God. So is the karmayogin (practitioner of the Yoga of action) who does nothing to vex the world, who is not vexed by the world because he is not interested in it and who therefore is not joyous, intolerant, fearful and irascible." - Ramanuja.

verses.translation:
He who is free from wants, pure, capable,
Disinterested, free from anxiety,
Who has abandoned all undertakings
And is devoted to Me, is dear to Me.
verses.accessible: One who is free from selfish desires, pure, capable, impartial, and untroubled by anxiety—who has let go of ego-driven ambitions and remains devoted to Me—is truly dear to Me.

verses.translation:
He who neither rejoices nor hates,
Nor grieves nor desires,
Has renounced good and evil,
And is full of devotion, is dear to Me.
verses.accessible: One who neither clings to joy nor feels hatred, who neither grieves over loss nor craves what is absent, and who has let go of both pleasant and unpleasant outcomes—living with deep devotion, that person is dear to Me.

verses.translation:
Alike toward enemy and friend,
The same in honor and disgrace,
Alike in cold and heat, pleasure and pain,
Freed from attachment,
verses.accessible: One who treats both friends and enemies alike, remains steady in honor and disgrace, stays calm in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and is free from selfish attachment,

verses.translation:
Indifferent to blame or praise, silent,
Content with anything whatever,
Homeless, steady-minded,
Full of devotion; this man is dear to Me.
verses.accessible: who responds to praise and blame with the same composure, speaks with restraint, is content with whatever comes, is not attached to a home, and keeps a firm mind full of devotion—that person is deeply dear to Me.

verses.translation:
Those who honor this immortal law described above,
Endowed with faith,
Devoted and intent on Me as the Supreme;
They are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.accessible: Those who faithfully follow this immortal wisdom that I have shared, full of faith and cherishing Me as their supreme goal—those devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.
notes: • Some translators have rendered dharmyamrtam idam as "this means of attaining immortality." Either translation may be correct. The confusion arises because" amrta " means both "nectar" and" immortality." .

verses.translation:
Arjuna said:
Prakriti and Purusha,
The field and the knower of the field,
Knowledge and the knower of knowledge,
I wish to know about these, Krishna.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'Krishna, I wish to learn about material nature and conscious spirit, the field and the knower of the field, and what true knowledge is, along with what is to be known.'
notes: • This first unnumbered stanza does not occur in all versions. It may have been deleted in order to make the total number of verses an even seven hundred.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
This body, Arjuna,
Is said to be the field;
He who knows this is called the knower of the field
By those who are wise in such things.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Arjuna, this physical body is called the field, and the conscious soul who is aware of it is called the knower of the field by those who see the truth.'
notes: • "Sages who possess exact knowledge of the body call it the experiencing-atman's field of experience. A person who knows this body and, because of this very knowledge, must be different from his body which is the object of his knowledge, is called a k~etrajiia (knower of the field) by these sages." - Ramanuja.

verses.translation:
Know also that I am the knower of the field
In all fields, Arjuna;
Knowledge of the field and of the knower of the field,
That is considered by Me to be true knowledge.
verses.accessible: Understand that I am also the Knower of the field within all bodies, Arjuna. Truly understanding both the field and the knower of the field—that is what I consider genuine wisdom.

verses.translation:
This field, what it is, and of what kind,
What its modifications are and whence they come,
And who he (the knower of the field) is, and what are his powers,
That, in brief, hear from Me:
verses.accessible: Now listen as I briefly explain what this field is, what its nature is, how it changes and where those changes come from, who the knower of the field is, and what powers he possesses.

verses.translation:
Sages have sung of it in many ways, distinctly,
In various sacred (Vedic) hymns,
And with quotations concerning Brahman,
Full of reasoning.
verses.accessible: Sages have explained this truth in many different ways through sacred hymns, and it has been clearly set forth in well-reasoned and definitive teachings about the ultimate reality.
notes: <I< Edgerton has pointed out that Badarayal).a's Brahma Sutra (zoo A.D.) probably did not exist at the time the Gita was. written, and that the meaning of "brahma siitra padais" here is probably therefore more general.

verses.translation:
The great elements, egoism,
Intellect and the unmanifest,
The senses, ten and one,
And the five objects of the senses,
verses.accessible: The field is composed of the five great elements, the sense of ego, the intellect, unmanifest nature, the eleven senses, and the five objects of perception,
notes: " I.e. ether, air, fire, water and earth. t Eye, ear, skin, tongue, nose and the five organs of action, viz. hand, foot, mouth, anus, genital organ. t The mind. § Sound, touch, color, taste and smell. N.B. These are all Samkhya concepts, as are the gw:zas.

verses.translation:
Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain,
the body, intelligence, steadfastness
this briefly is described as the field
with its modifications.
verses.accessible: along with desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the physical body, conscious awareness, and inner resolve. In short, this is what makes up the field and its various changes.
notes: • The physical body.

verses.translation:
Absence of pride, freedom from hypocrisy,
Non-violence, patience, rectitude,
Service of the teacher, purity,
Constancy, self-restraint,
verses.accessible: Humility, honesty, nonviolence, patience, uprightness, respect and service to a spiritual teacher, inner and outer purity, steadfastness, and self-control;
freedom from craving sensory pleasures, freedom from egotism, and a clear awareness of the inherent suffering in birth, old age, disease, and death;

verses.translation:
Non-attachment, absence of clinging
To son, wife, home, and so on,
And constant even-mindedness
Toward desired and undesired events;
verses.accessible: detachment and freedom from possessiveness toward children, spouse, or home, along with constant balance of mind through both pleasant and unpleasant events;

verses.translation:
And unswerving devotion to Me
With single-minded yoga,
Frequenting secluded places,
Distaste for the society of men,
verses.accessible: unwavering and single-minded devotion to Me, an appreciation for quiet and peaceful places, and a lack of interest in worldly crowds;

verses.translation:
Constancy in knowledge of the supreme Spirit,
Observing the goal of knowledge of the truth;
This is declared to be true knowledge.
Ignorance is what is contrary to this.
verses.accessible: steadfast commitment to spiritual wisdom, and keeping the pursuit of ultimate truth as your goal—all this is declared to be true knowledge. Everything contrary to this is ignorance.

verses.translation:
I shall declare that which has to be known,
Knowing which, one attains immortality;
It is the beginningless supreme Brahman,
Which is said to be neither existent nor non-existent.
verses.accessible: Now I will describe what must be known, because knowing it leads to immortality. It is the beginningless supreme reality, Brahman, which is said to be neither existent nor non-existent.

verses.translation:
Having hands and feet everywhere,
Eyes, heads and faces everywhere,
Having ears everywhere,
That stands, enveloping everything in the world.
verses.accessible: With hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces in every direction, and ears listening everywhere, that supreme reality exists, pervading and enveloping the entire universe.

verses.translation:
Shining by the function of the senses,
Yet freed from all the senses,
Unattached yet maintaining all,
Free from the qualities yet experiencing the qualities;
verses.accessible: It appears to possess the functions of all the senses, yet it is completely independent of them. It is completely unattached, yet it sustains everything; it is beyond the qualities of nature, yet it experiences them all.

verses.translation:
Outside and inside beings,
Those that are moving and not moving,
Because of its subtlety This is not comprehended.
This is far away and also near.
verses.accessible: It exists both outside and inside all living beings, in what moves and what is still. Because it is so subtle, it cannot be perceived by ordinary senses; it is unimaginably far away, yet it is intimately near.

verses.translation:
Undivided yet remaining as if divided
In all beings,
This is to be known as the sustainer of beings,
Their devourer and creator.
verses.accessible: Although it is undivided, it appears to exist as separate entities in all beings. Know that this reality sustains all creatures, dissolves them, and brings them forth once more.
notes: • This and stanzas 13, 14 and 15 are, of course, a description of Brahman and the dtman.

verses.translation:
Also This is said to be the light of lights
That is beyond darkness;
It is knowledge, the object of knowledge and that which is to be attained through knowledge.
It is seated in the hearts of all.
verses.accessible: It is said to be the light of all lights, far beyond any darkness. It is knowledge itself, the object of all knowledge, and the goal reached through wisdom. It is seated within the hearts of everyone.
notes: I< "Knowledge, the light of the titman, illuminates even luminaries such as the sun, a lamp, etc. which dispel only that darkness which hinders the contacts of the senses with objects. It is beyond prakrti (material nature)." - Ramanuja.

verses.translation:
Thus the field, knowledge,
And the object of knowledge have been briefly described.
My devotee, understanding this,
Enters into My state of being.
verses.accessible: I have briefly explained to you the field, the nature of knowledge, and what is to be known. When My devotee understands these truths, they become ready to enter into My divine nature.

verses.translation:
Know that material nature and Spirit
Are both beginningless,
And know also that the modifications of the field,
And the qualities, too, arise from material nature.
verses.accessible: Understand that both material nature and the conscious spirit have no beginning. Know also that all bodily changes and the three qualities of nature arise entirely from material nature.

verses.translation:
Material nature is said to be the cause
In the producing of cause and effect.
The Spirit is said to be the cause
In the experiencing of pleasure and pain.
verses.accessible: Material nature is the source of the physical body, the instruments of action, and cause and effect. But the conscious spirit is what experiences pleasure and pain.
notes: • "The activity of body and organs which are activities in experiencing depend on the prakrti (material nature) developed into k~etra (field or body). This prakrti is subservient to the person or puru~a who is the agent, as stated in the Sutras. This agency of the puru~a means that the puru~a is the cause and initiator of all activities to which the subservient prakrti is instrumental. So all experience of happiness and unhappiness depends on the puru~a conjoined with prakrti. The pur~a itself finds no happiness except in self-experience. When, however, the puru~a is conjoined with prakrti, it has experiences of happiness, unhappiness, etc., which are conditioned by its conjunction with prakrti and effectuated by gU1:zas, sattva,

verses.translation:
For the Spirit, abiding in material nature,
Experiences the qualities born of material nature.
Attachment to the qualities
Is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs.
verses.accessible: When the conscious spirit dwells within material nature, it experiences the qualities born of that nature. Its attachment to these qualities is what causes it to be reborn into higher or lower conditions of life.
notes: • "The puru~a (spirit of the individual), existing in a particular shape and nature divine, human etc. which is a result of previous developments of prakrti, is attached to happiness, etc. which consist of the gutJas and are proper to that particular nature, and is active in performing the good and evil acts leading to that happiness, etc. In order to experience the results of his acts he is born in a certain nature, good or evil; this new existence induces him again to be active and consequently to be born again in samsara (reincarnation), until he cultivates the qualities of humility, etc. by which he may attain the atman." - Rarnanuja.

verses.translation:
The highest Spirit in this body
Is called the witness, the consenter,
The supporter, the experiencer, the great Lord,
And also the supreme Spirit.
verses.accessible: The supreme Spirit dwelling within this body is described as the silent witness, the permitter, the supporter, the experiencer, the great sovereign Lord, and the ultimate Self.
notes: • "The purufa (spirit of the individual), when existing in such a body and conniving at its activities, looks on and consents; therefore it is the lord of the body. In the same way it experiences the happiness and unhappiness resulting from the body's activities. So because it rules, supports and exceeds the body, it is a sovereign lord as compared to its body, senses and mind. Likewise it is called the body's sovereign iitman sovereign as compared to the body and a most sublime purUfa, i.e. a puru~a whose knowledge and power are not to be circumscribed by the body .... Nevertheless, so long as it is attached to gu':tas, the purUfa is sovereign only as compared with the servile body." - Rlimlinuja.

verses.translation:
He who in this way knows the Spirit
And material nature, along with the qualities,
In whatever stage of transmigration he may exist,
Is not born again.
verses.accessible: Whoever understands the conscious spirit, material nature, and its qualities in this way will never be bound to the cycle of rebirth, no matter what their current way of life may be.
notes: • "He who knows that the pUTU~a and the prakrti have the aforesaid natures and who knows the nature of the gUlJas which is still left to explain he knows discriminatingly. He will not be reborn conjointly with prakrti but attain the purified iitman characterized by non-circumscribable knowledge, as soon as he dies."- Ramanuja.

verses.translation:
Some perceive the Self in the Self
By the Self through meditation;
Others by the discipline of Sankhya
And still others by the yoga of action.
verses.accessible: Some perceive the inner Self through the quiet practice of meditation; others realize it through philosophical reflection, and still others through the path of selfless action.
notes: .. Siimkhya, one of the earliest systems of Hindu philosophy, rational, non-theistic, dualistic, regarding prakrti and puru~a as the ultimate realities of existence, and believing that nothing new is ever created, all things being manifestations of

verses.translation:
Yet others, not knowing this,
Worship, having heard it from others,
And they also cross beyond death,
Devoted to what they have heard.
verses.accessible: Then there are others who do not know these spiritual paths on their own, but begin to worship after hearing the truth from others. By faithfully following what they have learned, they too cross beyond the cycle of death.
notes: .. Death, i.e. the kind of death that eventuates in rebirth.

verses.translation:
Know, Arjuna, that
Any being whatever that is born,
Moving or unmoving,
Arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
verses.accessible: Arjuna, understand that whatever comes into being—whether it moves or remains still—arises entirely from the union between the physical field and the conscious knower of the field.
notes: ... I.e. the union of body (field) and spirit (purufa).

verses.translation:
He who sees the Supreme Lord,
Existing alike in all beings,
Not perishing when they perish,
Truly sees.
verses.accessible: The person who sees the Supreme Lord living equally within all creatures, remaining imperishable even when their bodies perish—that person truly sees.

verses.translation:
Seeing indeed the same Lord
Established everywhere,
He does not injure the Self by the self.
Thereupon he goes to the supreme goal.
verses.accessible: Because they recognize the same Divine Lord present in all beings, they do not harm themselves or others through selfish actions, and so they attain the supreme goal.
notes: • Since the self (atman) of others is identical with one's own self, the line means that in injuring the self of others, one injures one's own self.

verses.translation:
He who sees that all actions
Are performed exclusively by material nature,
And thus the Self is not the doer,
Truly sees.
verses.accessible: Whoever sees that all actions are performed entirely by material nature, and that the conscious Self is not the actual doer, is the one who truly sees.
notes: • "When a person perceives that all acts are performed by the prakrti (material nature), that therefore the atman (self) is non-agent, and that the atman has the form of knowledge, then he perceives that the atman's conjunction with prakrti (material nature), its (the atman's) directing capacity and its experience of happiness or unhappiness all result from ignorance effected by karman (action) -, and then he has an exact

verses.translation:
When he perceives the various states of being
As resting in the One,
And from That alone spreading out,
Then he attains Brahman.
verses.accessible: When someone realizes that the diverse forms of all living beings are rooted in the One, and that everything expands from that single source, they attain oneness with the supreme reality.
notes: • "When a person perceives that all different modes of existence of all beings depend on one principle, prakrti (material nature), and not on the titman, and that the varieties of new beings issuing from these beings again arise from prakrti, then he will attain the otman in its purest form"- Rllmllnuja.

verses.translation:
This imperishable supreme Self
Is beginningless and without qualities;
Even though situated in the body, Arjuna,
It does not act, and is not tainted.
verses.accessible: Because this supreme, imperishable Self has no beginning and is free from the qualities of nature, it neither acts nor becomes tainted by action, Arjuna, even while residing within the physical body.

verses.translation:
As the all-pervading ether, because of its subtlety,
Is not tainted,
So the Self, seated in the body,
Is not tainted in any case.
verses.accessible: Just as all-pervading space is never stained because of its subtle nature, in the same way, the Self dwelling in every body is never contaminated by anything the body experiences.

verses.translation:
As the sun alone illumines
This entire world,
So the Lord of the field illumines
The entire field, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Just as a single sun lights up the whole world, Arjuna, the conscious soul—the Knower of the field—illuminates the entire body with consciousness.

verses.translation:
They who know, through the eye of knowledge,
The distinction between the field and the knower of the field,
As well as the liberation of beings from material nature,
Go to the Supreme.
verses.accessible: Those who perceive with the eye of wisdom the difference between the physical field and the knower of the field, and who understand how living beings can be freed from the grip of material nature, attain the supreme reality.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
I shall declare, further, the highest
Knowledge, the best of all knowledge,
Having known which all the sages
Have gone from here to supreme perfection.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'I will teach you once more the supreme wisdom, the highest of all knowledge. By understanding this, all the great sages have attained the highest perfection beyond this world.'

verses.translation:
Resorting to this knowledge,
And arriving at a state of identity with Me,
Even at the creation of the world they are not born,
Nor do they tremble at its dissolution.
verses.accessible: By taking refuge in this wisdom and becoming one with My divine nature, they are not reborn when the universe is created, nor are they troubled when it dissolves.
notes: • In reading stanzas like this, one must remember that, in the Hindu view, to be born is a misfortune. The ideal is to escape birth, or rebirth, and go on to nirva~a, or divine nonexistence. Also, in this instance, "beings" are assumed to be born at the creation of the universe and to be constantly reborn thereafter until the dissolution of this particular universe.

verses.translation:
Great Brahma is My womb.
In it I place the seed.
The origin of all beings
Exists from that, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Total material nature is My womb, Arjuna; within it I plant the seed of life, and from that source all living beings come into existence.

verses.translation:
Whatever forms are produced
In any womb, Arjuna,
The great Brahma is their womb,
And I am the seed-sowing father.
verses.accessible: Whatever forms of life are born into any womb in this world, Arjuna, material nature is their mother, and I am the father who gives the seed of life.

verses.translation:
Sattva, rajas, tamas, thus,
The qualities born of material nature,
Bind fast in the body, O Arjuna,
The imperishable embodied One (the atman).
verses.accessible: Material nature produces three fundamental qualities: sattva, rajas, and tamas—harmony, passion, and inertia. These qualities bind the imperishable soul to the physical body, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Of these, sattva, free from impurity,
Illuminating and free from disease,
Binds by attachment to happiness
And by attachment to knowledge, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Among these, sattva is pure, illuminating, and free from disturbance. Yet it still binds the soul, Arjuna, by creating an attachment to happiness and an attachment to knowledge.

verses.translation:
Know that rajas is characterized by passion
Arising from thirst and attachment.
This binds fast the embodied one, Arjuna,
By attachment to action.
verses.accessible: Know that rajas is driven by passion, springing from intense craving and emotional attachment. It binds the embodied soul, Arjuna, through a compulsive drive for action and results.

verses.translation:
Know indeed that tamas is born of ignorance,
Which confuses all embodied beings.
This binds fast, Ajuna,
With negligence, indolence, and sleepiness.
verses.accessible: Know that tamas is born of ignorance and deceives all embodied beings. It binds the soul, Arjuna, through carelessness, laziness, and excessive sleep.

verses.translation:
Sattva causes attachment to happiness,
Rajas to action, Arjuna;
Tamas, obscuring knowledge,
Causes attachment to negligence.
verses.accessible: Sattva attaches a person to happiness, rajas attaches them to restless activity, Arjuna, while tamas clouds their understanding and binds them to negligence.

Sometimes sattva rises by overcoming passion and inertia; sometimes rajas dominates by overpowering harmony and dullness; and at other times, tamas takes over by conquering both harmony and passion, Arjuna.
notes: " Three different relationships between, or proportions of, the three gUlJas, representing three types of personality, or three phases of behavior, are intended here. The distinction is in the relative proportion of one gur,za to the others in a given personality. The idea is continued in the next three stanzas.

verses.translation:
When the light of knowledge shines
Through all the gates of this body,
Then it should be known that
Sattva is dominant.
verses.accessible: When the light of clear understanding shines through every sense in the body, you can know that sattva is the dominant quality.

verses.translation:
Greed, activity and the undertaking
Of actions, restlessness, desire;
These are born when rajas
Is dominant, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Greed, frantic activity, ambitious projects, restlessness, and craving—all these arise when rajas becomes dominant, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Darkness and inertness,
Heedlessness and confusion;
These are born when tamas
Is dominant, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Mental darkness, sluggishness, carelessness, and deep confusion—these are the traits that emerge when tamas takes control, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
When an embodied being goes to dissolution (death)
Under the dominance of sattva,
Then he attains the stainless worlds
Of those who know the highest.
verses.accessible: If a person dies when sattva is the prevailing quality, they rise to the pure, untainted realms where the knowers of the highest truth dwell.

verses.translation:
He who goes to dissolution (death) when rajas is dominant,
Is reborn among those attached to action;
Likewise, dissolved (dying) when tamas is dominant,
He is reborn from the wombs of the deluded.
verses.accessible: If someone dies when rajas is dominant, they are reborn among people driven by work and ambition. And if they die under the influence of tamas, they are reborn into the lowest and most ignorant states of life.

verses.translation:
They say the fruit of good action
Is sattvic and without impurity,
But the fruit of rajasic action is pain,
And the fruit of tamasic action is ignorance.
verses.accessible: The reward of good actions is pure and harmonious, reflecting sattva. But the consequence of rajasic action is suffering, and the outcome of tamasic action is deeper ignorance.

verses.translation:
From sattva knowledge is born,
And from rajas desire;
Negligence and delusion arise
From tamas, and ignorance too.
verses.accessible: True knowledge arises from sattva, while greed and craving come from rajas. From tamas arise carelessness, delusion, and blind ignorance.
Those grounded in sattva move upward to higher realms; people ruled by rajas remain in the middle human realm; and those steeped in tamas sink downward into lower conditions.

verses.translation:
When the seer perceives
No doer other than the qualities,
And knows that which is higher than the qualities,
He attains My being.
verses.accessible: When an awakened observer sees that no agent acts other than these three natural qualities, and recognizes the supreme reality that stands beyond them, they enter into My divine nature.

verses.translation:
When an embodied being transcends
These three qualities, which are the source of the body,
Released from birth, death, old age, and pain,
He attains immortality.
verses.accessible: When a soul rises above these three qualities that produce the physical body, it is freed from the cycle of birth, death, old age, and sorrow, attaining immortal life.
notes: • This would appear on the surface to be one of the GWi's slight contradictions. Since the iitman of every being is already considered to be "immortal" the attainment of immortality through transcendence of the gUlJas would seem to be redundant. Ramanuja suggests that amrtam, immortality, means the opposite of what it means to us, that is, absorption in Brahman, nirvii1;w, or divine non-existence. The stanza makes sense if one considers that Brahman is "immortal," "unchanging" and "permanent."

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
By what marks is he recognized
Who has transcended these three qualities, O Lord?
What is his conduct? And how
Does he go beyond these three qualities?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'Lord, by what signs can we recognize someone who has risen above these three qualities of nature? How do they behave, and how do they manage to go beyond them?'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
He neither hates nor desires
The presence or the absence
Of light or activity
Or delusion, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Arjuna, such a person does not dislike clarity when it is present, restless activity when it arises, or delusion when it appears; neither do they crave them when they fade away.'
notes: .. The characteristic attributes of sattva, rajas and tamas.

verses.translation:
He who is seated as if indifferent,
Who is not disturbed by the qualities,
Thinking “the qualities are operating,”
And who stands firm and does not waver,
verses.accessible: They sit like an unconcerned observer, undisturbed by the play of the qualities. Knowing that it is merely the forces of nature interacting with nature, they remain firm and never waver.

verses.translation:
To whom pain and pleasure are equal, who dwells in the Self,
To whom a clod, a stone, and gold are the same,
To whom the loved and the unloved are alike, who is steadfast,
To whom blame and praise of himself are alike.
verses.accessible: Rooted in their true Self, they treat pleasure and pain alike, and view a lump of clay, a common stone, and a piece of gold as equal in value. They remain steady through pleasant and unpleasant events, unaffected by either criticism or praise.

verses.translation:
To whom honor and dishonor are equal,
Dispassionate toward the side of friend or foe,
Renouncing all undertakings
He is said to transcend the qualities.
verses.accessible: They remain the same in honor and dishonor, treat friends and enemies with equal goodwill, and have let go of ego-driven ambitions. Such a person is said to have risen above the three qualities of nature.

verses.translation:
And he who serves Me
With the yoga of unswerving devotion,
Transcending these qualities,
Is ready for absorption in Brahman.
verses.accessible: Whoever serves Me with unwavering, loving devotion rises above these three qualities and becomes ready to unite with the supreme reality, Brahman.

verses.translation:
For I am the abode of Brahman,
Of the immortal and the imperishable,
Of everlasting virtue,
And of absolute bliss.
verses.accessible: For I am the foundation of the eternal Brahman, the source of deathless immortality, the home of everlasting spiritual truth, and the wellspring of ultimate joy.

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
They speak of the eternal ashvattha tree,
Having its roots above and branches below,
Whose leaves are the (Vedic) hymns.
He who knows this is a knower of the Vedas.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'They speak of an eternal sacred banyan tree with its roots above in the Divine and its branches reaching down below into the world. Its leaves are the sacred verses of the Vedas, and whoever truly understands this cosmic tree knows the deeper truth of the scriptures.'
notes: • The asvattha (derived by some from asva stha meaning "where the horse remains" or "where the horse is tied "), is mentioned in the Vedas, but not in this fanciful upside down form, which appears, however, in the later Katha Upanishad (6, I). It is a sacred tree whose wood, along with that of the par~a tree, was used to kindle sacrifices. It belongs to the fig family. The symbol refers to the Supreme Spirit branching downward into the

verses.translation:
Below and above its branches spread,
Nourished by the qualities, with objects of the senses as sprouts;
And below its roots stretch forth
Engendering action in the world of men.
verses.accessible: Its branches spread both upward and downward, nourished by the three qualities of nature, with sensory objects budding as its tender sprouts. Its secondary roots extend down into the human world, binding people to their actions and desires.
notes: earthly realm. The following stanza seems to blur the symbolism somewhat by speaking of the "roots stretched forth below," but the asvattha tree, like the banyan to which it is related, strikes roots from its branches. Both trees are considered sacred in India. • Tr#tubh metre begins again.

verses.translation:
Its form is not perceptible here in the world,
Not its end, nor its beginning, nor its existence.
Cutting this ashvattha tree, with its well grown root,
By the strong axe of non-attachment,
verses.accessible: Its true form cannot be seen in this world—neither its beginning, nor its end, nor its firm foundation. But with the sharp and sturdy axe of detachment, one must cut down this deeply rooted tree,
notes: '" Line I of stanza 3 (trif!ubh metre) has an extra syllable. t Cutting the supernatural asvattha tree is a symbol for destroying the process of rebirth, and stanza 4 indicates that after the tree of life, or of rebirth, is cut, one seeks the place (nirva~a) from which there is no return to rebirth, and seeks refuge in the primal spirit whence activity streamed forth (see following stanza), that is to say Brahman. The cutting of the tree involves doing away with earthly desires (the branches or roots of stanza z), and leaving only the spiritual part which exists "above." The metaphor is rather confused by the lower" roots" of stanza z, line 3.

verses.translation:
Then that goal is to be sought
From which, having gone, no one returns.
In that primal Spirit I take refuge,
Whence the primeval energy streamed forth.
verses.accessible: and then seek that ultimate destination from which no one ever returns, saying: 'I take refuge in that original, supreme Spirit from whom the ancient stream of creation first poured forth.'

verses.translation:
