Without arrogance or delusion, with the evils of attachment conquered,
Dwelling constantly in the supreme Self, with desires turned away,
Released from the dualities known as pleasure and pain,
The undeluded go to that imperishable goal.
verses.accessible: Free from pride and delusion, having overcome the trap of selfish attachment, constantly united with the inner Self, and freed from the opposing swings of pleasure and pain, the wise reach that eternal, unchanging goal.
notes: • Triltubh metre continues. t I.e. Brahman.

verses.translation:
The sun does not illumine,
Nor the moon, nor fire, that place
To which, having gone, no one returns;
That is My supreme abode.
verses.accessible: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire is needed to light that supreme realm. Those who reach it never return to this world of suffering, for that is My highest abode.

verses.translation:
Merely a fragment of Myself,
Becoming an eternal (individual) soul in the world of the living,
Draws to itself the senses, of which the sixth is the mind,
That exist in material nature.
verses.accessible: An eternal spark of My own divine being becomes an individual soul in the world of living things. It draws to itself the bodily senses and the mind—the sixth sense—all rooted in material nature.
notes: '" Mind, in Gita psychology, is regarded as the sixth sense.

verses.translation:
When the Lord acquires a body,
And also when He departs from it,
He goes, taking them along,
Like the wind blowing perfumes from their source.
verses.accessible: When this soul takes on a new body or departs from an old one, it carries these senses and the mind along with it, just as the wind carries scents away from flowers.
notes: .. The mind and other senses, to be used in connection with another acquired body. t "Whatever body the iitman enters and from whatever body it departs, it will always retain those senses with the subtle elements and roam with them as the breeze roams with odors which it has carried from their original abodes."- Ramanuja. Thus, apparently, the iitman is not totally devoid of characteristics between one

verses.translation:
Presiding over hearing, sight and touch,
Taste and smell, as well as the mind,
He (i.e. the fragment of the Lord incarnated as the individual soul)
Enjoys the objects of the senses.
verses.accessible: Experiencing life through hearing, sight, touch, taste, and smell—and centered in the mind—the embodied soul interacts with and enjoys the objects of the senses.

verses.translation:
When He departs, remains,
Or enjoys (sense objects) while accompanied by the qualities,
The deluded do not perceive Him.
Those with the eye of knowledge see Him.
verses.accessible: Those who are confused and ignorant do not recognize the soul when it departs, stays in the body, or enjoys experiences under the influence of nature's qualities. But those with the clear eyes of spiritual wisdom see it clearly.
notes: • .. Those who are perplexed by ignorance do not perceive that the atman-with-gu~as is conjoined, forms a whole, with human nature etc., which are particular developments of prakrti consisting of gu~as, nor do they perceive that this iitman is either departing from a certain mass of prakrti, or existing in it and experiencing the objects (of the senses), and that (this) iitman might at some time be different from such a masshuman nature etc. and have only one form, knowledge. They are unable to perceive this, for they have the misconception that the iitman is akin to that mass to which it is conjoined. Those, however, who know the difference between mass and iitman and so perceive that the iitman, albeit present in all conditions, is different from whatever mass it is conjoined with, have a clear vision of the truth." - Riimiinuja.

verses.translation:
The yogins, striving, see Him (the embodied fraction of the Lord)
Situated in the Self,
But the unthinking, those of unperfected selves,
Strive but do not see Him.
verses.accessible: Diligent practitioners of yoga, striving with self-discipline, see this divine presence dwelling within themselves. But the thoughtless, whose minds are undisciplined and unrefined, fail to see it no matter how hard they try.

verses.translation:
That brilliance which resides in the sun,
Which illumines the entire universe,
Which is in the moon and which is in fire,
Know that brilliance to be Mine.
verses.accessible: Know that the radiant brilliance of the sun that lights up the whole world, the cool glow of the moon, and the blazing light of fire all come from Me.

verses.translation:
Entering the earth, I support
All beings with energy,
And, having become the watery moon,
I cause all the plants to thrive.
verses.accessible: Entering the earth, I sustain all living creatures with My vital energy. And becoming the nourishing moon, I supply life and flavor to all growing plants and crops.
notes: • There has been much speculation among scholars as to the identity of Soma, the drink of the gods the juice of a plant with inebriating properties that was drunk by the priests, the laity and the gods during sacrifices described in the Vedas. As the Vedic Aryans moved into India, the knowledge of the Soma plant seems to have disappeared, and, even from late Vedic times, substitutes for it were used mostly plants of the milkweed family whose juice is not inebriating. Recently R. Gordon Wasson, a mycologist acquainted with the Vedas in translation, has advanced a persuasive but still controversial hypothesis that the Soma plant was, in fact, a hallucinogenic mushroom (the amanita muscaria) which grew in the Aryans' original homeland in western Asia, and in Southern Asia only in the highest mountains. This circumstance, Wasson thinks, would explain the loss of the Soma as the Aryans migrated southward. It would also explain the rapturous descriptions of the effects of Soma drinking recorded in the B.g Veda. (See" Soma the Divine Mushroom," published by the Stamperia Valdonega, Verona.)

verses.translation:
Having become the digestive fire of all men,
I abide in the body of all living beings;
And joining with the prana and apana,
I (digest) the four kinds of food.
verses.accessible: I become the digestive fire within the bodies of all living creatures, and working together with the incoming and outgoing breaths, I digest all four kinds of food.

I am seated deep within the hearts of all beings. From Me come memory, knowledge, and forgetfulness. I am the one to be known through all the sacred scriptures; I am the creator of the Vedanta and the true knower of the Vedas.
notes: • TriNubh metre. t Vedanta, literally" the end (in the sense of conclusion) of the Veda," the predominant system of religious thought in India, expressed in the Brahma sfitra of BadarayaQa and the Upanishads, as well as in the present poem. Its formulation dates from approximately 500 B.C. and it has many points of difference from the Vedas of the original Aryans who invaded India circa 1600 B.C. Vedanta means primarily the thought expressed in the Upanishads, and secondarily, a system of philosophy based on it.

verses.translation:
There are these two spirits in the world
The perishable and the imperishable.
All beings are the perishable;
The unchanging is called the imperishable.
verses.accessible: There are two kinds of beings in this world: the perishable and the imperishable. All physical bodies and created forms are perishable, while the unchanging soul within is called imperishable.

verses.translation:
But the highest Spirit is another,
Called the supreme Self,
Who, entering the three worlds as the eternal Lord,
Supports them.
verses.accessible: Yet far beyond both of these is the highest Spirit, known as the Supreme Self. As the eternal, unchanging Lord, He enters and sustains all three worlds.

verses.translation:
Since I transcend the perishable
And am higher than the imperishable,
Therefore I am, in the world, and in the Vedas,
Celebrated as the supreme Spirit.
verses.accessible: Because I transcend the perishable world and rise higher even than the imperishable soul, I am celebrated throughout the world and in sacred scriptures as the Supreme Spirit—Purushottama.

verses.translation:
He who, thus undeluded, knows Me
As the supreme Spirit,
He, all-knowing, worships Me
With his whole being, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Whoever is free from confusion and knows Me as this Supreme Spirit truly understands everything, Arjuna, and loves and worships Me with their whole heart.

verses.translation:
Thus this most secret doctrine
Has been taught by Me, O Arjuna;
Having awakened to this, a man becomes wise
And fulfills all his duties, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: This is the most sacred and secret wisdom, Arjuna, which I have now revealed to you. A person who truly awakens to this becomes genuinely wise and achieves life's highest purpose.'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
Fearlessness, purity of being,
Perseverance in yoga and knowledge,
Giving, self-restraint and sacrifice,
Study of sacred texts, austerity, and uprightness,
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfast devotion to knowledge and meditation, generosity, self-control, selfless sacrifice, study of sacred wisdom, self-discipline, and straightforward honesty;

verses.translation:
Non-violence, truth, absence of anger,
Renunciation, serenity, absence of calumny,
Compassion for all beings, freedom from desire,
Gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness,
verses.accessible: nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, letting go of selfish attachment, inner calm, refusal to slander others, compassion for all living beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and steady composure;

verses.translation:
Vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity,
Freedom from malice, freedom from pride;
These are the endowment of those
Born to a divine destiny, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: radiant strength of character, forgiveness, resilience, cleanliness of body and mind, absence of malice, and freedom from excessive pride—these, Arjuna, are the qualities of a person born with a divine nature.

verses.translation:
Hypocrisy, arrogance, pride,
Anger, insolence,
And ignorance, are the endowment of those born
To a demoniacal destiny, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: Hypocrisy, arrogance, boastful conceit, anger, cruel harshness, and willful ignorance—these, Arjuna, are the marks of someone born with a demonic nature.
The divine qualities lead to spiritual freedom and liberation, while the demonic qualities drag a person into inner bondage. Do not grieve, Arjuna, for you were born with the divine qualities.

verses.translation:
There are two classes of created beings in this world
The divine and the demoniacal.
The divine has been explained at length;
Now hear from Me, Arjuna, about the demoniacal.
verses.accessible: There are two types of human natures in this world: the divine and the demonic. I have already explained the divine nature in detail; now listen carefully, Arjuna, as I describe the demonic.

verses.translation:
Demoniacal men do not understand
When to act and when to refrain from action.
Neither purity, nor good conduct,
Nor truth is found in them.
verses.accessible: People of a demonic nature do not understand what right actions to undertake or what harmful actions to avoid. In them, neither purity, nor ethical conduct, nor truthfulness can be found.

verses.translation:
“The universe,” they say, “is without truth,
Without basis, without a God;
Brought about by a mutual union.
How else? It is caused by lust alone.”
verses.accessible: They say: 'The universe has no moral truth, no foundation, and no governing God. It was brought about merely by random biological union—what else could cause it other than selfish lust?'
notes: • aparasparasambhiUam is somethines translated as "brought about by mutual union of man and woman," i.e. by sex, an interpretation favored by some native translators which does explain the fourth line better than the common translation. However, if one accepts this version of the line, the last line becomes redundant. The idea that sexual passion was the cause of all beings was held by the lokayatikas, followers of a nastika, or atheist and anti-orthodox school of philosophy which may be the object of this denunciation.

verses.translation:
Holding this view,
These men of lost souls, of small intelligence,
And of cruel actions, come forth as enemies
Of the world for its destruction.
verses.accessible: Clinging to this distorted worldview, these ruined souls with shallow minds engage in brutal and reckless deeds. They rise as enemies of the world, bringing only destruction and suffering.

verses.translation:
Attached to insatiable desire,
Full of hypocrisy, arrogance, and pride,
Having accepted false notions through delusion,
They work with unclean resolves,
verses.accessible: Driven by insatiable desires and puffed up with hypocrisy, vanity, and pride, they hold fast to foolish delusions and pursue impure, self-serving goals.

verses.translation:
Clinging to immeasurable
Anxiety, ending only in death,
With gratification of desire as their highest aim,
Convinced that this is all;
verses.accessible: Burdened by endless worries that end only at death, they make the indulgence of sensory desires their highest priority, convinced that this physical world is all there is.

verses.translation:
Bound by a hundred snares of hope,
Devoted to desire and anger,
They seek to obtain, by unjust means,
Hoards of wealth for the gratification of their desires.
verses.accessible: Trapped in a hundred tangled nets of selfish expectations, consumed by craving and fury, they scramble to hoard wealth by corrupt and unjust means just to satisfy their cravings.
They tell themselves: 'I gained this today, and I will get what I want tomorrow. All this wealth is already mine, and even more will belong to me soon!'

verses.translation:
“That enemy has been slain by me,
And I shall slay others too;
I am a lord, I am the enjoyer,
I am successful, powerful, and happy,
verses.accessible: 'I destroyed that enemy, and I will wipe out the rest as well! I am the master here; I enjoy whatever I please; I am successful, powerful, and happy!'

verses.translation:
“I am wealthy and high born.
Who else is equal to me?
I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice.”
Thus, they are deluded by ignorance.
verses.accessible: 'I am rich and from a prestigious family. Who can possibly match me? I will host grand rituals, give away charity for show, and celebrate my greatness!' Blown about by such thoughts, they are completely blinded by ignorance.

verses.translation:
Led astray by many imaginings,
Enveloped in a net of delusion,
Attached to the gratification of desires,
They fall into a foul hell.
verses.accessible: Misled by countless restless desires, trapped in a web of illusions, and addicted to indulging their senses, they sink down into a miserable, corrupt state of hell.

verses.translation:
Self-conceited, stubborn,
Filled with the pride and arrogance of wealth,
They perform sacrifices only in name,
With hypocrisy, and not according to Vedic injunction.
verses.accessible: Full of self-admiration and stubborn arrogance, drunk on wealth and social status, they perform rituals only in name—hypocritically and purely for show, with no regard for sacred tradition.

verses.translation:
Clinging to egotism, force, insolence,
Desire, and anger,
Those malicious people hate Me
In their own and others’ bodies.
verses.accessible: Surrendering to ego, brute force, arrogance, lust, and wrath, these resentful people hate Me, scorning the divine presence dwelling within their own bodies and in the bodies of others.

verses.translation:
Those cruel haters,
The worst of men, I constantly hurl
Into the wombs of demons
In the cycles of rebirth.
verses.accessible: Because they are cruel, hateful, and the lowest of humans, I repeatedly cast these destructive souls into the harsh cycle of rebirth, into degraded, demonic conditions.

verses.translation:
Having entered the wombs of demons,
Those who are deluded, not attaining Me
In birth after birth, Arjuna,
From there go to a condition still lower than that.
verses.accessible: Trapped in those degraded lives birth after birth, these deluded people fail to find Me, Arjuna, and sink deeper and deeper into even darker states.

verses.translation:
This is the threefold gate of hell,
Destructive of the self:
Desire, anger, and greed.
Therefore one should abandon these three.
verses.accessible: There are three gates leading directly to the hell of self-destruction: lust, anger, and greed. For that reason, every person must completely turn away from these three.

verses.translation:
Released from these three gates to darkness,
Arjuna,
A man does what is best for himself.
Then he goes to the highest goal.
verses.accessible: Whoever breaks free from these three gates of darkness, Arjuna, acts in ways that truly serve their highest good, and ultimately reaches the supreme destination.

verses.translation:
He who acts under the impulse of desire,
Casting aside the injunctions of the scriptures,
Does not attain perfection,
Nor happiness, nor the highest goal.
verses.accessible: Anyone who casts aside sacred wisdom and moral guidance to live purely by the impulse of selfish desires finds neither personal fulfillment, nor genuine joy, nor the highest goal.

verses.translation:
Therefore, determining your standard by the scriptures,
As to what is and what is not to be done,
Knowing the scriptural injunction prescribed,
You should perform action here in this world.
verses.accessible: Therefore, let the scriptures and timeless ethical wisdom be your standard in determining what you should do and what you should avoid. Understand what sacred guidance requires, and then carry out your work in this world.'

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
Those who sacrifice
Casting the injunctions aside, but filled with faith,
What is their condition, Krishna?
Is it sattva, rajas, or tamas?
verses.accessible: Arjuna asked: 'Krishna, what is the status of those who set aside scriptural rules but still offer worship with genuine faith? Is their devotion rooted in goodness, in passion, or in darkness?'

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds,
Born of their innate nature;
It is sattvic, rajasic,
And tamasic. Now hear of this.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, arising naturally from their inner character: it may be pure and good (sattvic), passionate and restless (rajasic), or dark and ignorant (tamasic). Now listen to how they differ.

verses.translation:
Faith is in accordance
With the truth (nature) of each, Arjuna.
Man is made of faith.
Whatever faith he has, thus he is.
verses.accessible: Every person's faith reflects their essential nature, Arjuna. A human being is truly shaped by their faith; whatever a person places their faith in, that is what they become.

verses.translation:
The sattvic worship the gods,
The rajasic worship the Yakshas and demons;
The others, the tamasic men, worship
The ghosts and the hordes of nature spirits.
verses.accessible: People in the mode of goodness worship divine beings; those driven by passion worship power-hungry spirits and demons; and those stuck in darkness worship ghosts and lower nature spirits.

verses.translation:
Men who undergo terrible austerities
Not enjoined by the scriptures,
Accompanied by hypocrisy and egotism,
Along with desire and passion,
verses.accessible: Some people subject themselves to extreme, harsh mortifications not recommended by sacred wisdom, driven by vanity, ego, lust, and stubborn willpower.

verses.translation:
The unthinking, torturing within the body
The aggregate of elements,
And also torturing Me thus within the body,
Know them to be of demoniacal resolves.
verses.accessible: In their thoughtlessness, they torture the physical elements within their own bodies, and in doing so, they torture Me, who dwells within them. Know that their resolutions come from a demonic nature.
notes: • This and the preceding stanzas constitute one of several injunctions in the Bhagavad Gitil against exaggerated austerities, or mortifications of the flesh. These injunctions are interesting because they show that such abuses were common enough to arouse denunciation.

verses.translation:
But also the food preferred by all
Is of three kinds,
As are their sacrifices, austerities, and gifts.
Hear now the distinction between them.
verses.accessible: Even the foods people prefer fall into three distinct types, as do their worship, self-discipline, and charity. Listen now to the differences among them.

verses.translation:
Promoting life, virtue, strength, health,
Happiness, and satisfaction,
Which are savory, smooth, firm, and pleasant to the stomach;
Such foods are dear to the sattvic.
verses.accessible: Foods that promote long life, mental clarity, physical strength, health, happiness, and cheerfulness—foods that are flavorful, smooth, nourishing, and satisfying to the heart—are loved by those in the mode of goodness.

verses.translation:
Causing pain, misery, and sickness,
Bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot,
Pungent, dry, and burning;
Such foods are desired. by the rajasic.
verses.accessible: Foods that are excessively bitter, sour, salty, burning hot, pungent, dry, and scorching are preferred by passionate people. Such foods cause discomfort, distress, and disease.

verses.translation:
Stale, tasteless, putrid, rotten,
And refuse as well as the impure,
Is the food which
Is dear to the tamasic.
verses.accessible: Food that is stale, cold, flavorless, rotting, spoiled, left over from someone else's plate, or impure is favored by people in the mode of darkness.
notes: • I t is not difficult to detect in this and the preceding two stanzas the hand of the brahman caste, insisting on its superiority to an extent that is almost comic. It has been pointed out by historians that, though the Mahabharata is primarily an epic of the /qatriya, or warrior, caste, the Bhagavad Glta, along with some other interpolations of a moral or religious character, was probably inserted into the poem later by the priestly caste of brahmans.

verses.translation:
Sacrifice which is offered, observing the scriptures,
By those who do not desire the fruit,
Concentrating the mind only on the thought “this is to be sacrificed”;
That sacrifice is sattvic.
verses.accessible: Worship performed in accordance with sacred guidelines by those who expect no personal reward, keeping their minds focused solely on duty—believing with all their heart that worship ought to be done—is pure and sattvic.

verses.translation:
But sacrifice which is offered
With a view to the fruit, Arjuna,
And also for the purpose of ostentation;
Know that to be rajasic.
verses.accessible: But worship performed with an eye on personal gain or merely to impress others and put on a public show, Arjuna, know that worship to be rajasic.

verses.translation:
Sacrifice devoid of faith,
Contrary to scriptural ordinances, with no food offered,
Without mantras and without gifts (to the presiding priest),
They regard as tamasic.
verses.accessible: Worship performed with no regard for sacred tradition, with no food shared, without sacred prayers, with no honoring of teachers, and devoid of genuine faith, is considered tamasic.

verses.translation:
Worship of the gods, the twice-born, teachers,
And wise men; purity, rectitude,
Celibacy, and non-violence;
These are called austerities of the body.
verses.accessible: Showing respect to the divine, the wise, teachers, and elders, along with physical cleanliness, honesty, self-restraint, and nonviolence—this is called the austerity of the body.
Speaking words that cause no offense, words that are truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, together with the regular study of sacred writings—this is called the austerity of speech.

verses.translation:
Peace of mind, gentleness,
Silence, self-restraint,
Purity of being; these
Are called austerities of the mind.
verses.accessible: Inner serenity, kindness, quiet reflection, self-control, and purity of intention—this is called the austerity of the mind.

verses.translation:
This threefold austerity
Practiced with the highest faith by men
Who are not desirous of fruits and are steadfast,
They regard as sattvic.
verses.accessible: When this threefold self-discipline is practiced with deep faith by steadfast individuals who seek no selfish rewards, it is declared to be sattvic.

verses.translation:
Austerity which is practiced with hypocrisy
For the sake of honor, respect, and reverence;
That, here in the world, is declared to be
Rajasic, unsteady, and impermanent.
verses.accessible: Self-discipline practiced hypocritically for the sake of winning applause, respect, and admiration from others is declared to be rajasic. It is unstable, shallow, and temporary.

verses.translation:
Austerity which is performed
With deluded notions and with self-torture,
Or with the aim of destroying another,
Is declared to be tamasic.
verses.accessible: Self-discipline practiced through foolish obstinacy, involving painful self-harm or intended to injure and destroy someone else, is declared to be tamasic.

verses.translation:
The gift which is given only with the thought “it is to be given,”
To a worthy person who has done no prior favor,
At the proper place and time;
That gift is held to be sattvic.
verses.accessible: A gift given simply because giving is right, offered at the proper time and place to a deserving person who cannot repay it, is recognized as sattvic.

verses.translation:
But that gift which is given grudgingly,
With the aim of recompense
Or gain, with regard to fruit,
Is considered rajasic.
verses.accessible: But a gift given reluctantly, with the expectation of getting something in return or with an eye on future reward, is regarded as rajasic.

verses.translation:
That gift which is given at the wrong place and time
To the unworthy,
Without paying respect, or with contempt,
Is declared to be tamasic.
verses.accessible: A gift handed out at the wrong time and place to an undeserving person, given with disrespect or outright contempt, is said to be tamasic.

verses.translation:
“Om tat sat” this has been taught as
The threefold designation of Brahman.
By this the brahmins, the Vedas,
And the sacrifices were created in ancient times.
verses.accessible: ‘OM TAT SAT’ has been revealed as the threefold designation of Brahman, the ultimate Reality. By this sacred phrase, seekers of truth, sacred scriptures, and acts of worship were created in ancient times.
notes: " om tat sat (" om that [is] real ") is a common mantra, or sacred utterance, among Hindus. It begins with the sacred syllable "oriz" which is made up of three sounds a, u, m representing the three Vedas, the "three worlds" (heaven, atmosphere, earth), the three principal deities (Brahma, Vishnu and Siva) and the beginning, middle and ending of all things. The rest of the mantra is an affirmation of the existence of Brahman, for which "om" is a designation, but see commentary on "tat sat" in stanzas 2S and 26. "Sat" in Sanskrit has the meanings of "real" or "true" and that of "good."

verses.translation:
Therefore, acts of sacrifice, giving, and austerity
Are always begun uttering the syllable “Om”
By the students of Brahman,
As prescribed in the Vedic injunctions.
verses.accessible: Therefore, spiritual seekers who revere the Supreme always begin their prescribed acts of worship, charity, and self-discipline by speaking the sacred syllable 'OM'.

verses.translation:
Uttering “tat” and without aiming at
Fruits, acts of sacrifice and austerity
And acts of giving of various sorts
Are performed by those who desire liberation.
verses.accessible: Uttering 'TAT' ('That'), and letting go of all desire for personal reward, those who yearn for spiritual freedom perform their varied acts of worship, self-discipline, and charity.

verses.translation:
“Sat” is used
In its meaning of “reality” and in its meaning of “goodness.”
Also the word “sat” is used
For an auspicious act, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: The word 'SAT' represents ultimate reality and genuine goodness. In the same way, Arjuna, the word 'SAT' is used to describe every noble and honorable deed.

verses.translation:
Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and
Giving is also called “sat,”
And action relating to these
Is likewise designated as “sat.”
verses.accessible: Steadfast dedication to worship, self-discipline, and charity is also called 'SAT', and any work done for the sake of the Divine is likewise known as 'SAT'.

verses.translation:
An oblation offered or an austerity practiced
Without faith
Is called “asat,” Arjuna,
And is nothing in the hereafter or here in the world.
verses.accessible: Whatever worship is offered, charity given, self-discipline practiced, or action performed without faith is declared to be 'ASAT'—meaningless and false. It brings no lasting benefit, Arjuna, neither in this world nor in the life to come.'

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
I wish to know the truth
Of sannyasa, Krishna,
And of renunciation,
And the difference between them.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'Krishna, I want to understand the true nature of renunciation—both sannyasa, the renouncing of selfish actions, and tyaga, the giving up of attachment to results—and the real difference between them.'
notes: • mahiibiiho, "0 Mighty Armed One," usually an epithet of Arjuna, is here applied to Krishna. It is a general epithet of distinguished warriors. t The iisura Kdin was slain by Vishnu (Krishna) in another part of the Mahiibhiirata. (See chapter on "The Setting of the Bhagaviid Gltii".)

verses.translation:
The Blessed Lord spoke:
The relinquishment of actions prompted by desire
The sages understand as sannyasa;
The relinquishment of the fruit of all action
The wise declare to be renunciation.
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'The sages understand sannyasa as giving up all actions driven by selfish desire, while the wise define tyaga as letting go of the fruits of all actions.'
notes: .. The words are clear enough, but, to avoid any misunderstanding, what is said is that renunciation (samnyiisa) is the relinquishment of all action which is aimed at a desired result; abandonment (tyiiga) is the relinquishment of the results of action, and thus does not imply nonaction as renunciation does.

verses.translation:
Some men of wisdom declare
That action is to be abandoned and is full of evil,
And others say that acts of sacrifice, giving, and austerity
Are not to be abandoned.
verses.accessible: Some thinkers argue that all action is flawed and should be abandoned, while others insist that acts of sacrifice, charity, and self-discipline should never be given up.

verses.translation:
Hear My conclusion in this matter
Concerning renunciation, Arjuna.
Renunciation is declared
To be of three kinds:
verses.accessible: Listen now, Arjuna, to My definitive conclusion regarding renunciation. Truly, renunciation is declared to be of three kinds.

verses.translation:
Acts of sacrifice, giving, and austerity
Are not to be abandoned, but rather to be performed;
Sacrifice, giving, and austerity
Are purifiers of those who are wise.
verses.accessible: Acts of sacrifice, charity, and self-discipline must not be abandoned; they should always be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, giving, and self-discipline purify the hearts of even the wise.

verses.translation:
These actions, however, are to be performed
Abandoning attachment to the fruits.
This is My definite
And highest belief, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: However, these actions must be carried out simply as a duty, free from personal attachment and with no craving for rewards. This, Arjuna, is My firm and final conviction.

verses.translation:
But renunciation of obligatory action
Is not proper;
The abandonment of it through delusion
Is proclaimed to be tamasic.
verses.accessible: It is not proper to abandon required duties. Giving up prescribed responsibilities out of confusion or delusion is declared to be tamasic, rooted in darkness.

verses.translation:
He who abandons action merely because it is difficult,
Or because of fear of bodily suffering,
Performs rajasic renunciation.
He does not obtain the fruit of that renunciation.
verses.accessible: Anyone who gives up their duties simply because the work is difficult, or out of fear of physical discomfort, performs rajasic renunciation. Such a person never gains the true spiritual reward of letting go.

verses.translation:
When action is done because it is a duty,
Arjuna,
And abandoning attachment to the fruit,
Such renunciation is thought to be sattvic.
verses.accessible: When a required duty is performed simply because it ought to be done, letting go of all attachment and craving for the outcome, that renunciation is considered sattvic, pure and harmonious.
notes: • Action "to be done," i.e. religiously prescribed action such as sacrifice, purification, giving, austerity.

verses.translation:
The man of renunciation, the wise man
Whose doubt is cut away, filled with goodness,
Does not hate disagreeable action,
Nor is he attached to agreeable action.
verses.accessible: A true renouncer, filled with goodness, wise, and freed from doubt, neither resents unpleasant work nor clings eagerly to pleasant work.

verses.translation:
Indeed embodied beings are not able
To abandon actions entirely;
He, then, who abandons the fruit of action,
Is called a man of renunciation.
verses.accessible: It is impossible for any embodied human being to give up all action completely. Therefore, the person who genuinely lets go of the fruits of action is the one called a true renouncer.

verses.translation:
The fruit of action for those who have not renounced
When they depart (die) is threefold:
Evil, good, and mixed;
But for the renouncers there is none whatever.
verses.accessible: For those who do not renounce the results of their deeds, the karmic consequences after death are threefold: pleasant, unpleasant, and mixed. But for those who have truly renounced attachment to results, there are no karmic consequences at all.

verses.translation:
Learn from Me, O Arjuna,
These five factors,
Declared in the Sankhya doctrine
For the accomplishment of all actions:
verses.accessible: Learn from Me, Arjuna, the five essential factors taught in the Sankhya philosophy for the accomplishment of every action:
notes: • See note to stanza 39, Book II, for explanation of the SJimkhya system.

verses.translation:
The seat of action (the body), the doer,
The various organs,
And the various separate activities,
With the presiding deities as the fifth;
verses.accessible: The physical body as the seat of action, the conscious agent or doer, the various senses and organs, the distinct kinds of effort, and divine providence or destiny as the fifth.
notes: • adhiithdna (seat of action) is interpreted by most commentators as the physical body. t The word "agent" is used here and elsewhere in this book in the meaning of "one who

verses.translation:
Whatever action a man undertakes
With his body, speech or mind,
Either right of wrong,
These are its five factors.
verses.accessible: Whatever action a person undertakes with body, speech, or mind—whether right or wrong—these five factors are its causes.
notes: • Again, in Gitli psychology the mind acts, and so does speech.

verses.translation:
This being so, he who sees his Self
As the doer does not really see,
Because of the fact that
He has not perfected his understanding.
verses.accessible: Since this is true, anyone who regards their pure Self alone as the sole doer fails to see reality, because their understanding is untrained and incomplete.

verses.translation:
He whose state of mind is not egoistic,
Whose intellect is not tainted,
Even though he slays these people,
He does not slay, and is not bound (by his actions).
verses.accessible: One who is entirely free from ego—who does not think 'I am the doer'—and whose intellect remains untainted by selfish motives does not kill even if they strike down these warriors in battle, nor are they bound by their actions.

verses.translation:
Knowledge, the process of knowing, and the knower
Are the threefold impulse to action;
The instrument, the action, and the doer
Are the threefold basis of action.
verses.accessible: Knowledge, the object to be known, and the knower form the threefold impulse to action. The instrument, the action itself, and the doer form the threefold foundation through which action takes place.

verses.translation:
It is declared in Sankhya that
Knowledge, action, and the doer
Are of three kinds, distinguished according to the qualities.
Hear about these also:
verses.accessible: In the Sankhya philosophy of nature's qualities, knowledge, action, and the doer are each described as having three forms based on the gunas. Listen carefully as I explain them to you:

verses.translation:
That knowledge by which one sees
One imperishable Being in all beings,
Undivided in separate beings;
Know that knowledge to be sattvic.
verses.accessible: The knowledge that enables you to see a single, imperishable reality in all living beings—undivided among the seemingly separate—know that knowledge to be sattvic, pure and true.

verses.translation:
But that knowledge which sees
In all beings
Separate entities of various kinds, by differentiation,
Know that knowledge to be rajasic.
verses.accessible: But the knowledge that sees living beings as completely distinct and divided into separate, disconnected entities—know that knowledge to be rajasic, driven by passion.

verses.translation:
That (knowledge), however, which is attached to one single effect
As if it were all, and without reason,
Without a real purpose and small in significance,
Is declared to be tamasic.
verses.accessible: And the narrow knowledge that blindly fixates on a single, isolated thing as if it were everything—irrational, devoid of truth, and trivial—is declared to be tamasic, rooted in ignorance.

verses.translation:
That action which is ordained and free from attachment,
Performed without desire or hate,
With no wish to obtain fruit,
Is said to be sattvic.
verses.accessible: Action that is required by duty, done without attachment, free from love or hate, and performed by someone who has no craving for personal reward, is called sattvic.

verses.translation:
But that action which is performed with a wish to obtain desires,
With selfishness, or, again,
With much effort,
Is declared to be rajasic.
verses.accessible: Action carried out with stressful effort, fueled by selfish desires, or driven by ego and pride, is declared to be rajasic.

verses.translation:
That action which is undertaken because of delusion,
Disregarding consequences, loss, or injury to others,
As well as one’s own ability,
Is said to be tamasic.
verses.accessible: Action undertaken out of delusion, disregarding future consequences, waste of resources, harm to others, or one's own limitations, is called tamasic.

verses.translation:
Released from attachment, free from ego,
Endowed with steadfastness and resolution,
Unperturbed in success or failure;
Such a doer is said to be sattvic.
verses.accessible: A doer who is free from selfish attachment, devoid of ego, filled with steadfast determination and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.

verses.translation:
Passionate, desiring the fruits of action,
Greedy, violent-natured, impure,
Subject to joy or sorrow;
Such a doer is proclaimed to be tajasic.
verses.accessible: A doer who is swayed by passion, obsessed with the fruits of their work, greedy, cruel-hearted, impure, and easily thrown into joy or sorrow, is proclaimed to be rajasic.

verses.translation:
Undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate,
Wicked, deceitful, lazy,
Despondent, and procrastinating;
Such a doer is said to be tamasic.
verses.accessible: A doer who is undisciplined, crude, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, easily depressed, and prone to endless procrastination, is called tamasic.

verses.translation:
Now hear the threefold distinctions of intellect
And also of firmness, according to the qualities,
Taught completely
And separately, Arjuna:
verses.accessible: Now listen, Arjuna, as I describe completely and distinctly the threefold division of intellect and determination according to the three qualities of nature:

verses.translation:
That intellect which knows when to act and when not to act,
What is to be done and what is not to be done,
And what is to be feared and what is not to be feared,
Along with the knowledge of bondage and liberation, Arjuna, is sattvic.
verses.accessible: The intellect that clearly discerns when to act and when to refrain, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, what to fear and what not to fear, and what leads to bondage versus what leads to liberation—that intellect, Arjuna, is sattvic.

verses.translation:
That intellect which distinguishes incorrectly
Between the right and the wrong,
And between that which is to be done and that which is not to be done,
Is rajasic, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: The intellect that confuses right with wrong, fails to grasp true morality, and misjudges what should and should not be done—that intellect, Arjuna, is rajasic.

verses.translation:
That intellect which, enveloped in darkness,
Imagines wrong to be right,
And all things to be perverted,
Is tamasic, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: The intellect that is shrouded in darkness, mistaking injustice for justice and seeing everything twisted upside down—that intellect, Arjuna, is tamasic.

verses.translation:
The unswerving firmness by which,
Through yoga, one holds fast
The functions of the mind, vital breath, and senses,
That firmness, Arjuna, is sattvic.
verses.accessible: The unwavering resolve by which a person, through the steady practice of yoga, disciplines and harmonizes the activities of the mind, the life-breath, and the senses—that determination, Arjuna, is sattvic.

verses.translation:
But the firmness by which one holds to
Duty, pleasures, and wealth,
With attachment and desire for the fruits of action,
That firmness, Arjuna, is rajasic.
verses.accessible: The stubborn resolve by which someone clings to duty, wealth, and sensual pleasures out of personal attachment, driven by a craving for rewards—that determination, Arjuna, is rajasic.

verses.translation:
That firmness by which a stupid man
Does not abandon sleep, fear, grief,
Depression, and conceit,
Is tamasic, Arjuna.
verses.accessible: The foolish resolve by which a shortsighted person refuses to let go of excessive sleep, fear, grief, depression, and arrogance—that determination, Arjuna, is tamasic.

verses.translation:
And now, hear from Me, Arjuna,
The threefold happiness
That one enjoys through practice,
And in which one comes to the end of suffering.
verses.accessible: And now hear from Me, Arjuna, about the three kinds of happiness. That joy which one discovers through patient practice, and which brings an end to all suffering:

verses.translation:
That which in the beginning is like poison
But in the end like nectar;
That happiness, born from the tranquility of one’s own mind,
Is declared to be sattvic.
verses.accessible: That happiness which tastes like poison at first but turns into nectar in the end, born from the inner peace of clear self-awareness—that happiness is declared to be sattvic.

verses.translation:
That which in the beginning, through contact
Between the senses and their objects, is like nectar,
And in the end like poison;
That happiness is declared to be rajasic.
verses.accessible: That happiness which arises from the senses contacting their objects, tasting like nectar at first but turning into poison in the end—that happiness is recognized as rajasic.

verses.translation:
That happiness which both in the beginning
And afterwards deludes the self,
Arising from sleep, indolence, and negligence,
Is declared to be tamasic.
verses.accessible: That happiness which deludes the self from beginning to end, springing from laziness, excessive sleep, and reckless negligence—that happiness is declared to be tamasic.

verses.translation:
There is no being, either on earth
Or yet in heaven among the gods,
Which can exist
Free from these three qualities born of material nature.
verses.accessible: There is no living being on earth, nor even among the heavenly gods, that is free from these three qualities born of material nature.

verses.translation:
The duties of the brahmins, the kshatriyas, the vaishyas,
And of the shudras, Arjuna,
Are distributed according to
The qualities which arise from their own nature.
verses.accessible: The duties of teachers and priests, warriors and rulers, merchants and farmers, and laborers and artisans are distributed according to the qualities arising from their own inherent nature, Arjuna.

verses.translation:
Tranquility, restraint, austerity, purity,
Forgiveness, and uprightness,
Knowledge, wisdom, and faith in God
Are the duties of the brahmins, born of their innate nature.
verses.accessible: Serenity, self-control, self-discipline, inner and outer purity, patience, honesty, spiritual knowledge, practical wisdom, and firm faith in the Divine—these are the duties of teachers and priests, born of their inherent nature.
notes: • Thus states of mind, in Gltii psychology, also constitute action.

verses.translation:
Heroism, majesty, firmness, skill,
Not fleeing in battle,
Generosity, and lordly spirit
Are the duties of the kshatriyas, born of their innate nature.
verses.accessible: Courage, majesty, resolve, skill, refusing to retreat from battle, generosity, and natural leadership—these are the duties of warriors and rulers, born of their inherent nature.

verses.translation:
Plowing, cow-herding, and trade
Are the duties of the vaishyas, born of their innate nature.
Service is the duty of the shudras,
Born of their innate nature.
verses.accessible: Agriculture, cattle raising, and trade are the natural duties of merchants; while work based on service and craft is the natural duty of laborers, born of their inherent nature.

verses.translation:
Devoted to his own duty,
A man attains perfection.
Hear then how one who is devoted to his own duty
Finds perfection:
verses.accessible: By dedicating themselves wholeheartedly to their own natural duty, any person can reach spiritual perfection. Listen now to how one who is devoted to their own work achieves this perfection:

verses.translation:
By worshiping with his own proper duty
Him from whom all beings have their origin,
Him by whom all this universe is pervaded,
Man finds perfection.
verses.accessible: By honoring the Supreme Being—the source from whom all creatures originate and who pervades the entire universe—through the dedicated offering of one's own work, a human being attains perfection.

verses.translation:
Better one’s own duty, though imperfect,
Than the duty of another well performed;
Performing the duty prescribed by one’s own nature,
One does not incur evil.
verses.accessible: It is far better to perform one's own natural duty, even with flaws, than to perform another person's duty perfectly. By doing the work that aligns with your own nature, you incur no fault.
notes: • Caste duty is meant here.

verses.translation:
One should not abandon the duty to which one is born
Even though it be deficient, Arjuna.
Indeed, all undertakings are enveloped by evil
As fire is by smoke.
verses.accessible: One should never abandon the work born of one's natural disposition, Arjuna, even if it has shortcomings. Truly, all endeavors are clouded by some imperfection, just as fire is surrounded by smoke.

verses.translation:
With his intellect unattached at all times,
With conquered self, free from desire,
By renunciation, one attains
The supreme state of freedom from action.
verses.accessible: With an intellect unattached to worldly outcomes, self-mastered, and free from selfish longing, a person attains through selfless renunciation the supreme state of actionless peace.

verses.translation:
Learn from Me briefly, Arjuna,
How one who has attained perfection
Also attains Brahman,
Which is the highest state of knowledge.
verses.accessible: Learn briefly from Me, Arjuna, how someone who has reached this perfection also attains Brahman, the supreme culmination of spiritual wisdom:

verses.translation:
Endowed with a pure intellect,
Controlling the self with firmness,
Abandoning sound and the other objects of sense,
Casting off attraction and hatred,
verses.accessible: Endowed with a purified intellect, disciplining the self with firm resolve, turning away from distracting sensory pleasures, and casting aside attraction and hatred;
notes: • There are five objects, or .. provinces" (vilayiis), of the senses (indriyii1,li); I. sabda or sruti vilaya (sound) for the ear. 2. sparsa v#aya (tangibility) for the touch. 3. rupa vilaya (form) for the eye. 4. rasa v#aya (flavor) for the tongue. 5. gandha vilaya (smell) for the nose. And these are often referred to as the gU1,las respectively of; (I) ether; (2) air; (3) fire; (4) water; (5) earth.

verses.translation:
Dwelling in solitude, eating lightly,
Controlling speech, body, and mind,
Constantly devoted to yoga meditation,
Taking refuge in dispassion,
verses.accessible: dwelling in a quiet place, eating moderately, mastering speech, body, and mind, constantly absorbed in meditation, and taking shelter in deep detachment;

verses.translation:
Relinquishing egotism, force, arrogance,
Desire, anger, and possession of property;
Unselfish, tranquil,
He is fit for oneness with Brahman.
verses.accessible: relinquishing egotism, violence, arrogance, craving, anger, and possessiveness; peaceful and free from the sense of 'me and mine'—such a person is truly ready to become one with Brahman.

verses.translation:
Absorbed in Brahman, he whose self is serene
Does not mourn, nor does he desire;
Impartial among all beings,
He attains supreme devotion to Me.
verses.accessible: United with Brahman, their spirit serene, they neither grieve over loss nor crave what is missing. Viewing all living beings with equal reverence, they attain supreme devotion to Me.
notes: • Impartial, lit. "the same," i.e. regarding his own iitman (self) as identical with the iitmans of all beings.

verses.translation:
By devotion to Me he comes to know
Who I am in truth;
Then having known Me in truth,
He enters Me immediately.
verses.accessible: Through devotion, they come to know Me as I truly am—My full essence and reality. And having known Me in truth, they enter directly into union with Me.

verses.translation:
Performing all actions,
He whose reliance is always on Me,
Attains, by My grace,
The eternal, imperishable abode.
verses.accessible: Even while constantly carrying out all kinds of actions, one who relies wholly on Me attains, by My grace, the eternal and imperishable realm.

verses.translation:
Mentally renouncing
All actions in Me, devoted to Me as the Supreme,
Taking refuge in the yoga of discrimination,
Constantly think of Me.
verses.accessible: Mentally offer all your actions to Me, dedicate yourself to Me as your supreme goal, rely on the yoga of clear discernment, and always keep your heart and mind centered on Me.

verses.translation:
Fixing your mind on Me, you shall pass over
All difficulties, through My grace;
But if, through egoism, you will not listen,
Then you shall perish.
verses.accessible: If you keep your mind focused on Me, you will overcome all difficulties and obstacles by My grace. But if you refuse to listen because of your ego, you will ruin yourself.

verses.translation:
If, filled with egoism,
You think, “I shall not fight,”
Your resolve will be in vain;
Your own material nature will compel you.
verses.accessible: If, driven by ego, you declare, 'I will not fight,' your resolution will be in vain, for your own warrior nature will compel you to act.

verses.translation:
What you wish not to do, through delusion,
You shall do that
Against your will, Arjuna,
Bound by your own karma, born of your own material nature.
verses.accessible: Bound by the duties and habits born of your own nature, Arjuna, what you now refuse to do out of confusion, you will end up doing helplessly against your will.
notes: • I have left the word "karma" untranslated here, as it refers in this case, not to action in general, but to fate resulting from action in a previous in~arnation. Arjuna is foredoomed to certain actions by the laws governing his" material nature" as a k~atriya, or member of the warrior caste.

verses.translation:
The Lord abides in the hearts
Of all beings, Arjuna,
Causing all beings to revolve,
By the power of illusion, as if fixed on a machine.
verses.accessible: The Supreme Lord lives in the hearts of all living beings, Arjuna, guiding the movement of every creature through His cosmic power, as though they were seated on a revolving machine.
notes: • Like puppets fixed to a merry-go-round, an interpretation made by Samkara (circa 800 A.D.).

verses.translation:
Fly unto Him alone for refuge
With your whole being, Arjuna.
From His grace, you shall attain
Supreme peace and the eternal abode.
verses.accessible: Surrender to Him alone with all your heart, Arjuna. By His divine grace, you will attain supreme peace and the eternal dwelling place.

verses.translation:
Thus the knowledge that is more secret
Than all that is secret has been expounded to you by Me.
Having reflected on this fully,
Do as you please.
verses.accessible: Thus, I have revealed to you wisdom that is more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it deeply and thoroughly, and then do as you choose.

verses.translation:
Hear again My supreme word,
Most secret of all.
You are surely loved by Me;
Therefore, I shall speak for your good.
verses.accessible: Hear once more My supreme word, the most confidential teaching of all. Because you are so deeply loved by Me, I speak this for your highest well-being.

verses.translation:
Fix your mind on Me, worshiping Me,
Sacrificing to Me, bowing down to Me;
In this way you shall come truly to Me,
I promise, for you are dear to Me.
verses.accessible: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, and bow down before Me. In this way, you will surely come to Me. I promise you this, for you are truly dear to Me.

verses.translation:
Abandoning all duties,
Take refuge in Me alone.
I shall liberate you
From all evils; do not grieve.
verses.accessible: Abandon all varieties of dharma and take refuge in Me alone. I will deliver you from all sins; do not grieve.

verses.translation:
This shall not be spoken of by you to one who is without austerity,
Nor to one who is without devotion,
Nor to one who does not render service,
Nor to one who does not desire to listen,
Nor to one who speaks evil of Me.
verses.accessible: You should never share this sacred teaching with someone who lacks self-discipline, who has no devotion, who is unwilling to serve, who refuses to listen, or who harbors resentment against Me.

verses.translation:
He who shall teach this supreme
Secret to My worshipers,
Having performed the highest devotion to Me,
Shall come to Me, without doubt.
verses.accessible: Whoever shares this supreme secret with My devotees, offering their highest devotion to Me, will undoubtedly come to Me.

verses.translation:
And no one among men shall
Do more pleasing service to Me than he,
And no other on earth
Shall be dearer to Me.
verses.accessible: No one among all human beings performs a service more pleasing to Me than this, nor will anyone on earth ever be dearer to Me.

verses.translation:
And he who shall study this
Sacred dialogue of ours,
By him I shall have been worshiped
With the wisdom sacrifice; such is My conviction.
verses.accessible: And whoever studies this sacred conversation between us worships Me through the sacrifice of knowledge; this is My firm conviction.

verses.translation:
Even the man who hears it
With faith and free from malice,
He also, liberated, shall attain
The happy worlds of those whose actions are pure.
verses.accessible: Even someone who simply listens to this teaching with deep faith and a heart free from cynicism will be liberated and will reach the joyous worlds of the virtuous.

verses.translation:
Has this been heard by you, Arjuna,
With a concentrated mind?
Have your ignorance and delusion
Been destroyed?
verses.accessible: Krishna said: 'Arjuna, have you listened to all this with single-minded focus? Has your delusion born of ignorance been completely destroyed?'

verses.translation:
Arjuna spoke:
My delusion is destroyed and I have gained wisdom
Through Your grace, Krishna.
My doubts are gone.
I shall do as You command.
verses.accessible: Arjuna said: 'My delusion is destroyed, and through Your grace, Krishna, my memory has returned. I stand firm, my doubts are gone, and I am ready to act according to Your word.'

verses.translation:
Sanjaya spoke:
Thus I have heard from Krishna
And the great-souled Arjuna,
This wondrous dialogue
Which causes the hair to stand on end.
verses.accessible: Sanjaya said: 'In this way, I heard this wondrous, awe-inspiring dialogue between Krishna and the noble-hearted Arjuna, a conversation so thrilling that it makes the hair stand on end.'

verses.translation:
By the grace of Vyasa I have heard
This supreme and most secret yoga
Which Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, has divulged
Directly, speaking Himself.
verses.accessible: By the grace of the sage Vyasa, I was able to hear this supreme and most secret yoga directly from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, as He spoke it Himself.
notes: • Vyasa, legendary sage, compiler of the Vedas; also, according to legend, the natural father of Par;lC;lu and Dhrtara~tra, thus the grandfather of Arjuna, as well as of the Pal)<;Iava princes along with the hundred sons of Dhrtara~tra. Vyasa is also said to have compiled the Mahabharata including the Gita, though he must have existed before most of the events recounted in these works.

verses.translation:
O King, remembering again and again
This marvelous and holy dialogue
Of Krishna and Arjuna,
I rejoice again and again.
verses.accessible: O King, as I recall again and again this marvelous and holy conversation between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice with overwhelming joy at every moment.

verses.translation:
And remembering again and again
That marvelous form of Krishna,
My amazement is great, O King,
And I rejoice again and again.
verses.accessible: And as I remember again and again that astonishing, cosmic form of Lord Krishna, my wonder is boundless, O King, and I rejoice again and again.

verses.translation:
Wherever there is Krishna, Lord of Yoga,
Wherever there is Arjuna, the archer,
There will surely be
Splendor, victory, wealth, and righteousness; this is my conviction.
verses.accessible: Wherever there is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and wherever there is Arjuna, the archer, there will certainly be prosperity, victory, flourishing abundance, and unwavering justice. This is my firm conviction.
